notes.2300: (tn): That is, about the Lord’s accomplishments on their behalf.
notes.2301: (sn): Psalm 65. The psalmist praises God because he forgives sin and blesses his people with an abundant harvest.

rashi.heb:
*ישמח צדיק.* 
דניאל:
rashi.eng: *The righteous will rejoice.* This is Daniel.

rashi.heb:
*ויתהללו כל ישרי לב.* 
יתפארו על יושר לבם וישתבחו בעצמם כי בטוחים הם שהקב"ה בעזרתם:
rashi.eng: *and all upright of heart will boast.* They will boast about the uprightness of their heart, and they will praise themselves because they are confident that the Holy One, blessed be He, will help them.

notes.2302: (tn, Heb): “for you, silence, praise.” Many prefer to emend the noun דֻּמִיָּה (dumiyyah, “silence”) to a participle דּוֹמִיָּה (domiyyah), from the root דָּמָה (damah, “be silent”), understood here in the sense of “wait.”

rashi.heb:
*לך דמיה תהלה.* 
השתיקה תהלה לך לפי שאין קץ לשבחך והמרבה בשבח אינו אלא גורע:
rashi.eng: *Silence is praise to You.* Silence is praise to You; because there is no end to Your praise, the more one praises, the more one detracts.

rashi.heb:
*אלהים בציון.* 
אלהים השוכן בציון, (מצאתי שימו כבוד תהלתו, לא יותר מדאי, אך דומיה תהלה וכמדומה הללוהו באימה בלשון הללויה שם בן שתי אותיות מתורגם דחילא עזי וזמרת יה (לקמן קי"ח) ויד על כס יה (שמות י״ז:ט״ז) ולשון וגילו ברעדה דומה לזה) ד"א:
rashi.eng: *O God in Zion.* God, Who dwells in Zion. [I found the following: make glorious His praise Not effusion, but silence is praise. It appears that דמיה means “praise God with awe,” with the expression “praise Ya-h.” The name consisting of two letters is translated (Exod. 15:2) as, the fear of God, for “My strength and my praise is God (י-ה).” Also (Exod. 17:16), “For a hand is on the throne of God (י-ה).” And the expression (above 2:11): “and rejoice with quaking” resembles this. Shem Ephraim comments: “It appears to me that Rashi should read as follows: Make glorious, etc. But silence to God is praise, and its interpretation is: Praise Him with awe, etc.” The intention is that the word דמיה is divided into two words. For it was difficult for him to understand why it should appear that one is to recite any praise of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore he says, “Make glorious His praise,” but not excessively, for that is equivalent to detracting. Therefore he says, “To You is silence (דום),” meaning that silence is fitting, but י-ה is praise, i.e., with the name consisting of two letters. His statement that the expression, “rejoice with quaking” resembles this, should read: “Worship the Lord with awe and rejoice with quaking.” His intention is that both verses mean that one may worship the Lord with awe; that is, one may worship the Holy One, blessed be He, with the name י-ה. Otherwise, worship with love is superior. It is also possible that the reading, “and it appears that, etc.” is a copyist’s error. It should read instead: “But be silent and praise Him with the name י-ה, in the expression Hallelujah.” But this needs study. Later I found (below 68:5) that Rashi writes something similar. There, for him to write that the expression “and rejoice with quaking” resembles this is more appropriate, because there it says: “and rejoice before Him.” Compare. Therefore, it appears to me that this entire statement was erroneously copied here.) The gloss belongs below 66:2.] Another explanation:

rashi.heb: *לך דומיה תהלה אלהים בציון.* את אשר דוממת והחרשת על מה שעשה אויביך בציון תהלה היה לך שהיכולת בידך להנקם ואתה מאריך אף:
rashi.eng: *To You is silence praise, O God, in Zion.* That You were silent and still concerning Your enemies’ deeds in Zion is praise to You, for You are able to take revenge, yet You are slow to anger.

notes.2305: (tn, Heb): “the records of sins are too strong for me.”

notes.2307: (tn): The Hebrew noun is an abstract plural. The word often refers metonymically to the happiness that God-given security and prosperity produce (see Pss 1:1; 2:12; 34:9; 41:1; 84:12; 89:15; 106:3; 112:1; 127:5; 128:1; 144:15).
notes.2308: (tn, Heb): “[whom] you bring near [so that] he might live [in] your courts.”

rashi.heb:
*דברי עונות גברו מני.* 
ואין אנו יכולים להספיק לסדר כולם לפניך לפי שהם רב אלא בכלל אחד אנו מתפללים לפניך שפשעינו אתה תכפרם:
rashi.eng: *Words of iniquities have overcome me.* and we cannot manage to arrange them all before You because they are many. However, we offer a general prayer before You that You atone for our transgressions.

notes.2310: (tn, Heb): “[with] awesome acts in deliverance you answer us, O God of our salvation.”
notes.2311: (tn, Heb): “a source of confidence [for] all the ends of the earth.” All the ends of the earth trust in you. This idealistic portrayal of universal worship is typical hymnic hyperbole, though it does anticipate eschatological reality.
notes.2312: (tc, Heb): “and [the] distant sea.” The plural adjective is problematic after the singular form “sea.” One could emend יָם (yam, “sea”) to יָמִים (yamim, “seas”), or emend the plural form רְחֹקִים (r�khoqim, “far”) to the singular רָחֹק (rakhoq). In this case the final mem (ם) could be treated as dittographic; note the mem on the beginning of the first word in v. 6.

rashi.heb:
*אשרי.* 
מי אשר תבחר ותקרב אשר ישכן בחצריך:
rashi.eng: *Praiseworthy is.* he whom You choose and draw near, who will dwell in Your courts.

rashi.heb:
*נשבעה בטוב.* 
שבביתך ומקדושת היכלך ששכינתך שורה שם:
rashi.eng: *let us be sated with the goodness.* that is in Your house and of the sanctity of Your Temple, in which Your Shechinah dwells.

notes.2313: (tn, Heb): “[the] one who establishes [the] mountains by his power.”
notes.2314: (tn, Heb): “one [who] is girded with strength”; or “one [who] girds himself with strength.”

rashi.heb:
*נוראות בצדק תעננו.* 
בצדקתך תעננו לעשות נוראות בגוים:
rashi.eng: *With awesome deeds, through [Your] charity You shall answer us.* Through Your charity, You shall answer us by performing awesome deeds upon the heathens.

rashi.heb:
*מבטח.* 
אתה ומנוס לכל יושבי קצות ארץ מקצה הארץ ועד קצהו:
rashi.eng: *the trust.* You are [the trust] and the refuge of all the dwellers of the ends of the earth, from one end of the earth to the other.

rashi.heb:
*וים רחוקים.* 
אפילו לרחוקים שבים אתה מבטח שבכל מקום ממשלתך:
rashi.eng: *distant… and the sea.* Even to the distant ones in the sea You are the trust, for Your rule is everywhere.

notes.2316: (sn): The raging seas…the commotion made by the nations. The raging seas symbolize the turbulent nations of the earth (see Ps 46:2-3, 6; Isa 17:12).

rashi.heb:
*מכין הרים בכחו.* 
שמצמיח ההרים שהם קשים בכחו ומזמן ומכין בהן מזונות ומכין מטר כדכתיב (לקמן קמז) המכין לארץ מטר המצמיח הרים:
rashi.eng: *Who sets mountains with His strength.* With His strength, He makes the mountains which are hard sprout, and He prepares and readies food through them and prepares rain, as it is written (below 147:8): “Who prepares rain for the earth, Who makes the mountains grow grass.”

rashi.heb:
*נאזר בגבורה.* 
לפי שבא להזכיר גבורת גשמים אמר נאזר בגבורה:
rashi.eng: *Who is girded with might.* Because he wishes to mention the mighty deeds of the rains, he says, “Who is girded with might.”

notes.2317: (tn, Heb): “and the inhabitants of the ends fear because of your signs.” God’s “signs” are the “awesome acts” (see v. 5) he performs in the earth.
notes.2318: (tn, Heb): “the goings out of the morning and the evening you cause to shout for joy.” The phrase “goings out of the morning and evening” refers to the sunrise and sunset, that is, the east and the west.

rashi.heb:
*משביח.* 
משפיל, וכן וחכם באחור ישבחנה (משלי כ"ט) בשוא גליו אתה תשבחם (לקמן פ"ט):
rashi.eng: *Who humbles.* Heb. משביח, He humbles. Similarly (Prov. 29:11): “but afterwards, a wise man will quiet it (ישבחנה); (below 89:10),” When it raises its waves, You humble them (תשבחם)."

notes.2319: (tn): The verb form is a Polel from שׁוּק (shuq, “be abundant”), a verb which appears only here and in Joel 2:24 and 3:13, where it is used in the Hiphil stem and means “overflow.”
notes.2321: (tn, Heb): “[with] a channel of God full of water.” The divine name is probably used here in a superlative sense to depict a very deep stream (“a stream fit for God,” as it were).
notes.2322: (tn): The pronoun apparently refers to the people of the earth, mentioned in v. 8.
notes.2323: (tn, Heb): “for thus [referring to the provision of rain described in the first half of the verse] you prepare it.” The third feminine singular pronominal suffix attached to the verb “prepare” refers back to the “earth,” which is a feminine noun with regard to grammatical form.

rashi.heb:
*מוצאי בקר וערב תרנין.* 
לך את הבריות יושבי הקצוות בבקר אומרים ברוך יוצר המאורות ובערב ברוך המעריב ערבים:
rashi.eng: *with the emergence of the morning and evening, You cause [them] to sing praises.* [You cause] the creatures who dwell at the extremes to sing praises. In the morning, they say, “Blessed is He Who formed the luminaries,” and in the evening “Blessed is He Who brings about evening.”

notes.2324: (tn, Heb): “saturating” [the form is an infinitive absolute].
notes.2327: (tn, Heb): “soften it,” that is, the earth.
notes.2328: (tn, Heb): “its vegetation you bless.” Divine “blessing” often involves endowing an object with special power or capacity.

rashi.heb:
*פקדת הארץ.* 
כשאתה חפץ להטיב אתה פוקד את הארץ ומשקה אותה:
rashi.eng: *You remember the earth.* When You wish to do good, You remember the earth and water it.

rashi.heb:
*רבת תעשרנה.* 
הרבה אתה מעשרה מפלג שלך שהוא מלא מים ותכין בו דגנם של יושבי קצוות כי בכן אתה מכין אותם:
rashi.eng: *You enrich it greatly.* You enrich it greatly from Your stream, which is full of water, and You prepare therewith the corn of the dwellers of “the ends,” for therewith You prepare it.

notes.2329: (tn, Heb): “your good,” which refers here to agricultural blessings.
notes.2330: (tn, Heb): “and your paths drip with abundance.”

rashi.heb:
*תלמיה.* 
הן שורות המחרישה:
rashi.eng: *its furrows.* Heb. תלמיה. They are the rows of the plowshare.

rashi.heb:
*רוה.* 
כמו לרוה:
rashi.eng: *To sate.* Heb. רוה, like לרוה.

rashi.heb:
*נחת גדודיה.* 
כמו לנחת גדודיה להניח לגדודיה לעשות נחת לבריות אתה תמוגגנה ברביבים של מטר:
rashi.eng: *to afford pleasure to its troops.* Heb. נחתגדודה, like לְנַחֵתגְדוּדֶהָ, to give rest to its troops. To afford pleasure to its creatures, You dissolve it with drops of rain.

rashi.heb:
*תמוגגנה.* 
לשון המסה:
rashi.eng: *You dissolve it.* Heb. תמגגנה, an expression of melting.

notes.2332: (tn): That is, with rich vegetation that brings joy to those who see it.

rashi.heb:
*עטרת שנת טובתך.* 
ע"י הגשמים אתה מעטר בכל טוב את השנה שאתה חפץ להטיב:
rashi.eng: *You crowned a year of Your goodness.* Through the rains, You crown with total goodness the year that You wish to benefit.

rashi.heb:
*ומעגליך.* 
הם השמים שהם אבק רגליך:
rashi.eng: *and Your paths.* They are the heavens, which are the dust of Your feet.

notes.2333: (sn): Psalm 66. The psalmist praises God because he has delivered his people from a crisis.

rashi.heb:
*ירעפו.* 
השמים בנאות המדבר:
rashi.eng: *They drip.* The heavens [drip] upon the dwellings of the desert.

rashi.heb:
*לבשו כרים הצאן.* 
יתלבשון השרון והערבה מן הצאן הבאים לרעות הדשא אשר הצמיח המטר:
rashi.eng: *Meadows are clothed with flocks.* The Sharon and the Arabah are clothed with the flocks that come to graze on the grass that the rain causes to grow.

rashi.heb:
*ועמקים יעטפו בר.* 
ע"י המטר יהיו מעוטפים העמקים בתבואה ואז יתרועעו הבריות תרועת שמחה וישירו מרוב הברכה:
rashi.eng: *and valleys are enwrapped with corn.* Through the rain, the valleys will be enwrapped with grain. Then the creatures will shout with shouts of joy and sing because of the abundant blessing.

notes.2334: (tn, Heb): “his name,” which here stands metonymically for God’s reputation.

rashi.heb:
*זמרו כבוד שמו.* 
זמרו בכבוד שמו א"נ ספרו כבוד שמו בזמר ושיר:
rashi.eng: *Sing the glory of His name.* Sing in honor of His name. Or: Recite the glory of His name with music and song.

notes.2336: (tn): See Deut 33:29; Ps 81:15 for other uses of the verb כָּחַשׁ (kakhash) in the sense “cower in fear.” In Ps 18:44 the verb seems to carry the nuance “be weak, powerless” (see also Ps 109:24).

rashi.heb:
*מה נורא.* 
כל אחד ממעשיך:
rashi.eng: *How awesome.* is each one of Your deeds!

rashi.heb:
*ברוב עוזך.* 
כשאתה מראה לעולם עוזך על ידי דבר או חרב או רעב או ברקים:
rashi.eng: *Through the greatness of Your might.* When You show the world Your might, through pestilence, sword, famine, or lightning.

rashi.heb:
*אויביך.* 
הרשעים מרוב פחד מודים על כחש ועבירות שבידם (ע"כ התוס'):
rashi.eng: *Your enemies.* The wicked, confess their lies and sins because of their great fear.

notes.2337: (tn): Or “bows down to.” The prefixed verbal forms in v. 4 are taken (1) as imperfects expressing what is typical. Another option (2) is to interpret them as anticipatory (“all the earth will worship you”) or (3) take them as jussives, expressing a prayer or wish (“may all the earth worship you”).

notes.2340: (tn, Heb): “awesome [is] an act toward the sons of man.” It is unclear how the prepositional phrase relates to what precedes. If collocated with “act,” it may mean “on behalf of” or “toward.” If taken with “awesome” (see 1 Chr 16:25; Pss 89:7; 96:4; Zeph 2:11), one might translate “his awesome acts are beyond human comprehension” or “his awesome acts are superior to anything men can do.”

rashi.heb:
*נורא עלילה.* 
יראוי על בני אדם פן ימצא להם פשע כי כל מעשיהם גלוים לך:
rashi.eng: *awesome in His deeds.* Feared by mankind, lest He find a transgression in them, for all their deeds are revealed to You.

notes.2341: (sn): He turned the sea into dry land. The psalmist alludes to Israel’s crossing the Red Sea (Exod 14:21).
notes.2342: (tn): Because of the reference to “the river,” some understand this as an allusion to Israel’s crossing the Jordan River. However, the Hebrew term נָהָר (nahad) does not always refer to a “river” in the technical sense; it can be used of sea currents (see Jonah 2:4). So this line may also refer to the Red Sea crossing (cf. NEB).
notes.2343: (tn): The adverb שָׁם (sham, “there”) is used here, as often in poetic texts, to point “to a spot in which a scene is localized vividly in the imagination” (BDB 1027 s.v.).

rashi.heb:
*הפך ים ליבשה.* 
ים סוף:
rashi.eng: *He turned the sea into dry land.* The Sea of Reeds.

rashi.heb:
*שם נשמחה בו.* 
מצאתי שם היה דבר שהיה נשמח בו כלומר שראה הים את הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *there it rejoiced with it.* I found: There was a thing with which the sea rejoiced, i.e., that the sea saw the Holy One, blessed be He.

notes.2345: (tn, Heb): “his eyes watch.” “Eyes” are an anthropomorphism, attributed to God here to emphasize his awareness of all that happens on earth.
notes.2346: (tn): The verb form is jussive (note the negative particle אַל, ’al). The Kethib (consonantal text) has a Hiphil form of the verb, apparently to be understood in an exhibitive sense (“demonstrate stubborn rebellion”; see BDB 927 s.v. רוּם Hiph), while the Qere (marginal reading) has a Qal form, to be understood in an intransitive sense. The preposition -לְ (lamed) with pronominal suffix should be understood in a reflexive sense (“for themselves”) and indicates that the action is performed with the interest of the subject in mind.

rashi.heb:
*אל ירומו.* 
אל תהי ידם רמה:
rashi.eng: *will not exalt themselves.* Their hand will not be high.

notes.2347: (tn, Heb): “bless,” in the sense of declaring “God to be the source of…special power” (see HALOT 160 s.v. II ברך pi).
notes.2348: (tn, Heb): “cause the voice of his praise to be heard.”

rashi.heb:
*ברכו עמים אלהינו.* 
על נפלאותיו שהוא שם נפשנו בחיים בגלות ואינכם יכולים להשמיד אותנו:
rashi.eng: *O peoples, bless our God.* for His wonders, that He kept our soul alive in exile, and you cannot annihilate us.

notes.2349: (tn, Heb): “the one who places our soul in life.”

rashi.heb:
*כי בחנתנו.* 
בצרה בגולה:
rashi.eng: *You tested us.* with distress in the exile.

rashi.heb:
*צרפתנו.* 
להסיר הסיגים ממנו שנשוב בתשובה לפניך כמו שצורפים הכסף להסיר הסיגים ממנו:
rashi.eng: *You refined us.* to remove the dross from us when we repent before You, as they refine silver to remove its dross.

notes.2351: (tn, Heb): “you brought us into a net.” This rare word for “net” also occurs in Ezek 12:13; 13:21; 17:20.
notes.2352: (tn, Heb): “you placed suffering on our hips.” The noun מוּעָקָה (mu’aqah, “suffering”) occurs only here in the OT.

rashi.heb:
*הבאתנו במצודה.* 
במקום צר כמו במאסר:
rashi.eng: *You brought us into a trap.* A narrow place, like in a prison.

rashi.heb:
*מועקה.* 
לשון מסגר וכל המעיק והמציק כמוהו:
rashi.eng: *a chain.* Heb. מועקה, an expression of locking up, and every [expression of] מֵעִיק and מֵצִיק is like it.

notes.2353: (tc): The MT reads רְוָיָה (“saturation”) but this should be emended to רְוָחָה (r�vakhah, “wide open place”; i.e., “relief”), a reading supported by several ancient versions (LXX, Syriac, Jerome, Targum).

rashi.heb:
*הרכבת אנוש לראשינו.* 
מלכי כל אומה ואומה:
rashi.eng: *You caused man to ride at our head.* The kings of all the heathen nations.

notes.2354: (sn): Here the psalmist switches to the singular; he speaks as the representative of the nation.

rashi.heb:
*אבוא ביתך.* 
בבנותך בית המקדש נשלם נדרינו שנדרנו בגולה:
rashi.eng: *I shall come to Your house.* when You build the Temple, we shall pay our vows that we vowed in exile.

rashi.heb:
*מיחים.* 
שמנים לשון מוח:
rashi.eng: *fat.* Heb. מיחים, fat, an expression of מוֹחַ, marrow.

notes.2355: (tn, Heb): “all of the fearers of God.”

rashi.heb:
*כל יראי אלהים.* 
הם הגרי' שיתגיירו:
rashi.eng: *all you who fear God.* They are the proselytes who became converted.

notes.2356: (tn, Heb): “to him [with] my mouth I called.”
notes.2357: (tn, Heb): “and he was extolled under my tongue.” The form רוֹמַם (romam) appears to be a polal (passive) participle from רוּם (rum, “be exalted”), but many prefer to read רוֹמָם, “high praise [was under my tongue]” (cf. NEB). See BDB 928 s.v. רוֹמָם.

rashi.heb:
*אליו פי קראתי.* 
כשהיינו בגולה קראנוהו וספרנו רוממותיו בלשוננו:
rashi.eng: *My mouth called out to Him.* When we were in exile, we called out to Him, and we recited His exaltation with our tongue.

rashi.heb:
*ורומם.* 
כמו ונתרומם, מצאתי בפי קראתי אליו ורומם שם מלה רוממות שלו מוכן תחת לשוני להוציאו בפה כמו (איוב כ) יכחידנה תחת לשונו:
rashi.eng: *and He was exalted.* Heb. ורומם, like ונתרומם, and He was exalted. I found: With my mouth, I called out to Him. ורומם is a noun. His exaltation is ready under my tongue to be let out of my mouth, as (Job 20:12): “though he hide it under his tongue.”

notes.2358: (tn, Heb): “sin if I had seen in my heart.”

rashi.heb:
*און אם ראיתי וגו'.* 
לא פעל עמנו כחטאתינו עשה עמנו כלא רואה ולא שומע און שבלבבנו:
rashi.eng: *If I saw iniquity, etc..* He did not deal with us according to our sins, but He made Himself as though He neither saw nor heard the iniquity that was in our hearts.

rashi.heb:
*אכן.* 
באמת יש לדעת:
rashi.eng: *But.* indeed you should know.

notes.2360: (tn): Or “who.” In a blessing formula after בָּרוּךְ (barukh, “blessed be”) the form אֲשֶׁר (’asher), whether taken as a relative pronoun or causal particle, introduces the basis for the blessing/praise.
notes.2361: (tn, Heb): “did not turn aside my prayer and his loyal love with me.”
notes.2362: (sn): Psalm 67. The psalmist prays for God’s blessing upon his people and urges the nations to praise him for he is the just ruler of the world.

rashi.heb:
*אשר לא הסיר תפלתי.* 
מלפניו וחסדו לא הסיר מאתי:
rashi.eng: *Who did not remove my prayer.* from before Him, and He did not remove His kindness from me.

notes.2364: (tn): The prefixed verbal forms are understood as jussives expressing the psalmist’s prayer. Note the jussive form יָאֵר (ya’er) in the next line.
notes.2365: (tn, Heb): “may he cause his face to shine with us.”

notes.2366: (tn, Heb): “to know in the earth your way, among all nations your deliverance.” The infinitive with -לְ (lamed) expresses purpose/result. When God demonstrates his favor to his people, all nations will recognize his character as a God who delivers. The Hebrew term דֶּרֶךְ (derekh, “way”) refers here to God’s characteristic behavior, more specifically, to the way he typically saves his people.

rashi.heb:
*יאר פניו.* 
להראות פנים שוחקות לתת טל ומטר:
rashi.eng: *He will cause His countenance to shine.* To show a laughing countenance, to give dew and rain.

notes.2367: (tn, Heb): “let the nations, all of them, thank you.” The prefixed verbal forms in vv. 3-4a are understood as jussives in this call to praise.

rashi.heb:
*לדעת בארץ דרכך.* 
להודיע שמדתך להטיב לעמך ועל זה יודוך וישמחו וירננו לאמים:
rashi.eng: *That Your way should be known on earth.* To make known that Your trait is to benefit Your people, and because of this, kingdoms will rejoice and sing praises.

notes.2369: (tn, Heb): “for you judge nations fairly, and [as for the] peoples in the earth, you lead them.” The imperfects are translated with the present tense because the statement is understood as a generalization about God’s providential control of the world. Another option is to understand the statement as anticipating God’s future rule (“for you will rule…and govern”).

notes.2370: (tn, Heb): “let the nations, all of them, thank you.” The prefixed verbal forms in v. 5 are understood as jussives in this call to praise.

rashi.heb:
*כי תשפוט עמים מישור.* 
לזכות:
rashi.eng: *for You will judge peoples fairly.* Favorably.

rashi.heb:
*תנחם.* 
תנהגם בדרך המישור ועל זאת יודוך עמים כולם:
rashi.eng: *You will lead them.* You will lead them in a fair way; therefore, all peoples will thank You.

notes.2371: (tn): The prefixed verb forms in vv. 6b-7a are understood as jussives.
notes.2372: (tn, Heb): “will fear him.” After the jussive of the preceding line, the prefixed verbal form with prefixed vav (ו) conjunctive is understood as indicating purpose/result. (Note how v. 3 anticipates the universal impact of God showing his people blessing.) Another option is to take the verb as a jussive and translate, “Let all the ends of the earth fear him.”
notes.2373: (sn): Psalm 68. The psalmist depicts God as a mighty warrior and celebrates the fact that God exerts his power on behalf of his people.

rashi.heb:
*ארץ נתנה יבולה.* 
וגם אל הארץ שנתנה יבולה ועל אשר יברכנו השם (סא"א):
rashi.eng: *The earth gave forth its produce.* Also for the earth, which gave forth its produce, and because God will bless us.

rashi.heb:
*וייראו אותו כל אפסי ארץ.* 
שיאמרו ראו אלו שהיו יראי השם איך ברכם וגדלם:
rashi.eng: *and all the ends of the earth will fear Him.* for they will say, “See these people, who feared the Lord, how He blessed them and magnified them.”

notes.2374: (tn): Or “rises up.” The verb form is an imperfect, not a jussive. The psalmist is describing God’s appearance in battle in a dramatic fashion.
notes.2376: (sn): The wording of v. 1 echoes the prayer in Num 10:35: “Spring into action, Lord! Then your enemies will be scattered and your adversaries will run from you.”

notes.2377: (tn, Heb): “as smoke is scattered, you scatter [them].”

rashi.heb:
*יקום אלהים יפוצו אויביו.* 
עמלק וכיוצא בו:
rashi.eng: *May God rise; His enemies scatter.* Amalek and his ilk.

notes.2378: (tn): By placing the subject first the psalmist highlights the contrast between God’s ecstatic people and his defeated enemies (vv. 1-2).
notes.2379: (tn, Heb): “and they are happy with joy” (cf. NEB). Some translate the prefixed verbal forms of v. 3 as jussives, “Let the godly be happy, let them rejoice before God, and let them be happy with joy!” (Cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV; note the call to praise in v. 4.)

rashi.heb:
*כהנדוף.* 
כהתנדף כאשר יתנדף העשן כן תנדפם:
rashi.eng: *As smoke is driven away.* as it is driven away. As the smoke is driven away so will You drive [them] away.

rashi.heb:
*מפני אלהים.* 
מפני הארון בימי משה ובנוחה יאמר שובה ה' וגו' (במדבר י׳:ל״ו):
rashi.eng: *from before God.* From before the Ark in the days of Moses. (And it came to pass when the Ark traveled, that Moses said, “Arise, O Lord, and Your enemies will scatter.” Shem Ephraim) And when it rested, he would say, “Return, O Lord, etc.”

notes.2380: (tn): Traditionally the Hebrew term עֲרָבוֹת (’aravot) is taken as “steppe-lands” (often rendered “deserts”), but here the form is probably a homonym meaning “clouds.” Verse 33, which depicts God as the one who “rides on the sky” strongly favors this (see as well Deut 33:26), as does the reference in v. 9 to God as the source of rain. The term עֲרָבָה (’aravah, “cloud”) is cognate with Akkadian urpatu/erpetu and with Ugaritic ’rpt. The phrase rkb ’rpt (“one who rides on the clouds”) appears in Ugaritic mythological texts as an epithet of the storm god Baal. The nonphonemic interchange of the bilabial consonants b and p is attested elsewhere in roots common to Hebrew and Ugaritic, though the phenomenon is relatively rare.
notes.2381: (tc, Heb): “in the Lord his name.” If the MT is retained, the preposition -בְ (bet) is introducing the predicate (the so-called bet of identity), “the Lord is his name.” However, some prefer to emend the text to כִּי יָהּ שְׁמוֹ (ki yah sh�mo, “for Yah is his name”). This emendation, reflected in the present translation, assumes a confusion of bet (ב) and kaf (כ) and haplography of yod (י).

rashi.heb:
*וישישו בשמחה.* 
וזהו המשוש וכן יאמרו שירו לאלהים וגו':
rashi.eng: *and they will delight with joy.* And this is the joy, and so will they say, “Sing to God, etc.”

notes.2382: (sn): God is depicted here as a just ruler. In the ancient Near Eastern world a king was responsible for promoting justice, including caring for the weak and vulnerable, epitomized by the fatherless and widows.
notes.2383: (tn, Heb): “God [is] in his holy dwelling place.” He occupies his throne and carries out his royal responsibilities.

rashi.heb:
*סולו.* 
לשון שבח וכן לא תסלה בכתם (איוב כ״ח:ט״ז) המסולאים בפז (איכה ד'):
rashi.eng: *praise.* Heb. סולו, an expression of praise. Similarly (Job 28:16): “It cannot be praised (תסלה) with the jewelry of Ophir;” (Lam. 4:2), “worth their weight (המסלאים) in fine gold.”

rashi.heb:
*ביה שמו.* 
בשם י"ה שהוא ל' יראה כדמתרגמינן דחילא עזי וזמרת יה (לקמן קי"ח) וכן כי יד על כס יה (שמות י״ז:ט״ז) בתרגום וכן כי ביה ה' (ישעיה כ"ו) ארי בכן תתפרקון במימרא דחילא ה' ותקיף עלמא אומר המשורר שבחו לפניו וגורו מפניו ועלזו וזהו דוגמת האמור במקום אחר וגילו ברעדה (לעיל ב'):
rashi.eng: *by His name Yah.* By the name י-ה, which is an expression of fear, as we translate it דחילא, fear (below 118:14): “My might and my praise is the fear of the Lord (י-ה).” Likewise (Exod. 17:16): “For a hand is on the throne of the Lord (י-ה),” in the Targum: [And he said, “This is stated with an oath from below the fear of the Shechinah on the throne of His glory, etc.] Similarly (Isa. 26:4): ” for in Yah the Lord, “ is paraphrased by the Targum: for then You will be redeemed by the word of the fear of the Lord, the Strongest of the world.” The Psalmist says, “Praise Him, fear Him, and rejoice.” This resembles what is said elsewhere (above 2:11): “and rejoice with quaking.”

notes.2384: (tn, Heb): “God causes the solitary ones to dwell in a house.” The participle suggests this is what God typically does.
notes.2385: (tn, Heb): “he brings out prisoners into prosperity.” Another option is to translate, “he brings out prisoners with singing” (cf. NIV). The participle suggests this is what God typically does.
notes.2386: (tn): Or “in a parched [land].” God delivers the downtrodden and oppressed, but sinful rebels who oppose his reign are treated appropriately.

rashi.heb:
*אבי יתומים.* 
זהו השבח שתשבחו לפניו כל הענין עד סוף כל המזמור:
rashi.eng: *O Father of orphans.* And this is the praise that You shall praise before Him: the entire matter until the end of the psalm.

rashi.heb:
*אבי יתומים.* 
שנעשה אב לישראל שהם יתומי' כמו שנאמר (איכה ה׳:ג׳) יתומים היינו ואין אב:
rashi.eng: *Father of orphans.* Who became a father to Israel, who are orphans, as it is said (Lam. 5:3): “We were orphans without a father.”

rashi.heb:
*ודין אלמנות.* 
שעשה משפטה של ירושלים שנאמר בה היתה כאלמנה (שם א'):
rashi.eng: *and Judge of widows.* Who performed the judgment of Jerusalem, concerning which it says (Lam. 1:1): “was like a widow.”

notes.2387: (tn, Heb): “when you go out before your people.” The Hebrew idiom “go out before” is used here in a militaristic sense of leading troops into battle (see Judg 4:14; 9:39; 2 Sam 5:24).
notes.2388: (sn): When you march through the desert. Some interpreters think that v. 7 alludes to Israel’s exodus from Egypt and its subsequent travels in the desert. Another option is that v. 7, like v. 8, echoes Judg 5:4, which describes how the God of Sinai marched across the desert regions to do battle with Sisera and his Canaanite army.

rashi.heb:
*מושיב יחידים ביתה.* 
ישראל שהיו מפוזרין כנסם יחד איש איש מנדחו והושיבם בית שלם וכנסיה שלימה:
rashi.eng: *settles the solitary in a house.* Israel, who were spread out. He gathered together each one from the place where he was lost and settled them in a complete household and a complete nation.

rashi.heb:
*מוציא אסירים בכושרות.* 
הוציא את ישראל ממצרים בחדש שהוא כשר להולכי דרכים לא חמה ולא צנה:
rashi.eng: *He takes the prisoners out at the most opportune time.* He took Israel out of Egypt in the month that is best suited for travelers, neither hot nor cold.

rashi.heb:
*אך סוררים.* 
מצרים:
rashi.eng: *but the rebellious.* The Egyptians.

rashi.heb:
*שכנו צחיחה.* 
ונשארה ארצם ציה וצמאה, (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *dwell in an arid land.* Their land remained arid and thirsty. I found [this].

notes.2389: (tn, Heb): “this one of Sinai.” The phrase is a divine title, perhaps indicating that the Lord rules from Sinai.
notes.2390: (sn): The language of vv. 7-8 is reminiscent of Judg 5:4-5, which tells how the God of Sinai came in the storm and annihilated the Canaanite forces led by Sisera. The presence of allusion does not mean, however, that this is a purely historical reference. The psalmist is describing God’s typical appearance as a warrior in terms of his prior self-revelation as ancient events are reactualized in the psalmist’s experience. (For a similar literary technique, see Hab 3.)

rashi.heb:
*בצעדך.* 
כשצעדת בצעדך בצעד שלך:
rashi.eng: *when You marched.* When You stepped with your step.

rashi.heb:
*סלה.* 
שם הראיתני זה דרכך לעולם לכל צרה גאולה:
rashi.eng: *forever.* There You showed me that this is Your way forever: for every distress, redemption.

notes.2391: (tn): The verb נוּף (nuf, “cause rain to fall”) is a homonym of the more common נוּף (“brandish”).
notes.2392: (tn, Heb): “[on] your inheritance.” This refers to Israel as God’s specially chosen people (see Pss 28:9; 33:12; 74:2; 78:62, 71; 79:1; 94:5, 14; 106:40). Some take “your inheritance” with what follows, but the vav (ו) prefixed to the following word (note וְנִלְאָה, v�nil’ah) makes this syntactically unlikely.

rashi.heb:
*זה סיני.* 
גם הוא רעש מפני ה' אלהי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *this is Sinai.* That too quaked because of the Lord God of Israel.

notes.2395: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew text is unclear; it appears to read, “your animals, they live in it,” but this makes little, if any, sense in this context. Some suggest that חָיָּה (khayah) is a rare homonym here, meaning “community” (BDB 312 s.v.) or “dwelling place” (HALOT 310 s.v. III *הַיָּה). In this case one may take “your community/dwelling place” as appositional to the third feminine singular pronominal suffix at the end of v. 9, the antecedent of which is “your inheritance.” The phrase יָשְׁבוּ־בָהּ (yashvu-vah, “they live in it”) may then be understood as an asyndetic relative clause modifying “your community/dwelling place.” A literal translation of vv. 9b-10a would be, “when it [your inheritance] is tired, you sustain it, your community/dwelling place in [which] they live.”

rashi.heb:
*גשם נדבות תניף.* 
עוד זאת עשית לנו אם הוצרכנו לגשמים הניפות והטלת עלינו תמיד גשמי נדבה וברכה:
rashi.eng: *Generous rain You poured down.* This too You did for us: if we needed rain, You lifted them and poured upon us constantly rains of generosity and blessing.

rashi.heb:
*נחלתך ונלאה אתה כוננתה.* 
כשהיתה נחלת ארצך נלאה וצמאה למטר אתה כוננת אותה, (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *Your heritage, which was weary, You established.* When the heritage of Your land was weary and thirsty for rain, You established it [Your heritage]. I found:

rashi.heb:
*נחלתך ונלאה.* 
הקרויה נחלתך והיא נלאה כלו' פעמים שהיא כך:
rashi.eng: *Your heritage which was weary.* Which is called your heritage, and which is weary; i.e., sometimes it is so.

notes.2396: (tn, Heb): “gives a word.” Perhaps this refers to a divine royal decree or battle cry.
notes.2397: (tn, Heb): “the ones spreading the good news [are] a large army.” The participle translated “the ones spreading the good news” is a feminine plural form. Apparently the good news here is the announcement that enemy kings have been defeated (see v. 12).

rashi.heb:
*חיתך ישבו בה.* 
עדתך ישבו בה כמו ויאספו פלשתים את מחניהם לחיה (שמואל ב כ״ג:י״א) ד"א חיתך, כנסת ישראל קרויה בהמתו וחיתו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *Your congregation dwelt therein.* Heb. (חיתך). Your congregation has dwelt therein, as (II Sam. 23:11): “and the Philistines gathered together their camp (sic) into a troop (לחיה).” Another explanation: The congregation of Israel is known as the animal and the beast of the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*תכין בטובתך.* 
כשיצאו ממצרים הסיבותם במדבר ארבעים שנה לפי שעמדו כנעניים וגדעו את האילנות ובתוך כך שעכבו במדבר עמדו ותקנו הכל:
rashi.eng: *You prepare with your goodness.* When they left Egypt, You led them around in the desert for forty years because the Canaanites rose and cut down the trees. During the interim, when they tarried in the desert, they rose and rectified it all.

notes.2398: (tn): The verbal repetition draws attention to the statement.
notes.2399: (tn): The Hebrew form appears to be the construct of נוּה (nuh, “pasture”) but the phrase “pasture of the house” makes no sense here. The translation assumes that the form is an alternative or corruption of נצוה (“beautiful woman”). A reference to a woman would be appropriate in light of v. 11b.

rashi.heb:
*אד' יתן אומר המבשרות וגו'.* 
אומר מאמר עוד הוא ישאג בקול להשמיע צבאות הגוים הרבים ומהו האומר: מלכי צבאות הגוים ידדון ידדון יתנדו וישלכו מתוך א"י וכנסת ישראל שהיא נות בית תחלק את שללם כמו שנאמר והי' סחרה ואתננה קדש וגומר (ישעיהו כ״ג:י״ח)
rashi.eng: *The Lord will give out a word; they will announce it to a great multitude.* Heb. אמר, [like] מאמר, statement. He will yet roar with [His] voice to allow the hosts of the great nations to hear it. Now what is the word? The kings of the hosts of nations will wander, yea they will wander. They will wander and be cast out of the land of Israel, and the congregation of Israel, who is the dweller of the house, will divide their spoils, as it is said (Isa. 23:18): “And her commerce and her hire shall be holy, etc.”

notes.2401: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew word translated “sheepfolds” is uncertain. There may be an echo of Judg 5:16 here.
notes.2402: (tn, Heb): “and her pinions with the yellow of gold.” The point of the imagery of v. 13 is not certain, though the reference to silver and gold appears to be positive. Both would be part of the loot carried away from battle (see v. 12b).

notes.2403: (tn): The divine name used here is שַׁדַּי (“Shaddai”). Shaddai/El Shaddai is the sovereign king/judge of the world who grants life, blesses and kills, and judges. In Genesis he blesses the patriarchs with fertility and promises numerous descendants. Outside Genesis he both blesses (protects) and takes away life and/or happiness.
notes.2404: (tn): The Hebrew text adds “in it.” The third feminine singular pronominal suffix may refer back to God’s community/dwelling place (v. 10).
notes.2405: (tn): The verb form appears to be a Hiphil jussive from שָׁלַג (shalag), which is usually understood as a denominative verb from שֶׁלֶג (sheleg, “snow”) with an indefinite subject. The form could be taken as a preterite, in which case one might translate, “when the sovereign judge scattered kings, it snowed on Zalmon” (cf. NIV, NRSV). The point of the image is unclear. Perhaps “snow” suggests fertility and blessing (see v. 9 and Isa 55:10), or the image of a snow-capped mountain suggests grandeur. Zalmon was apparently a mountain in the region, perhaps the one mentioned in Judg 9:46 as being in the vicinity of Shechem.

rashi.heb:
*אם תשכבון בין שפתים וגו'.* 
כל זה האומר יאמר להם אם אתם שכבתם בין תחומיכ' והתענגתם בתענוגים זאת יונתי כנסייתי כנפיה נחפה בכסף ומהו הכסף והחרוץ:
rashi.eng: *If you lie between the borders, etc..* All this is the word. He says to them, “If you had lain between your borders and had enjoyed pleasures, this My dove, My congregation, whose feathers are covered with silver.” Now what is the silver, and what is the gold?

rashi.heb: *בפרש שדי וגו'.* כשפירש הקב"ה לפניהם תורתו אשר המלכים נשלגים ומתלבנים בה בארץ צלמות וחשך אז נחפו כנפיה (כנפי יונה) בכספה וחמדתה של תורה ומצות:
rashi.eng: *(15) When the Almighty spreads out, etc..* When the Holy One, blessed be He, explained His Torah, with which the kings are “snowed and whitened” in a land of the Shadow of Death and darkness then its feathers (dove’s feathers) were covered with the desire and yearning for the Torah and [its] Commandments.

rashi.heb: *כנפי יונה.* פלומ"א בלעז:
rashi.eng: *the feathers of a dove.* Plumes in French.

rashi.heb:
*ואברותיה.* 
כנפיה שעופפת בהן:
rashi.eng: *and its pinions.* Its wings, with which it flies.

rashi.heb:
*בירקרק חרוץ.* 
פתר דונש בן לברט החרוץ הוא זהב ולכך נתנו המשורר אצל הכסף וירקרק החרוץ הוא הזהב אשר יובא מארץ החוילה ומארץ כוש זהב טוב מאד מאד לא הוא ירוק ולא הוא אדום ולכך קראו ירקרק כמו (ויקרא י״ג:מ״ב) לבן אדמדם שאינו לא לבן ולא אדום לכך נכפל ירקרק אדמדם:
rashi.eng: *with brilliant gold.* Heb. בירקרק חרוץ. Dunash the son of Labrat interpreted חרוּץ as gold. Therefore, the Psalmist juxtaposed it to silver, and ירקרק חרוץ is the gold brought from the land of Havilah and from the land of Cush; very good gold, neither yellow nor red. Therefore, it is called ירקרק, as (Lev. 13:42): “reddish white (לבן אדמדם),” which is neither white nor red. Therefore, it is doubled: אדמדם, ירקרק.

notes.2406: (sn): The mountain of Bashan probably refers to Mount Hermon.
notes.2407: (tn, Heb): “a mountain of God.” The divine name is probably used here in a superlative sense to depict a very high mountain (“a mountain fit for God,” as it were). Cf. NIV “are majestic mountains”; NRSV “O mighty mountain.”
notes.2408: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term, which appears only here in the OT, is uncertain. HALOT 174 s.v. גַּבְנוֹן suggests “many-peaked,” while BDB 148 s.v. גַּבְנִן suggests “rounded summit.”

rashi.heb:
*בפרש.* 
לשון ופרשו את השמלה (דברים כ"ב) בוררין את הדבר כשמלה חדשה:
rashi.eng: *kings.* These are the Torah scholars, as it is said (Prov. 8:15): “Kings reign with me.”

rashi.heb:
*מלכי'.* 
אלו ת"ח כמו שנאמר (משלי ח׳:ט״ו) בי מלכים ימלוכו:
rashi.eng: *When… spreads out.* Heb. בפרש, an expression of (Deut. 22:17): “and they will spread out (ופרשו) the garment”; they clarify the matter as a new garment.

notes.2409: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew verb רָצַד (ratsad), translated here “look with envy,” is uncertain; it occurs only here in the OT. See BDB 952-53. A cognate verb occurs in later Aramaic with the meaning “to lie in wait; to watch” (Jastrow 1492 s.v. רְצַד).
notes.2410: (tn): Perhaps the apparent plural form should be read as a singular with enclitic mem (ם; later misinterpreted as a plural ending). The preceding verse has the singular form.
notes.2411: (tn, Heb): “[at] the mountain God desires for his dwelling place.” The reference is to Mount Zion/Jerusalem.
notes.2412: (tn): The Hebrew particle אַף (’af) has an emphasizing function here.
notes.2413: (tn): The word “there” is supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*הר אלהים הר בשן.* 
והיכן פירשה בהר סיני שהוא הר אלהים סמוך לבשן בעבר הירדן:
rashi.eng: *The mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan.* And where did He spread it out? On Mt. Sinai, which is the mountain of God and is near Bashan on the eastern side of the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*הר גבנונים.* 
הר המיוחד שבהרים:
rashi.eng: *the mountain of peaks.* The special mountain among the mountains.

rashi.heb:
*גבנונים.* 
לשון הרים על שם גובהם כמו (יחזקאל ט״ז:כ״ד) ותבני לך גב כל דבר גבוה קרוי גב:
rashi.eng: *peaks.* Heb. גבננים, an expression of mountains, because of their height, as (Ezek. 16:24): “and you built for yourself a platform (גב).” Any high thing is called גַב.

notes.2414: (tn, Heb): “thousands of [?].” The meaning of the word שִׁנְאָן (shin’an), which occurs only here in the OT, is uncertain. Perhaps the form should be emended to שַׁאֲנָן (sha’anan, “at ease”) and be translated here “held in reserve.”
notes.2415: (tc): The MT reads, “the Lord [is] among them, Sinai, in holiness,” which is syntactically difficult. The present translation assumes an emendation to אֲדֹנָי בָּא מִסִּינַי (’adonay ba’ missinay; see BHS note b-b and Deut 33:2).

rashi.heb:
*למה תרצדון הרים גבנונים.* 
כל זה מוסב על ה' יתן אומר עוד יאמר להם למה תרצדון הרים גבנונים למה תארובון אתם ההרים גבנונים הגבוהים להשחית את ההר אשר חמד אלהים לשבתו לשרות עליו שכינה הוא הר הבית אף הוא לנצח ישכון שם קדושתו קדושת עולם משנבחר לשבתו לא שרתה שכינה במקום אחר, ראיתי ביסודו של רבי משה הדרשן רצד הוא מארב בל' ערבי, אבל מנחם פירש תרצדון כמו תרקדון אף אותו לשון נופל על השיטה הזאת:
rashi.eng: *Why do you lurk, you lofty mountains.* All this refers back to “The Lord will give out a word.” He says further to them, “Why do you lurk (תרצדון), you lofty mountains?” Why do you lurk, you lofty mountains, to destroy the mountain that God desired for His dwelling, to cause His Shechinah to rest upon it? That is the Temple Mount. Even He will dwell there forever. Its sanctity is a perpetual sanctity. After it was chosen for His dwelling, the Shechinah did not rest elsewhere. I saw in the works of Rabbi Moshe Hadarshan that רצד is “ambush” in Arabic. But Menachem (p. 166) explained תרצדוּן like תרקדוּן, you prance. That expression, too, fits the context.

notes.2416: (tn, Heb): “to the elevated place”; or “on high.” This probably refers to the Lord’s throne on Mount Zion.
notes.2420: (tn, Heb): “so that the Lord God might live [there].” Many take the infinitive construct with -לְ (lamed) as indicating purpose here, but it is unclear how the offering of tribute enables the Lord to live in Zion. This may be an occurrence of the relatively rare emphatic lamed (see HALOT 510-11 s.v. II לְ, though this text is not listed as an example there). If so, the statement corresponds nicely to the final line of v. 16, which also affirms emphatically that the Lord lives in Zion.

rashi.heb:
*רכב אלהים וגו'.* 
עוד זה מוסב על ה' יתן אומר להזכיר חבת עמו אף כשנגלה רכב אלהים רבותים של אלפים שנאנים שנונים מלאכים חדים וה' היה ביניהם בסיני בקודש אף שם:
rashi.eng: *God’s chariot, etc..* This too refers back to the “The Lord will give forth a word,” to mention the love of His people. Even when God’s chariot of “twice ten thousand times thousands of” brilliant “sharpened” angels appeared, and the Lord was among them at Sinai with His holiness, there too, you, the leader of His people, Moses the son of Amram ascended on high and took captives.

notes.2422: (tn): It is possible to take this phrase with what precedes (“The Lord deserves praise day after day”) rather than with what follows.

rashi.heb:
*עלית.* 
אתה נגיד עמו משה בן עמרם למרום, שבית שבי את התורה, ולקחת מתנות מן העליונים ולתתם לבני אדם ואף סוררים לשכון יה אלהים 
אף עוד גרמת ששכן הקב"ה במשכן בתוך עם שהיו סוררים וממרים ומקציפים אותו:
rashi.eng: *and also rebellious ones for Yah God to dwell.* Also you brought about that the Holy One, blessed be He, rested in the Tabernacle of the Torah, and you took gifts from the celestial beings to give them to the sons of men, also among a people who were rebellious and were rebelling against Him and provoking Him.

notes.2423: (tn, Heb): “and to the Lord, the Lord, to death, goings out.”

rashi.heb:
*ברוך אד' וגו'.* 
זה מן השיר האמור למעלה שירו לאלהים:
rashi.eng: *Blessed is the Lord, etc..* This is part of the song mentioned above: “Sing to God.”

rashi.heb:
*יעמס לנו.* 
יתן לנו ישועה רבה מכל עומס ככל אשר נוכל שאת, (מצאתי יום יום יעמס לנו כל הימים כן נוהג בנו לכל צרה ישועה)
rashi.eng: *lavishes upon us.* He will give us a great salvation, [greater] than any burden, as much as we can carry. (I found: "every day… lavishes upon us" He always behaves in this manner to us, that for every distress there is a salvation.)

notes.2424: (tn, Heb): “the hairy forehead of the one who walks about in his guilt.” The singular is representative.

rashi.heb:
*האל לנו אל למושעות.* 
אל מושיע הוא לנו ולפניו יש הרבה תוצאות מיני מות תוצאות דרכים אל המות אך לא עלינו הוא נותנם אבל ימחץ בהם ראש אויביו:
rashi.eng: *God is to us the God of salvations.* God is our Savior, but He has many paths, i.e., kinds of death. תוצאות means, ways to death. However, He does not lay them upon us, but with them He wounds the head of His enemies.

notes.2425: (tn): That is, the enemies mentioned in v. 21. Even if they retreat to distant regions, God will retrieve them and make them taste his judgment.

rashi.heb:
*קדקד שער.* 
קדקדו של עשו שהוא איש שעיר המתהלך תמיד באשמיו (ואינו חוזר מרעתו):
rashi.eng: *the hairy pate.* The pate of Esau, who is a “hairy man,” and who always goes with his guilt.

notes.2426: (tc): Some (e.g. NRSV) prefer to emend מָחַץ (makhats, “smash; stomp”; see v. 21) to רָחַץ (rakhats, “bathe”; see Ps 58:10).
notes.2427: (tn, Heb): “[and] the tongue of your dogs from [the] enemies [may eat] its portion.”

rashi.heb:
*אמר ה' מבשן אשיב.* 
כי כן הבטיח להשיב אותנו מתוך אבירי בשן ומאיי הים:
rashi.eng: *The Lord said, “I shall restore from Bashan”.* For so He promised to restore us from the mighty ones of Bashan and from the islands of the sea.

notes.2428: (tn): The subject is probably indefinite, referring to bystanders in general who witness the procession.
notes.2429: (tn): The Hebrew text has simply “in holiness.” The words “who marches along” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*למען תמחץ.* 
רגלינו בדם 
כשימחץ את ראש האויב תהא רגלינו בוקעת בדמם תמחץ לשון בוקע בתוך הדם כמו (שופטי' ה) מחצה וחלפה רקתו כמו בקעה ול' משנה הוא והיו עולי רגלים בוקעים עד ארכבותיהם בדם ד"א תמחץ שם כלי ששואבין בו יין מן הבור מחץ שמו במסכת ע"ז:
rashi.eng: *In order that your foot may wade through blood.* When He crushes the head of the enemy, our feet will wade through their blood. תִּמְחַץ is an expression of splitting into the blood, as (Jud. 5:26): “she split (ומחצה) and penetrated his temple,” like בָּקְעָה, she split. This is Mishnaic Hebrew: “and the pilgrims were wading (בוקעים) up to their knees in blood.” Another explanation: תִּמְחַץ The name of a vessel with which they draw wine from the pit is called מַחַץ, in Tractate Avodah Zarah (72b).

rashi.heb: *מאויבים.* מדם האויבים:
rashi.eng: *from the enemies.* From the blood of the enemies.

rashi.heb:
*מנהו.* 
תהיה פרנסתו כדאמרינן מאי משמע דמן לישנא דמזוני הוא דכתיב (דניאל א׳:י׳) אשר מנה את מאכלכם וגומר:
rashi.eng: *will have its portion.* Heb. מנהו, its sustenance will be, as we say (Suc. 39b): “How do we know that מן is an expression of food?” For it is written (Dan. 1:10): “who appointed (מנה) your food, etc.”

notes.2431: (sn): To celebrate a military victory, women would play tambourines (see Exod 15:20; Judg 11:34; 1 Sam 18:6).

rashi.heb:
*ראו הליכותיך אלהים.* 
כלומר לאלו נאה לך להושי' שכשראו הליכותיך בקדושתך בים קדמו שרים לשורר לפניך שירת הים ואחריהם באו הנוגנים אלו המלאכים:
rashi.eng: *They saw Your ways, O God.* That is to say, it is fitting that You save these people, for when they saw Your ways in Your sanctity in the sea, singers came first to sing before You the Song of the Sea, and after them came the minstrels, these are the angels.

notes.2432: (tn, Heb): “from the fountain of Israel,” which makes little, if any, sense here. The translation assumes an emendation to בְּמִקְרָאֵי (b�miqra’ey, “in the assemblies of [Israel]”).

rashi.heb:
*בתוך עלמות תופפות.* 
בתוך מרים ונערותיה אשר לקחה התוף בידה ואמרו בשבחם:
rashi.eng: *in the midst of maidens playing timbrels.* With Miriam and her maidens, who took the timbrel in her hand, and they said with their praise…

notes.2433: (sn): Little Benjamin, their ruler. This may allude to the fact that Israel’s first king, Saul, was from the tribe of Benjamin.
notes.2434: (tc): The MT reads רִגְמָתָם (rigmatam), which many derive from רָגַם (ragam, “to kill by stoning”) and translates, “[in] their heaps,” that is, in large numbers.

rashi.heb:
*במקהלות ברכו אלהים אד' ממקור ישראל.* 
אף עוברים ממעי אמן אמרו שירה:
rashi.eng: *In congregations bless God, the Lord, from the womb of Israel.* Even the fetuses in their mothers’ wombs recited the Song.

notes.2435: (tn, Heb): “God has commanded your strength.” The statement is apparently addressed to Israel (see v. 26).

rashi.heb:
*שם בנימין.* 
הצעיר נעשה רודה עליהם:
rashi.eng: *There Benjamin.* the youngest became the ruler over them.

rashi.heb:
*רודם.* 
כמו רודם בקמ"ץ משם זכה להיות מלך לפי שירד תחלה לים וכן אמר לו שמואל לשאול (שמואל א ט״ו:י״ז) הלא אם קטן אתה בעיניך ראש שבטי ישראל אתה ותרגמו יונתן שבטא דבנימן עבר בימא בריש כל שאר שבטיא:
rashi.eng: *rules over them.* Heb. רֹדֵם, like רֹדָם, with a “kamatz.” From there, he merited to become king because he descended first into the sea, and so did Samuel say to Saul (I Sam. 15:17): “Even if you are small in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Israel?” which Jonathan paraphrases: The tribe of Benjamin crossed the sea at the head of all the other tribes.

rashi.heb:
*שרי יהודה רגמתם.* 
מתקנאים בהם וזורקין בהם אבנים וכן שרי זבולון ונפתלי וכן אמר לו צוה אלהיך עזך (סא"א), ד"א (רגמתם רקמתם לבושן בגדי וכו') רקמתם לשון ארגמן, כך חברו מנחם:
rashi.eng: *the princes of Judah pelt them with stones.* They envy them and throw stones at them, and so do the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naftali. So, he says to him, “Your God has commanded your strength.” Another explanation: רִגְמָתָם is the equivalent of רִקְמָתָם, their embroidery, their embroidered garments, an expression of purple (ארגמן). In this way Menachem associated it (p. 161).

notes.2436: (tn, Heb): “Be strong, O God, [you] who have acted for us, from your temple in Jerusalem.” For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*עוזה אלהים וגו'.* 
עכשיו חוזר המשורר לתפלתו שהתפלל יקום אלהים ויפוצו אויביו עוזה אלהים והתגבר אשר כל אלה פעלת לנו:
rashi.eng: *show this strength, O God, etc..* Now the Psalmist returns to his prayer that he prayed, “Let God rise, and let His enemies scatter.” Show Your strength, O God, and strengthen Yourself, for You have wrought all these for us.

notes.2437: (tn): The Hebrew verb גָּעַר (ga’ar) is often understood to mean “rebuke.” In some cases it is apparent that scolding or threatening is in view (see Gen 37:10; Ruth 2:16; Zech 3:2). However, in militaristic contexts such as Ps 68 this translation is inadequate, for the verb refers in this setting to the warrior’s battle cry, which terrifies and paralyzes the enemy. See A. Caquot, TDOT 3:53, and note the use of the verb in Ps 106:9 and Nah 1:4, as well as the related noun in Job 26:11; Pss 18:15; 76:6; 104:7; Isa 50:2; 51:20; 66:15.
notes.2438: (sn): The wild beast of the reeds probably refers to a hippopotamus, which in turn symbolizes the nation of Egypt.
notes.2439: (tn, Heb): “an assembly of bulls, with calves of the nations.”
notes.2440: (tn, Heb): “humbling himself.” The verb form is a Hitpael participle from the root רָפַס (rafas, “to trample”). The Hitpael of this verb appears only here and in Prov 6:3, where it seems to mean, “humble oneself,” a nuance that fits nicely in this context. The apparent subject is “wild beast” or “assembly,” though both of these nouns are grammatically feminine, while the participle is a masculine form. Perhaps one should emend the participial form to a masculine plural (מִתְרַפִּם, mitrapim) and understand “bulls” or “calves” as the subject.
notes.2441: (tc, Heb): “with pieces [?] of silver.” The meaning of the Hebrew term רַצֵּי (ratsey) is unclear. It is probably best to emend the text to בֶּצֶר וְכָסֶף (betser v�khasef, “[with] gold and silver”).
notes.2442: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.2443: (tn): The verb בָּזַר (bazar) is an alternative form of פָּזַר (pazar, “scatter”).

rashi.heb:
*מהיכלך על ירושלם.* 
וממה שיראו המלכים כבוד היכלך אשר על ירושלים יובילו לך דורון ושי:
rashi.eng: *From Your Temple, which is over Jerusalem, etc..* And since the kings will see the glory of Your temple, which is over Jerusalem, they will bring You a gift and a tribute.

notes.2444: (tn): This noun, which occurs only here in the OT, apparently means “red cloth” or “bronze articles” (see HALOT 362 s.v. חַשְׁמַן; cf. NEB “tribute”). Traditionally the word has been taken to refer to “nobles” (see BDB 365 s.v. חַשְׁמַן; cf. NIV “envoys”). Another option would be to emend the text to הַשְׁמַנִּים (hashmannim, “the robust ones,” i.e., leaders).
notes.2446: (tn, Heb): “causes its hands to run,” which must mean “quickly stretches out its hands” (to present tribute).

rashi.heb:
*גער חית קנה.* 
זה עמלק שנמשל כחית יער הדר בין הקנים:
rashi.eng: *Rebuke the people of the forest.* This is Ishmael [Esau], who is compared to the “boar from the forest,” which dwells among the reeds (below 80:14).

rashi.heb:
*עדת אבירים בעגלי עמים.* 
עם ששמנו ועשתו כפרים אבירים בתוך שאר האומות שאינם אלא כעגלים לנגדם:
rashi.eng: *the congregation of mighty bulls, among peoples like calves.* A people that has become fat and thick like mighty bulls among the other nations, which are merely like calves as compared to them.

rashi.heb:
*מתרפס ברצי כסף.* 
אינם מתרצי' לכל אדם אלא א"כ מרצה להם מעות:
rashi.eng: *submitting himself for pieces of silver.* They do not submit themselves to any person unless he persuades them with money.

rashi.heb:
*בזר עמים.* 
פזרו את השבטים כד"א (דברים ל״ג:ג׳) אף חובב עמים ותמיד קרבות יחפצון, חפצים להלחם בנו:
rashi.eng: *he scatters peoples.* They scattered the tribes, as it is said: (Deut. 33:3): “Also He loves the peoples,” and they always desire battles. They want to fight with us.

rashi.heb:
*יאתיו חשמנים.* 
ואז כשתחריב את עמלק ויקום מלך המשיח יביאו לך דורונו' ממצרי' ומכוש, ומנחם פתר משמנים שם מדינה יושבי חשמונה והפותרים פותרין אותו ל' דורון:
rashi.eng: *Gifts will be brought.* (Then, when You destroy Esau and the King Messiah arises, they will bring you gifts from Egypt and from Cush. Parshandatha) Then, when You scatter the enemy, and the King Messiah arises in the future, they will bring you gifts from Egypt and from Cush. Menachem interpreted חשמנים as the name of a province, the dwellers of Hashmonah (p. 96), but the commentators interpret it as an expression of a gift.

notes.2447: (tc, Heb): “to the one who rides through the skies of skies of ancient times.” If the MT is retained, one might translate, “to the one who rides through the ancient skies.” (שְׁמֵי [sh�mey, “skies of”] may be accidentally repeated.) The present translation assumes an emendation to בַּשָּׁמַיִם מִקֶּדֶם (bashamayim miqqedem, “[to the one who rides] through the sky from ancient times”), that is, God has been revealing his power through the storm since ancient times.
notes.2448: (tn, Heb): “he gives his voice a strong voice.” In this context God’s “voice” is the thunder that accompanies the rain (see vv. 8-9, as well as Deut 33:26).

rashi.heb:
*שירו לאלהים.* 
שהראם גדלו וגאל את עמו:
rashi.eng: *sing to God.* Who showed His greatness and redeemed His people.

notes.2450: (sn): The language of v. 34 echoes that of Deut 33:26.

rashi.heb:
*הן יתן.* 
הן נותן:
rashi.eng: *behold He gives forth.* Heb. יתן, behold He gives.

notes.2451: (tn, Heb): “awesome [is] God from his holy places.” The plural of מִקְדָּשׁ (miqdash, “holy places”) perhaps refers to the temple precincts (see Ps 73:17; Jer 51:51).
notes.2454: (sn): Psalm 69. The psalmist laments his oppressed condition and asks the Lord to deliver him by severely judging his enemies.
notes.2455: (tn, Heb): “according to lilies.” See the superscription to Ps 45.

rashi.heb:
*נורא אלהים ממקדשיך.* 
ממה שהחרבתו אתה יראוי אם למקדשו לא נשא פנים קל וחומר לרשעים ומדרש אגדה אל תקרי ממקדשיך אלא ממקודשיך, שכשהקב"ה עושה דין בצדיקים מתירא ומתעלה ומתקלס, וכן הוא אומר בקרובי אקדש (ויקרא י') ונקדש בכבודי (שמות כ"ט) במיתת שני בני אהרן, ורבותינו דרשו כל המזמור עד ברוך ה' יום יום על מתן תורה וגשם נדבות במתן תורה וחיתך ישבו בה, ואני אין לבי מתיישב לאמן לשון ישבו בה בל' נתיישבו בתורה וההר חמד אלהים לשבתו אין מתיישב לדרשו על הר סיני שהרי לא לשבתו חמדו ולא לשכון בו לנצח וכאן כתיב ישכון לנצח וכן מלכי צבאות פירשו כמו מלאכי צבאות ואין זה לשון המקרא:
rashi.eng: *You are feared, O God, from Your Sanctuary.* Because You destroyed it, You are feared. If He did not show favoritism to His [own] Sanctuary, surely [He will] not [show favoritism] to the wicked of the heathens. The Midrash Aggadah explains: Do not read: מִמִּקְדָּשֶׁיךָ, “from Your Sanctuaries,” but מִמְּקֻדְּשֶׁיךָ, “from Your hallowed ones.” When the Holy One, blessed be He, executes justice upon the righteous, He is feared, elevated, and praised. Similarly, it is said (Lev. 10:3): “Through those near to me I will be sanctified.” [Also] (Exod. 29:43), “and it will be sanctified with My honor” [i.e., with My honored ones]. With the death of Aaron’s two sons (Zev. 115b). Our Rabbis, however, expounded on the entire psalm until (verse 20): “Blessed is the Lord; every day” as referring to the giving of the Torah; (verse 10) “generous rain” refers to the giving of the Torah, and (verse 11) “Your congregation dwelt therein,” means that they became engrossed in Torah (Mid. Ps. 68 with variations). But as for me I feel uncertain in explaining the expression ישבוּ as meaning that they became engrossed in Torah. Also, my heart is uneasy at explaining (verse 17) “the mountain that God desired for His dwelling” as referring to Mt. Sinai, because He did not desire it for His dwelling and [did] not [want] to dwell there forever, whereas here it is written: “Even the Lord will dwell there forever.” Likewise (verse 13): “Kings (מלכי) of hosts,” he explained as “angels (מלאכי) of hosts,” which is not the language of Scripture.

notes.2456: (tn): The Hebrew term נפשׁ (nefesh) here refers to the psalmist’s throat or neck. The psalmist compares himself to a helpless, drowning man.

rashi.heb:
*על שושנים.* 
על ישראל שהם כשושנה בין החוחים שהחוחים מנקבין אותם והתפלל עליהם:
rashi.eng: *on shoshannim.* Concerning Israel, who are like a rose (שושנה) among the thorns, pricked by the thorns, and he prayed for them.

notes.2457: (tn, Heb): “and there is no place to stand.”

rashi.heb:
*כי באו מים.* 
האומות:
rashi.eng: *for water has come up.* the nations.

notes.2460: (tn, Heb): “my eyes fail from waiting for my God.” The psalmist has intently kept his eyes open, looking for God to intervene, but now his eyes are watery and bloodshot, impairing his vision.

rashi.heb:
*ביון מצולה.* 
בבוץ טיט של מצולה:
rashi.eng: *in muddy depths.* In the mire, the mud of the deep.

rashi.heb:
*ושבולת.* 
הוא שטף חוזק הנהר פי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and the current.* That is the flood of the strength of the river, fil in Old French, current.

notes.2461: (tn, Heb): “[with] a lie.” The Hebrew noun שֶׁקֶר (sheqer, “lie”) is used here as an adverb, “falsely, wrongfully” (see Pss 35:19; 38:19).
notes.2462: (tn): The Hebrew verb עָצַם (’atsam) can sometimes mean “are strong,” but here it probably focuses on numerical superiority; note the parallel verb רָבַב (ravav, “be many”).
notes.2463: (tn, Heb): “that which I did not steal, then I restore.” Apparently אָז (’az, “then”) is used here to emphasize the verb that follows. They make me repay what I did not steal. The psalmist’s enemies falsely accuse him and hold him accountable for alleged crimes he did not even commit.

rashi.heb:
*נחר.* 
יבש כמו (איוב ל׳:ל׳) חרה מני חורב:
rashi.eng: *has become parched.* Heb. נחר, dry, as (Job 30:30): “are burned (חרה) with heat.”

rashi.heb:
*כלו עיני.* 
כל תוחלת ממושכה קרויה כליון עינים כמו (דברים כ״ח:ל״ב) וכלות אליהם כל היום, מכלות עינים (ויקרא כ״ו:ט״ז) ועיני רשעים תכלינה (איוב י״א:כ׳):
rashi.eng: *my eyes fail.* Any drawn-out hope is called “failure of the eyes,” as (Deut. 28:32): “and pine after them all day.” [Similarly] (Lev. 26:16): “that cause the eyes to pine away;” (Job 11:20), “and the eyes of the wicked will pine away.”

notes.2465: (sn): The psalmist is the first to admit that he is not perfect. But even so, he is innocent of the allegations which his enemies bring against him (v. 5b). God, who is aware of his foolish sins and guilt, can testify to the truth of his claim.

rashi.heb:
*אויבי שקר.* 
שונאים אותי על שקר שאין אני רודף אחר שקר שלהם לתפוש טעותם:
rashi.eng: *who are my enemies because of lies.* They hate me because of a lie, because I do not pursue their lies to adopt their error.

rashi.heb:
*אז אשיב.* 
כשהם נאספים עלי אני משחד אותם בממון מה שלא גזלתי מהם:
rashi.eng: *I will then return.* When they gather against me, I bribe them with money that I did not steal from them.

notes.2466: (tn, Heb): “O Master, Lord of hosts.” Both titles draw attention to God’s sovereign position.

rashi.heb:
*אל יבשו בי קויך.* 
אל תניחני בידם פן יבושו קויך במה שמאורע בי ויאמרו הלא כך אירע למי שהיה מקוה להקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *Do not let those who hope for You be shamed.* Do not leave me in their hands lest those who hope for You be shamed by what happens to me and say, “Didn’t that happen to one who hopes to the Holy One, blessed be He?”

notes.2470: (tn, Heb): “and I am estranged to my brothers, and a foreigner to the sons of my mother.”

notes.2471: (tn): Or “for.” This verse explains that the psalmist’s suffering is due to his allegiance to God.
notes.2473: (sn): God’s house, the temple, here represents by metonymy God himself.
notes.2474: (tn, Heb): “the insults of those who insult you fall upon me.” Jn 2:17 applies the first half of this verse to Jesus’ ministry in the context of John’s account of Jesus cleansing the temple.

rashi.heb:
*לאחי.* 
לעשו:
rashi.eng: *to my brothers.* To Esau.

notes.2475: (sn): Fasting was a practice of mourners. By refraining from normal activities such as eating food, the mourner demonstrated the sincerity of his sorrow.
notes.2476: (tn, Heb): “and it becomes insults to me.”

rashi.heb:
*קנאת ביתך.* 
ראו החבה שנהגת בנו בעוד ביתך קיים ונתקנאו בי:
rashi.eng: *the envy of Your house.* They saw the love that You showed us when Your house was still existing, and they envied me.

notes.2477: (tn, Heb): “and I am an object of ridicule to them.”

rashi.heb:
*ואבכה בצום נפשי.* 
בתעניתי:
rashi.eng: *And I bewailed my soul in fast.* In my fast.

rashi.heb:
*ותהי לחרפות לי.* 
מה שאני בוכה ומתענה לפניך הם מתלוצצים עלי:
rashi.eng: *and it was a disgrace for me.* When I weep and fast before You, they mock me.

notes.2478: (tn, Heb): “the mocking songs of the drinkers of beer.”

notes.2479: (tn, Heb): “as for me, [may] my prayer be to you, O Lord, [in] a time of favor.”
notes.2480: (tn, Heb): “O God, in the abundance of your loyal love, answer me in the faithfulness of your deliverance.”

rashi.heb:
*ונגינות.* 
בי לשותי שכר (סא"א):
rashi.eng: *and melodies.* they made of me for those who imbibe strong drink.

rashi.heb:
*ואני תפלתי לך ה'.* 
יהי עת תפלתי עת רצון:
rashi.eng: *But, as for me, may my prayer to You, O Lord, be.* may the time of my prayer be a desirable time.

notes.2482: (tn, Heb): “well,” which here symbolizes the place of the dead (cf. Ps 55:23).
notes.2483: (tn, Heb): “do not let the well close its mouth upon me.”

rashi.heb:
*ואל תאטר.* 
ואל תסגור עלי:
rashi.eng: *and let not… close.* And let it not close over me.

rashi.heb:
*באר.* 
צרה נכריה זו את פיה לבלעני:
rashi.eng: *a well.* This strange trouble [shall not close] its mouth to swallow me up.

rashi.heb:
*תאטר.* 
כמו אטר יד ימינו (שופטים ג׳:ט״ו) סגור יד ימינו שאינו משתמש בה:
rashi.eng: *close.* Heb. תאטר, as (Jud. 3:15): “with a shriveled (אטר) right hand” that he does not use it.

notes.2485: (tn, Heb): “do not hide your face from.” The Hebrew idiom “hide the face” can (1) mean “ignore” (see Pss 10:11; 13:1; 51:9) or (2) carry the stronger idea of “reject” (see Pss 30:7; 88:14).

notes.2487: (tn, Heb): “come near my life and redeem it.” The verb “redeem” casts the Lord in the role of a leader who protects members of his extended family in times of need and crisis (see Ps 19:14).

rashi.heb:
*קרבה אל נפשי.* 
(קרב אלי):
rashi.eng: *Come close to my soul.* (Come close to me.)

rashi.heb:
*גאלה.* 
גאול אותה:
rashi.eng: *redeem it.* Heb. גאלה, [equivalent to] גְאוֹל אוֹתָה.

notes.2489: (tn, Heb): “break my heart.” The “heart” is viewed here as the origin of the psalmist’s emotions.
notes.2490: (tn): The verb form appears to be a Qal preterite from an otherwise unattested root נוּשׁ (nush), which some consider an alternate form of אָנַשׁ (’anash, “be weak; be sick”; see BDB 60 s.v. I אָנַשׁ). Perhaps the form should be emended to a Niphal, וָאֵאָנְשָׁה (va’e’onshah, “and I am sick”). The Niphal of אָנַשׁ occurs in 2 Sam 12:15, where it is used to describe David’s sick child.
notes.2492: (tn, Heb): “and I wait for sympathy, but there is none.” The form נוּד (nud) is an infinitive functioning as a verbal noun:, “sympathizing.” Some suggest emending the form to a participle נָד (nad, “one who shows sympathy”). The verb נוּד (nud) also has the nuance “show sympathy” in Job 2:11; 42:11 and Isa 51:19.

notes.2493: (tn): According to BDB 912 s.v. II רֹאשׁ the term can mean “a bitter and poisonous plant.”
notes.2494: (sn): John 19:28-30 appears to understand Jesus’ experience on the cross as a fulfillment of this passage (or Ps 22:15). See the study note on the word “thirsty” in John 19:28.

rashi.heb:
*ואנושה.* 
ואאנש ואחלה כמו (מיכה א׳:ט׳) כי אנושה מכותיה וכמו (ש"ב י"ב) ויאנש הילד דבת שבע, וא"ת היאך האל"ף זו משמשת שורש ומשמשת שימוש המיסב הדיבור אל המדבר כן דרך תיבה שתחלתה אל"ף כגון (מלאכי א׳:ב׳) ואהב את יעקב אני אהבי אהב (משלי ח׳:י״ז) הרי הוא כמו ואאהב, וכן (צפניה א׳:ב׳) אסף אסף כמו אאסף:
rashi.eng: *and I have become ill.* Heb. ואנושה, I am ailing and sick, as (Micah 1:9): “For she is mortally ill (אנושה) [from] her wounds,” and as (II Sam. 12:15): “and the child (sic) became mortally ill (ויאנש),” of Bathsheba. Now if you ask how this “aleph” serves as a radical and also as a prefix denoting the first person, this is the way of a word beginning with “aleph.” For example, (Mal. 1:2): “and I loved (וָאֹהַב) Jacob;” (Prov. 8:17), “I will love (אֵהָב) those who love me.” It is equivalent to וָאֶאֶהַב Similarly, (Zeph. 1:2): “I will totally destroy (אָסֹף אָסֵף),” like אֶאֶסֹף.

rashi.heb:
*לנוד.* 
שיבואו לי אוהבים לנוד לי ולנחמני:
rashi.eng: *for sympathy.* Heb. לנוד, to shake. That friends should come to me to shake [their heads] over me and to comfort me.

notes.2495: (tc, Heb): “and to the friends for a snare.” The plural of שָׁלוֹם (shalom, “peace”) is used in Ps 55:20 of one’s “friends.” If the reading of the MT is retained here, the term depicts the psalmist’s enemies as a close-knit group of friends who are bound together by their hatred for the psalmist. Some prefer to revocalize the text as וּלְשִׁלּוּמִים (ul�shillumim, “and for retribution”). In this case the noun stands parallel to פַּח (pakh, “trap”) and מוֹקֵשׁ (moqesh, “snare”), and one might translate, “may their dining table become a trap before them, [a means of] retribution and a snare” (cf. NIV).

rashi.heb:
*בברותי.* 
בסעודתי כמו תבא נא תמר אחותי ואברה מידה (שמואל ב י״ג:ה׳) ראש מרה:
rashi.eng: *into my food.* Heb. בברותי, into my food, as (II Sam. 13:6): “Let my sister Tamar come now, etc., that I may eat (ואברה) from her hand.”

notes.2496: (tn, Heb): “may their eyes be darkened from seeing.”

rashi.heb:
*ולשלומים.* 
כשיקוו לשלום יהפך שלומם למוקש:
rashi.eng: *and for peace.* When they hope for peace, may their peace be turned into a snare.

notes.2498: (tn, Heb): “anger.” “Anger” here refers metonymically to divine judgment, which is the practical effect of God’s anger.
notes.2499: (tn, Heb): “the rage of your anger.” The phrase “rage of your anger” employs an appositional genitive. Synonyms are joined in a construct relationship to emphasize the single idea. For a detailed discussion of the grammatical point with numerous examples, see Y. Avishur, “Pairs of Synonymous Words in the Construct State (and in Appositional Hendiadys) in Biblical Hebrew,” Semitics 2 (1971), 17-81.

notes.2500: (tn, Heb): “in their tents may there not be one who dwells.” In Acts 1:20 Peter applies the language of this verse to Judas’ experience. By changing the pronouns from plural to singular, he is able to apply the ancient curse, pronounced against the psalmist’s enemies, to Judas in particular.

notes.2502: (tn, Heb): “for you, the one whom you strike, they chase.”
notes.2503: (tn, Heb): “they announce the pain of your wounded ones” (i.e., “the ones whom you wounded,” as the parallel line makes clear). The psalmist is innocent of the false charges made by his enemies (v. 4), but he is also aware of his sinfulness (v. 5) and admits that he experiences divine discipline (v. 26) despite his devotion to God (v. 9). Here he laments that his enemies take advantage of such divine discipline by harassing and slandering him. They “kick him while he’s down,” as the expression goes.

notes.2505: (tn, Heb): “let them not come into your vindication.”

rashi.heb:
*כי.* 
את העם הזה אשר אתה הכית:
rashi.eng: *For.* this nation, which You smote.

rashi.heb:
*רדפו.* 
אתה קצפת מעט והם עזרו לרעה:
rashi.eng: *they pursued.* For You were a little angry, and they helped cause harm.

rashi.heb:
*ואל מכאוב חלליך יספרו.* 
דבריהם לבוא בעצה נשחיתם בהיותם כאבים:
rashi.eng: *and about the pain of those whom You wounded they tell.* their words, to plot: “Let us destroy them while they are in pain.”

notes.2506: (tn, Heb): “let them be wiped out of the scroll of the living.” The phrase the scroll of the living occurs only here in the OT. It pictures a scroll or census list containing the names of the citizens of a community. When an individual died, that person’s name was removed from the list. So this curse is a very vivid way of asking that the enemies die.
notes.2507: (tn, Heb): “and with the godly let them not be written.” Do not let their names be listed with the godly. This curse pictures a scroll in which God records the names of his loyal followers. The psalmist makes the point that his enemies have no right to be included in this list of the godly.

notes.2508: (tn, Heb): “your deliverance, O God, may it protect me.”

notes.2509: (tn, Heb): “I will praise the name of God with a song.”
notes.2510: (tn, Heb): “I will magnify him with thanks.”

notes.2511: (sn): You who seek God refers to those who seek to have a relationship with God by obeying and worshiping him (see Ps 53:2).
notes.2512: (tn, Heb): “may your heart[s] live.” See Ps 22:26.

rashi.heb:
*ותיטב.* 
הלולי לה':
rashi.eng: *And it will appeal to the Lord.* My praise to the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*משור פר.* 
הוא שור שהקריב אדם הראשון שנברא בקומתו וביום שנקרא שור בו ביום הביאו שהשור בן יומו קרוי שור שנאמר (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ז) שור או כשב או עז כי יולד, בו ביום נדמה לפר שהוא בן שלש:
rashi.eng: *more than a young bull that is mature.* That is the bull sacrificed by Adam, which was created at its height. On the day it was called שּׁוֹר, on that very day, he brought it, for a bull on day of its birth is called שּׁוֹר, as it is said (Lev. 22:27): “A bull (שור), a lamb, or a goat, that is born.” On that very day, it resembled a פַּר, which is a three-year old.

rashi.heb:
*מקרן מפריס.* 
קרנותיו קדמו לפרסותיו שהרי בקומתו ובקרניו נברא וראשו יצא מן הארץ תחלה כדרך כל הנולדים הוציאתן הארץ נמצאו קרניו קדמו לרגליו:
rashi.eng: *with horns and hooves.* Its horns preceded its hooves, because it was created at its height with its horns, and its head emerged from the ground first; the earth thrust them forth in the manner in which all creatures are born, so that its horns preceded its feet.

notes.2513: (tn, Heb): “his prisoners he does not despise.”

notes.2514: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (God’s people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.2515: (tn, Heb): “it.” The third feminine singular pronominal suffix probably refers to “Zion” (see Pss 48:12; 102:14); thus the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.2516: (tn, Heb): “the lovers of his name.” The phrase refers to those who are loyal to God (cf. v. 35). See Pss 5:11; 119:132; Isa 56:6.
notes.2517: (sn): Verses 35-36 appear to be an addition to the psalm from the time of the exile. The earlier lament reflects an individual’s situation, while these verses seem to reflect a communal application of it.
notes.2518: (sn): Psalm 70. This psalm is almost identical to Ps 40:13-17. The psalmist asks for God’s help and for divine retribution against his enemies.
notes.2519: (tn, Heb): “to cause to remember.” The same form, a Hiphil infinitive of זָכַר (zakhar, “remember”), also appears in the superscription of Ps 38. Some understand this in the sense of “for the memorial offering,” but it may carry the idea of bringing one’s plight to God’s attention (see P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 303).

notes.2520: (tn, Heb): “O God, to rescue me.” A main verb is obviously missing. The verb רָצָה (ratsah, “be willing”) should be supplied (see Ps 40:13). Ps 40:13 uses the divine name “Lord” rather than “God.”
notes.2521: (tn, Heb): “hurry to my help.” See Pss 22:19; 38:22.

rashi.heb:
*לדוד להזכיר.* 
ל' תפלה הוא, כמו ואנחנו בשם ה' אלהינו נזכיר (לעיל כ'), וכן בדברי הימים להזכיר ולהודות לה' ובמדרש תהלים ראיתי משל למלך שכעס על צאנו וסתר את הדיר והוציא את הצאן ואת הרועה אחר זמן החזיר את הצאן ובנה את הדיר ולא הזכיר את הרועה אמר הרועה הרי הצאן מוחזר והדיר בנוי ואני איני נזכר כך למעלה מן הענין נאמר כי אלהים יושיע ציון וגו' ואוהבי שמו ישכנו בה הרי הדיר בנוי והצאן כנוס והרועה (זה דוד) לא נזכר לכך נאמר לדוד להזכיר אלהים להצילני:
rashi.eng: *of David, to make mention.* This is an expression of prayer, as (above 20:8): “but we pray (נזכיר) in the name of the Lord our God.” Similarly, in (I) Chronicles (16:4): “to invoke (להזכיר) and to give thanks to the Lord.” In Midrash Psalms (70:1) I saw: This is comparable to a king who became wroth with his flock, and demolished the sheepcote and took out the flock and the shepherd. Sometime later, he restored the flock and rebuilt the sheepcote, but he did not mention the shepherd. Said the shepherd, “Behold, the flock is restored and the sheepcote is rebuilt, but I am not mentioned.” Similarly, in the preceding chapter it says: “When God saves Zion, etc., and those who love His name dwell therein.” Behold the sheepcote is built and the flock is brought into it, but I am not mentioned. Therefore it says: “Of David, to make mention. O God, to save me.”

notes.2522: (tn, Heb): “may they be embarrassed and ashamed, the ones seeking my life.” Ps 40:14 has “together” after “ashamed,” and “to snatch it away” after “my life.”
notes.2523: (tn): The four prefixed verbal forms in this verse are understood as jussives. The psalmist is calling judgment down on his enemies. See Ps 35:4 for a similar prayer.

notes.2524: (tn): The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive in this imprecation.
notes.2525: (tn, Heb): “May they be turned back according to their shame, those who say, ‘Aha! Aha!’” Ps 40:15 has the verb “humiliated” instead of “turned back” and adds “to me” after “say.”

notes.2526: (tn, Heb): “those who love,” which stands metonymically for its cause, the experience of being delivered by God.
notes.2527: (tn): The three prefixed verbal forms prior to the quotation are understood as jussives. The psalmist balances out his imprecation against his enemies with a prayer of blessing on the godly.
notes.2528: (tn): Ps 40:16 uses the divine name “Lord” here instead of “God.”
notes.2529: (tn): The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive, “may the Lord be magnified [in praise].” Another option is to take the verb as an imperfect, “the Lord is great.” See Ps 35:27.

rashi.heb:
*ישובו על עקב בשתם.* 
מדה במדה כמו שעשו לי:
rashi.eng: *Let them return in the path of their shame.* Measure for measure, as they did to me.

rashi.heb:
*על עקב.* 
באותו מעגל עצמו אנציש"טראציש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *in the path.* In that very same path, en ses trazes, on (their) its footsteps.

rashi.heb:
*האומרים.* 
עלי:
rashi.eng: *those who say.* about me.

rashi.heb:
*האח האח.* 
ל' חדוה בראותו באויבו כרצונו:
rashi.eng: *“Aha”.* An expression of joy, when one sees that his wishes concerning his enemy have been fulfilled.

notes.2531: (tn): Ps 40:17 has “may the Lord pay attention to me.”
notes.2533: (sn): Psalm 71. The psalmist prays for divine intervention and expresses his confidence that God will protect and vindicate him. The first three verses are very similar to Ps 31:1-3a.

rashi.heb:
*חושה לי.* 
לעזרה:
rashi.eng: *hasten to me.* to aid [me].

notes.2534: (tn, Heb): “in your vindication rescue me and deliver me.” Ps 31:1 omits “and deliver me.”

notes.2537: (tc, Heb): “become for me a rocky summit of a dwelling place.” The Hebrew term מָעוֹן (ma’on, “dwelling place”) should probably be emended to מָעוֹז (ma’oz, “refuge”; see Ps 31:2).
notes.2538: (tc, Heb): “to enter continually, you commanded to deliver me.” The Hebrew phrase לָבוֹא תָּמִיד צִוִּיתָ (lavo’ tamid tsivvita, “to enter continually, you commanded”) should be emended to לְבֵית מְצוּדוֹת (l�vet m�tsudot, “a house of strongholds”; see Ps 31:2).
notes.2539: (sn): You are my high ridge. This metaphor pictures God as a rocky, relatively inaccessible summit, where one would be able to find protection from enemies. See 1 Sam 23:25, 28.

rashi.heb:
*לבוא תמיד.* 
באותו מעון, להנצל בתוכו מן הרודף:
rashi.eng: *in which to enter continually.* into that shelter, to save myself within it from the pursuer.

rashi.heb:
*צוית להושיעני.* 
פעמים רבות הושעתני על ידי שלוחיך:
rashi.eng: *You commanded to save me.* You saved me many times through Your messengers.

rashi.heb:
*וחומץ.* 
כמו חומס וכן (ישעיה א') אשרו חמוץ, נגזל:
rashi.eng: *and robs.* Heb. וחומץ, like וחומס. Similarly (Isa. 1:17): “strengthen the robbed (חמוץ);” the robbed.

notes.2542: (tn, Heb): “O Lord, my source of confidence from my youth.”

notes.2544: (tc): The form in the MT is derived from גָזָה (gazah, “to cut off”), perhaps picturing God as the one who severed the psalmist’s umbilical cord. Many interpreters and translators prefer to emend the text to גֹחִי (gokhiy), from גוּח (gukh) or גִיח, (gikh, “pull out”; see Ps 22:9; cf. the present translation) or to עוּזִּי (’uzziy, “my strength”; cf. NEB “my protector since I left my mother’s womb”).

rashi.heb:
*אתה גוזי.* 
אתה מוציאי ומעבירי כמו (במדבר י״א:ל״א) ויגז שלוים, כי גז חיש ונעופה (לקמן צ'):
rashi.eng: *You drew me.* You drew me and caused me to pass, as (Num. 11:31): “and drove up (ויגז) quails;” (below 90:10), “for it is cut off (גז) swiftly and we fly away.”

notes.2546: (tn, Heb): “like a sign [i.e., portent or bad omen] I am to many.”

rashi.heb:
*כמופת הייתי לרבים.* 
רבים ראו צרותי ודאגו פן יקראם דוגמת צרתי פן אהיה להם לאות כאשר הוקרה לזה כן יקרה לנו כענין שנאמר (יחזקאל כ"ד) והיה יחזקאל לכם למופת:
rashi.eng: *I was as an example for the multitude.* Many saw my troubles and worried lest an example of my trouble befall them; lest I be an example for them: “just as happened to this one, so will happen to us.” As the matter is said (Ezek. 24:24): “and Ezekiel will be an example to you.”
