The LXX and some other ancient textual witnesses assume a polal (passive) verbal form here. In this case the earth becomes the subject of the verb and the verb is understood as third feminine singular rather than second masculine singular.
notes.3271: (tn, Heb): “and from everlasting to everlasting you [are] God.” Instead of אֵל (’el, “God”) the LXX reads אַל (’al, “not”) and joins the negative particle to the following verse, making the verb תָּשֵׁב (tashev) a jussive. In this case v. 3a reads as a prayer, “do not turn man back to a low place.” However, taking תָּשֵׁב as a jussive is problematic in light of the following following wayyiqtol form וַתֹּאמֶר (vato’mer, “and you said/say”).

rashi.heb:
*בטרם הרים יולדו.* 
נבראו ובטרם חוללת ארץ ותבל ומעולם ראשון ועד עולם אחרון אתה אל:
rashi.eng: *Before the mountains were born.* [i.e., before they] were created, and before You brought forth the earth and the inhabited world, and from the first world to the last world, You are God.

notes.3272: (tn): In this context the shortened prefix form does not function as a preterite, but indicates what is typical of the world.
notes.3273: (tn): The Hebrew term דַּכָּא (daka’) carries the basic sense of “crushed.” Elsewhere it refers to those who are “crushed” in spirit or contrite of heart (see Ps 34:18; Isa 57:15). If one understands this nuance here, then v. 3 is observing that God leads mankind to repentance (the term שׁוּב, shuv, “return,” which appears twice in this verse, is sometimes used of repentance.) However, the following context laments mankind’s mortality and the brevity of life, so it is doubtful if v. 3 should be understood so positively. It is more likely that דַּכָּא here refers to “crushed matter,” that is, the dust that fills the grave (see HALOT 221 s.v. s.v. I דַּכָּא; BDB 194 s.v. דַּכָּא). In this case one may hear an echo of Gen 3:19.

rashi.heb:
*תשב אנוש עד דכא.* 
מביא אתה יסורין על האדם עד שאתה מחזירו להיות תשוש כח וקרוב למות, ותאמר לו ביסורין שובו בני אדם מדרכיכם הרעים:
rashi.eng: *You bring man to the crushing point.* You bring agonies upon man until You reduce him to a weakened state, near death, and You tell him with these agonies, “Return, O sons of men from your evil ways.”

notes.3275: (sn): The divisions of the nighttime. The ancient Israelites divided the night into distinct periods, or “watches.”

rashi.heb:
*כי אלף שנים בעיניך.* 
אלף שנים של בני אדם הם כיום אחד של הקב"ה ועוד מן הלילה עמו כי יום א' של הקב"ה ומעט מן הלילה של הקב"ה הם אלף שנים שהרי לא אמר הכתו' שיהא יומו של הקב"ה אחד כאלף שנים אבל כשיצא מעט מן הלילה עמו אז יומו שלם והוי אלף שנים ולכך מת אדם הראשון תוך אלף שאם היה חי אלף היה יותר מיומו של הקב"ה ושמא שיעור אותה אשמורה הוא כמו שיש ממיתת אדם הראשון עד אלף שנים ואנן לא ידעינן כמה הוי אותה אשמורה כי אם מסברא (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *For a thousand years are in Your eyes.* A thousand years of man are like one day of the Holy One, blessed be He, and part of the night with it; for one day of the Holy One, blessed He, and a little of the night of the Holy One, blessed be He, are a thousand years, for the text does not say that the day of the Holy One, blessed be He, is like a thousand years, but that when a little of the night elapses with it, then His day is complete, and it is a thousand years. Therefore, Adam died within a thousand [years] for had he lived a thousand [years] it would be more than the day of the Holy One, blessed be He. Perhaps the amount of that watch equals the time from the death of Adam until a thousand years, but we do not know how much that watch was, except from conjecture. I found [this]:

rashi.heb: *כי אלף שנים בעיניך וגו'.* וכשעלתה תשובה בדעתך מתחלה יפה דנת ובראת אותה וראוין היו השנים לכך לפי (שלא) היו ימי בני אדם רבים שלא היו אלף שנים בעיניך אלא כיום הולך שעבר וחלף ומעט מן הלילה עמו שהרי אמרת לאדם הראשון (בראשית ב׳:י״ז) כי ביום אכלך ממנו מות תמות וחיה תשע מאות ושלשים שנה נמצאו אלף שנים עולים ליום שלם ומעט מן הלילה עמו:
rashi.eng: *For a thousand years are in Your eyes, etc..* And when repentance came into Your thoughts from the beginning, You judged well and created it. Now those years were appropriate for it because people’s days were many, so that a thousand years were in Your eyes like one passing day, which passed and was gone, with a little of the night with it, for You said to Adam (Gen. 2:17): “for on the day you eat of it, you will surely die,” and he lived nine hundred and thirty years. We find that a thousand years equal one whole day and a little of the night with it.

rashi.heb:
*כיום אתמול כי יעבור.* 
שכבר עבר:
rashi.eng: *like yesterday, which passed.* Which already passed.

notes.3276: (tn, Heb): “you bring them to an end [with] sleep.” The Hebrew verb זָרַם (zaram) has traditionally been taken to mean “flood” or “overwhelm” (note the Polel form of a root זרם in Ps 77:17, where the verb is used of the clouds pouring down rain). However, the verb form here is Qal, not Polel, and is better understood as a homonym meaning “to make an end [of life].” The term שֵׁנָה (shenah, “sleep”) can be taken as an adverbial accusative; it is a euphemism here for death (see Ps 76:5-6).

rashi.heb:
*זרמתם שנה יהיו.* 
עכשיו חטפתם לאותם השנים והבאתם לימים מועטים שאינם אלא כשנת תנומה ששני הדורות שבעים שנה הם, כמו שמפורש בסוף הענין ימי שנותינו בהם שבעים שנה, והם חשובים שינה אחת כענין (לקמן קכ"ז) בשוב ה' את שיבת ציון היינו כחולמים ועל שבעים שנה של גלות בבל נאמר שהיה שבעים שנה:
rashi.eng: *You carry them away as a flood; they are like a sleep.* Now you have seized those years and had them become a few days, which are merely like a sleep of slumber, for the years of the generations are seventy years, as is explained at the end of the chapter: “The days of our years because of them are seventy years,” and they are regarded as one sleep. As the matter that is said (below 126:1) “When the Lord returns the returnees to Zion, we shall be like dreamers.” This was stated regarding the Babylonian exile, which lasted seventy years.

rashi.heb:
*זרמתם.* 
לשון שטיפה כמו (חבקוק ג) זרם מים:
rashi.eng: *You carry them away as a flood.* Heb. זרמתם, an expression of flooding, as (Hab. 3:10): “A stream (זרם) of water.”

rashi.heb:
*בבקר כחציר יחלוף.* 
הנולד בלילה מת בבוקר לסוף השינה ואם
rashi.eng: *in the morning, like grass it passes away.* If one is born at night, he dies in the morning at the end of his sleep. And if,…

notes.3277: (tn): Or “flourishes.” The verb is used of a crown shining in Ps 132:18. Perhaps here in Ps 90:6 it refers to the glistening of the grass in the morning dew.
notes.3278: (tn): The Polel form of this verb occurs only here. Perhaps the form should be emended to a Qal (which necessitates eliminating the final lamed [ל] as dittographic). See Ps 37:2.

rashi.heb:
*בבקר יציץ.* 
מיד חלף ועד בא הערב ימולל ויבש, למה:
rashi.eng: *In the morning, it blossoms.* it passes away immediately, and when evening comes, it is cut off and withered. Why?

rashi.heb:
*כי כלינו באפך וגו'.* 
ועל כל זאת:
rashi.eng: *For we perish from Your wrath, and from Your anger, etc..* That is to say: And because of all this,…

notes.3280: (tn, Heb): “you set our sins in front of you.”
notes.3281: (tn, Heb): “what we have hidden to the light of your face.” God’s face is compared to a light or lamp that exposes the darkness around it.

rashi.heb:
*שתה עונותינו לנגדך.* 
ואת עלומינו את חטאת נעורינו שמת למאור פניך:
rashi.eng: *You have placed our iniquities before You.* and our youth, the sins of our youth, You have placed before the light of Your countenance.

rashi.heb:
*עלמינו.* 
נעורינו כמו (שמואל א יז) בן מי זה העלם:
rashi.eng: *our youth.* Heb. עלמנו, our youth, as (I Sam. 17:56): “whose son is this youth (העלם).”

rashi.heb:
*למאור פניך.* 
למולך להביט בהם:
rashi.eng: *before the light of Your countenance.* opposite You and to look at them.

notes.3283: (tn, Heb): “all our days pass by in your anger.”
notes.3284: (tn, Heb): “we finish our years like a sigh.” In Ezek 2:10 the word הֶגֶה (hegeh) elsewhere refers to a grumbling or moaning sound. Here a brief sigh or moan is probably in view. If so, the simile pictures one’s lifetime as transient. Another option is that the simile alludes to the weakness that characteristically overtakes a person at the end of one’s lifetime. In this case the phrase could be translated, “we end our lives with a painful moan.”

rashi.heb:
*פנו בעברתך.* 
ופנו ונבערו והלכו להם בעברתך:
rashi.eng: *have passed away in Your anger.* Have turned, have been cleared away, and have gone away in Your anger.

rashi.heb:
*כמו הגה.* 
כדבור הממהר לכלות:
rashi.eng: *as a murmur.* Like speech, which hastens to disappear.

notes.3285: (tn, Heb): “the days of our years, in them [are] seventy years.”
notes.3286: (tn, Heb): “or if [there is] strength, eighty years.”
notes.3287: (tn, Heb): “and their pride [is] destruction and wickedness.” The Hebrew noun רֹהַב (rohav) occurs only here. BDB 923 s.v. assigns the meaning “pride,” deriving the noun from the verbal root רהב (“to act stormily [boisterously, arrogantly]”). Here the “pride” of one’s days (see v. 9) probably refers to one’s most productive years in the prime of life. The words translated “destruction and wickedness” are also paired in Ps 10:7. They also appear in proximity in Pss 7:14 and 55:10. The oppressive and abusive actions of evil men are probably in view (see Job 4:8; 5:6; 15:35; Isa 10:1; 59:4).
notes.3289: (tn, Heb): “it passes quickly.” The subject of the verb is probably “their pride” (see the preceding line). The verb גּוּז (guz) means “to pass” here; it occurs only here and in Num 11:31.
notes.3290: (sn): We fly away. The psalmist compares life to a bird that quickly flies off (see Job 20:8).

rashi.heb:
*ימי שנותינו בהם שבעים שנה.* 
שנותינו אלה בעונותינו אלה ובעלומינו אלה שבעים שנה הם:
rashi.eng: *The days of our years because of them are seventy years.* The days of these years of ours, because of these iniquities of ours and because of these sins of our youth, are seventy years.

rashi.heb:
*ואם בגבורות.* 
ואם הרבה גברו ימיו שמונים שנה הם:
rashi.eng: *and if with increase.* And if his days are much increased, they are eighty years.

rashi.heb:
*ורהבם עמל ואון.* 
וכל הגדולה והשררה שיש לו לאדם בימים האלה אינם אלא עמל ואון ולמה שהרי כי גז חיש ונעופ' בתוך עברה מהר אנו עפים ומתים:
rashi.eng: *but their pride is toil and pain.* But all the greatness and the dominion that a person enjoys in these days are only toil and pain. Why? Because it passes quickly and we fly away. During its swift passing, we fly away and die.

rashi.heb:
*גז.* 
לשון העברה כמו נגוזו ועבר (נחום א׳:י״ב) ויגז שלוים מן הים (במדבר י״א:ל״א):
rashi.eng: *it passes.* Heb. גז, an expression of passing, as (Nahum 1:12): “they have crossed (נגוזו);” (Num. 11:31), “and drove (ויגז) quails up from the sea.”

notes.3291: (tn, Heb): “Who knows the strength of your anger?”
notes.3292: (tn, Heb): “and like your fear [is] your raging fury.” Perhaps one should emend וּכְיִרְאָתְךְ (ukhyir’otekh, “and like your fear”) to יִרְאָתְךְ (yir’otkh, “your fear”), understanding a virtual dittography (אַפֶּךָ וּכְיִרְאָתְךְ, ’apekha ukhyir’otekh) to have occurred. In this case the psalmist asserts “your fear [is] your raging fury,” that is, your raging fury is what causes others to fear you. The suffix on “fear” is understood as objective.

rashi.heb:
*מי יודע עז אפך.* 
בימים מועטים כאלה מי יקנה לו לב לדעת את עז אפך ליראה אותך ואתה כיראתך עברתך. כשם שאתה יראוי כן עברתך קשה ונפרע מן החוטאים:
rashi.eng: *Who knows the might of Your wrath.* In these few days, who can acquire intelligence to know the might of Your wrath and to fear You, and as for You, Your fear is Your anger. Just as You are feared, so is Your anger harsh, and You exact retribution from the sinners.

notes.3293: (tn, Heb): “to number our days,” that is, to be aware of how few they really are.
notes.3294: (tn, Heb): “and we will bring a heart of wisdom.” After the imperative of the preceding line, the prefixed verbal form with the conjunction indicates purpose/result. The Hebrew term “heart” here refers to the center of one’s thoughts, volition, and moral character.

rashi.heb:
*למנות ימינו כן הודע.* 
כאשר בתחלה הודע בעולם את מנין ימינו ארוכים וכיון שנאריך ימים נוכל לקנות לב ונביא בתוכם לבב חכמה, ונביא לשון הבאה, (וי"א למנות ימינו כן כמנין כ"ן שבעים שנה ונמות לפי שיעור ימינו שהן מעט כן תייסר אותנו וכן ויודע בהם אנשי סוכות) (שופטים ח׳:ט״ז) (סא"א):
rashi.eng: *So teach the number of our days.* And just as in the beginning, make known in the world the number of our long days, and since we enjoy longevity, we will be able to acquire intelligence, and we will acquire in them a heart of wisdom. The word נביא is an expression of bringing [rather than of a prophet. Cf. B.B. 12a, Targum ad. loc, Redak below]. (Some say: According to the number of our days כן, according to the numerical value of כן, seventy years. He says: According to the number of our years, which are few, so shall You chastise us, as [Jud. 8:16]: “and with them he chastised (ויודע) the men of Succoth.” This does not appear in all editions.)

notes.3296: (tn): Elsewhere the Niphal of נָחַם (nakham) + the preposition עַל (’al) + a personal object has the nuance “be comforted concerning [the personal object’s death]” (see 2 Sam 13:39; Jer 31:15). However, here the context seems to demand “feel sorrow for,” “have pity on.” In Deut 32:36 and Ps 135:14, where “servants” is also the object of the preposition, this idea is expressed with the Hitpael form of the verb.

rashi.heb:
*שובה ה'.* 
מחרון אפיך:
rashi.eng: *Return, O Lord.* from Your burning wrath.

rashi.heb:
*והנחם.* 
חשוב מחשבה טובה על עבדיך:
rashi.eng: *And repent.* Think well about Your servants.

notes.3297: (sn): Morning is used metaphorically for a time of renewed joy after affliction (see Pss 30:5; 46:5; 49:14; 59:16; 143:8).
notes.3298: (tn): After the imperative (see the preceding line) the cohortatives with the prefixed conjunction indicate purpose/result.

rashi.heb:
*שבענו בבקר חסדך.* 
ביום הגאולה והתשועה שהוא בקר לליל הצרה והאנחה והחשיכה:
rashi.eng: *Satiate us in the morning.* On the day of the redemption and the salvation, which is the morning of the night of the trouble, the sighing, and the darkness.

rashi.heb:
*ונרננה ונשמחה בכל ימינו.* 
כלומר בכל הצרו' שעברו עלינו בימינו אלה:
rashi.eng: *and let us sing praises and rejoice with all our days.* i.e., with all the troubles that passed over us in these days of ours.

rashi.heb:
*שמחנו כימות עניתנו.* 
שמחנו לימות משיחנו כמנין ימות שעניתנו בגליות וכמנין שנות אשר ראינו רעה:
rashi.eng: *Cause us to rejoice according to the days that You afflicted us.* Cause us to rejoice in the days of our Messiah according to the number of days that You afflicted us in the exiles and according to the number of years that we experienced evil.

notes.3300: (tn, Heb): “may your work be revealed to your servants.” In this context (note v. 17) the verb form יֵרָאֶה (yera’eh) is best understood as an unshortened jussive (see Gen 1:9; Isa 47:3).
notes.3301: (tn, Heb): “and your majesty to their sons.” The verb “be revealed” is understood by ellipsis in the second line.

notes.3302: (tn, Heb): “and may the delight of the Master, our God, be on us.” The Hebrew term נֹעַם (no’am, “delight”) is used in Ps 27:4 of the Lord’s “beauty,” but here it seems to refer to his favor (see BDB 653 s.v.) or kindness (HALOT 706 s.v.).
notes.3303: (tn, Heb): “and the work of our hands establish over us, and the work of our hands, establish it.”
notes.3304: (sn): Psalm 91. In this psalm an individual (perhaps a priest) addresses one who has sought shelter in the Lord and assures him that God will protect him from danger (vv. 1-13). In vv. 14-16 God himself promises to keep his loyal follower safe.

rashi.heb:
*ויהי נועם אד' אלהינו.* 
שכינתו ותנחומיו:
rashi.eng: *And may the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us.* His presence and His consolations.

rashi.heb:
*ומעשה ידינו כוננה עלינו.* 
לשון תחינה הוא, כוננה כמו שמרה שפטה:
rashi.eng: *and the work of our hands establish for us.* Heb. כוננה. This is an expression of supplication. כוֹננה is like שמרה, watch, שפטה, judge.

rashi.heb:
*כוננהו.* 
כונן אותו, ושני פעמים ומעשה ידינו כוננהו א' על מלאכת המשכן שבירכן לישראל והתפלל שתשרה שכינה במעשה ידיהם במשכן ואחת שתהא ברכה במעשה ידיהם:
rashi.eng: *establish it.* Establish it. The two times “and the work of our hands establish” [are mentioned are for the following purposes]: One is for the work of the Tabernacle, when he blessed Israel and prayed that the Shechinah should rest on the work of their hands in the Tabernacle, and one is that there should be a blessing in the work of their hands.

notes.3307: (sn): The Lord is compared here to a bird who protects its young under the shadow of its wings (see v. 4).
notes.3308: (sn): The divine name used here is “Shaddai” (שַׁדַּי, shadday; see also Ps 68:14). Shaddai (or El Shaddai) is the mighty king (sovereign judge) of the world who grants life/blesses and kills/judges. In Genesis he blesses the patriarchs with fertility and promises numerous descendants. Outside Genesis he both blesses/protects and takes away life/happiness.

rashi.heb:
*יושב בסתר עליון.* 
מי שהוא חוסה בסתר כנפי השכינה הוא יתלונן בצלו שהקב"ה מגין עליו הרי משה רבינו זה משיא את בני האדם לחסות בכנפי השכינה:
rashi.eng: *He who dwells in the covert of the Most High.* He who takes shelter in the covert of the wings of the Shechinah, he will lodge in His shadow, for the Holy One, blessed be He, protects him. Moses, our teacher, hereby persuades people to take shelter in the wings of the Shechinah.

rashi.heb:
*יושב בסתר עליון.* 
כמו (שה"ש ב) בצלו חמדתי וישבתי:
rashi.eng: *He who dwells in the covert of the Most High.* Is like (Song 2:3): “in His shadow I desired and sat.”

rashi.heb:
*שדי.* 
לשון חוזק:
rashi.eng: *the Almighty.* Heb. שדי, an expression of strength.

rashi.heb:
*אומר לה' מחסי.* 
הוא ומצודתי והכל ילמדו ממני ולמה אני אומר כן:
rashi.eng: *I shall say of the Lord [that He is] my shelter and my fortress.* and all will learn from me. Now why do I say this?

notes.3309: (tn): The word refers specifically to a fowler (or hunter of birds).

rashi.heb:
*כי הוא יצילך מפח יקוש וגו'.* 
לכל אחד ואחד הוא אומר יושב בסתר עליון:
rashi.eng: *For He will save you from the snare that traps, etc..* To everyone he says, “He who dwells in the covert of the Most High.”

notes.3310: (tn, Heb): “put a cover over you” (see Ps 5:11).
notes.3311: (tc): The Hebrew text has the singular, but the plural should be read. The final yod (י) of the suffix, which indicates the plural, has dropped off by haplography (note the yod [י] at the beginning of the next word).
notes.3312: (tn): Traditionally the Hebrew term סֹחֵרָה (sokherah), which occurs only here in the OT, has been understood to refer to a buckler or small shield (see BDB 695 s.v.). But HALOT 750 s.v., on the basis of evidence from the cognate languages, proposes the meaning “wall.”

rashi.heb:
*באברתו.* 
כנף:

*יסך.* 
יסוכך:
rashi.eng: *With His wing He will cover… you will take refuge.* You will be covered.

rashi.heb:
*תחסה.* 
תתכסה:

*צנה וסחרה.* 
הוא צנה המקפת את האדם קרוב לארבע רוחותיו, סוחרה לשון סחור סחור:
rashi.eng: *an encompassing shield.* Heb. צנה וסחרה. This is a shield that encompasses a man closely on his four sides. וסֹחֵרָה is an expression of סְחוֹר סְחוֹר, around.

notes.3313: (tn): This probably alludes to a sneak attack by enemies in the darkness of night (see Song 3:8).

rashi.heb:
*לא תירא.* 
אם תבטח בו:
rashi.eng: *You will not fear.* if you trust in Him.

rashi.heb:
*מחץ יעוף יומם.* 
שד המעופף כחץ:
rashi.eng: *the arrow that flies by day.* the demon that flies like an arrow.

notes.3314: (sn): As in Deut 32:23-24, vv. 5-6 closely associate military attack and deadly disease. Perhaps the latter alludes to one of the effects of siege warfare on the population of an entrapped city, which was especially vulnerable to the outbreak of epidemics.

rashi.heb:
*מדבר, ומקטב.* 
שמות שדים הם, זה מזיק בלילה וזה מזיק בצהרים:
rashi.eng: *Pestilence, etc., destruction.* These are names of demons; one destroys at night, and one destroys at noon.

rashi.heb:
*ישוד.* 
ישודד:
rashi.eng: *ravages.* Heb. יָשוּד, [equivalent to] יְשוֹדֵד.

notes.3315: (tn): Apparently the deadly disease mentioned in v. 6b is the understood subject here.

rashi.heb:
*יפול מצדך אלף.* 
לשון חנייה כמו (בראשית כ״ה:י״ח) על פני כל אחיו נפל:
rashi.eng: *A thousand will be stationed at your side.* Heb. יפל, an expression of encamping, as (Gen. 25:18): “before the face of all his brothers did he settle (נפל).”

rashi.heb:
*מצדך.* 
משמאלך יחנו אלף שדים ואליך לא יגשו להזיק:
rashi.eng: *at your side.* At your left a thousand demons will be stationed, and they will not approach you to harm [you].

rashi.heb:
*ושלמת.* 
כליון, ולמה:
rashi.eng: *and… the annihilation.* Heb. ושלמת, complete destruction. And why?

notes.3317: (tn, Heb): “for you, the Lord, my shelter, the Most High, you have made your dwelling place.”

rashi.heb:
*כי אתה.* 
אמרת ה' מחסי. והרי זה מקרא קצר:
rashi.eng: *For you.* You said, “The Lord is my refuge.” This is an elliptical verse.

rashi.heb:
*עליון שמת מעונך.* 
את הקב"ה שמת מעון מבטחך:
rashi.eng: *the Most High you made your dwelling.* You made the Holy One, blessed be He, the seat of your trust.

notes.3319: (tn): For this sense of the Hebrew term נגע see Ps 38:11.

rashi.heb:
*לא תאנה.* 
לא תקרה וכן והאלהי' אנה לידו (שמות כ״א:י״ג):
rashi.eng: *No… will befall.* Heb. לא תאנה, will not happen. Similarly, (Exod. 21:13): “and God allowed it to happen (אנה) to his hand.”

notes.3321: (tn, Heb): “for his angels he will command concerning you.”

notes.3323: (tn, Heb): “so your foot will not strike a stone.”

rashi.heb:
*פן תגוף.* 
פן תכשל וכן כל לשון נגיפה אצופי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *lest… stumble.* Heb. תגף, lest it [your foot] stumble, and so every expression of נְגִפָה, acupir, azoper, to hit, strike against.

notes.3326: (tn): The words “the Lord says” are supplied in the translation to clarify that the words which follow are the Lord’s oracle of assurance.
notes.3327: (tn, Heb): Or “make him secure” ( “set him on high”).
notes.3328: (tn, Heb): “because he knows my name” (see Ps 9:10).

notes.3330: (sn): Psalm 92. The psalmist praises God because he defeats the wicked and vindicates his loyal followers.

rashi.heb:
*מזמור שיר.* 
של לוים (נביאים):
rashi.eng: *A song with musical accompaniment.* of the Levites.

rashi.heb:
*ליום השבת.* 
שאומרי' אותו בשבתות והוא מדבר בענין העולם הבא שכולו שבת:
rashi.eng: *for the Sabbath day.* that they would recite on Sabbaths, and it deals with the world to come, which is entirely Sabbath.

notes.3333: (tn): The words “it is fitting” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. Verses 1-3 are actually one long sentence in the Hebrew text, but this has been divided up into two shorter sentences in the translation in keeping with contemporary English style.

rashi.heb:
*להגיד בבקר חסדך.* 
בעת הגאולה:
rashi.eng: *To declare in the morning Your kindness.* At the time of the Redemption.

rashi.heb:
*ואמונתך בלילות.* 
ובעוד צרת הגלות להאמין בך שתשמור הבטחתך כל זה נאה וטוב:
rashi.eng: *and Your faith at night.* And during the distress of the exile, to believe in You that You will keep Your promise, all this is splendid and good.

rashi.heb:
*עלי עשור ועלי נבל.* 
כנור של עשרה נימין:
rashi.eng: *Upon a ten-stringed harp and upon a psaltery.* Heb. עשור, a harp of ten strings.

notes.3335: (tn, Heb): “very deep [are] your thoughts.” God’s “thoughts” refer here to his moral design of the world, as outlined in vv. 6-15.

notes.3336: (tn, Heb): “the brutish man does not know, and the fool does not understand this.” The adjective בַּעַר (ba’ar, “brutish”) refers to spiritual insensitivity, not mere lack of intelligence or reasoning ability (see Pss 49:10; 73:22; Prov 12:1; 30:2, as well as the use of the related verb in Ps 94:8).

notes.3338: (tn, Heb): “in order that they might be destroyed permanently.” God allows the wicked to prosper temporarily so that he might reveal his justice. When the wicked are annihilated, God demonstrates that wickedness does not pay off.

rashi.heb:
*איש בער לא ידע.* 
את האמור למטה:
rashi.eng: *A boorish man does not know.* What is stated below.

rashi.heb:
*בפרח רשעים כמו עשב.* 
אינם יודעי' שהפרחת' אינה אלא להשמידם עדי עד שמשלם לשונאיו על פניהם להאבידם:
rashi.eng: *When the wicked flourish like grass.* they do not know that their flourishing is only to destroy them to eternity, for He recompenses His enemies to their face to destroy them.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה מרום.* 
בכל משפטיך ידך על העליונה שהכל מצדיקים עליהם את דינך:
rashi.eng: *But You remain on high.* In all Your judgments, You have the upper hand, for all justify Your judgments.

notes.3342: (sn): The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “to exalt/lift up the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 75:10; 89:24; Lam 2:17).
notes.3343: (tn): The Hebrew verb בָּלַל (balal) usually has the nuance “to mix.” Here it seems to mean “to smear” or “to anoint.” Some emend the form to בַּלֹּתַנִי (ballotaniy; a second person form of the verb with a first person suffix) and read, “you anoint me.”

notes.3344: (tn, Heb): “my eye gazes upon those who watch me [with evil intent].” See also Pss 5:8; 27:11; 56:2. The form שׁוּרָי (shuray) should be emended to שׁוֹרְרָי (shor�ray).
notes.3345: (tn, Heb): “those who rise up against me, evil [foes], my ears hear.”

rashi.heb:
*בלותי בשמן רענן.* 
לבלותי בשמן של שררה בלותי כמו (במדבר טו) בלול בשמן:
rashi.eng: *to soak me with fresh oil.* Heb. בלתי. To soak me with the oil of dominion. בַלֹתִי is like (Num. 15:9): “mingled (בלולה) with oil.”

notes.3346: (tn): The singular is used in a representative sense, with the typical godly person being in view.
notes.3347: (sn): The cedars of the Lebanon forest were well-known in ancient Israel for their immense size.

rashi.heb:
*בשורי.* 
בעוייני כמו בשוררי:
rashi.eng: *upon those who stare at me.* Heb. בשורי, at those who stare at me, as (5:9): “those who lie in wait for me (בשוררי).”

rashi.heb:
*בקמים עלי מרעים.* 
על הרשעים הקמים עלי שמעו אזני מאחורי הפרגוד שלא יועילו לכלות אותנו, כך שמעתי:
rashi.eng: *when evildoers rise up against me.* About the wicked who rise up against me, my ears heard from behind the “veil” that they will not succeed in destroying us [perhaps, David and his men]. So I heard.

rashi.heb:
*צדיק כתמר יפרח וגו'.* 
כתמר לעשות פירות וכארז בלבנון להחליף גזעו:
rashi.eng: *The righteous one flourishes like the palm, etc..* Like the palm that produces fruit, and like the cedar insofar as its trunk renews itself.

rashi.heb:
*שתולים.* 
יהיו הצדיקים בבית ה':
rashi.eng: *Planted.* The righteous will be [planted] in the house of the Lord.

notes.3349: (tn, Heb): “so that [they] proclaim that upright [is] the Lord, my rocky summit, and there is no injustice in him.”
notes.3350: (sn): Psalm 93. The psalmist affirms that the Lord is the king of the universe who preserves order and suppresses the destructive forces in the world.

rashi.heb:
*ינובון.* 
יצמחון:
rashi.eng: *will… grow.* Heb. ישגה, will grow.

rashi.heb:
*דשנים.* 
שמנים ורעננים יהיו ואז יגידו כי ישר ה':
rashi.eng: *fat.* Heb. דשנים, They will be fat and fresh, and then they will declare that the Lord is upright.

notes.3351: (sn): Strength is compared here to a belt that one wears for support. The Lord’s power undergirds his rule.

rashi.heb:
*ה' מלך.* 
יאמרו לעתיד:
rashi.eng: *The Lord has reigned.* They will say in the future.

rashi.heb:
*אף תכון תבל.* 
במלכו תשמח הארץ:
rashi.eng: *The world also is established.* When He reigns, the earth will rejoice.

notes.3352: (tn, Heb): “from antiquity [are] you.” As the context suggests, this refers specifically to God’s royal position, not his personal existence.

notes.3353: (tn): The Hebrew noun translated “waves” often refers to rivers or streams, but here it appears to refer to the surging waves of the sea (see v. 4, Ps 24:2).
notes.3354: (tn, Heb): “the waves lift up, O Lord, the waves lift up their voice, the waves lift up their crashing.”

rashi.heb:
*נשאו נהרות ה'.* 
לשון צעקה וקובלן הוא זה אהה ה' הנה האומו' השוטפים כנהרו' נשאו קולם יהמיון ואת דוך עמקי נבכיהם ישאו ויגביהו תמיד להתגאות נגדך, כל לשון דכא לשון עומק ושפלות:
rashi.eng: *The rivers have raised, O Lord.* This is an expression of a cry and a plaint: Woe, O Lord, behold! Your enemies, who flood like rivers, have raised their voice and roar, and the lowness of the depths of their locks they will raise and lift on high constantly to be haughty against You. Every expression of דכא is an expression of depth and lowness.

notes.3355: (tn, Heb): “mighty waters.” The surging waters here symbolizes the hostile enemies of God who seek to destroy the order he has established in the world (see Pss 18:17; 29:3; 32:6; 77:20; 144:7; Isa 17:13; Jer 51:55; Ezek 26:19; Hab 3:15). But the Lord is depicted as elevated above and sovereign over these raging waters.

rashi.heb:
*מקלות מים רבים וגו'.* 
ידעתי אני כי יותר מקולות המים הרבים אשר יהמיון עלינו ומאדירי משברי הים הזה אתה אדיר במרום ה' וידך תקיפה עליהם:
rashi.eng: *More than the voices of great waters, etc..* I know that more than the voices of great waters, which roar over us, and more than the mightiest breakers of this sea, You are mighty, O Lord, and Your hand is powerful over them.

notes.3357: (tn): Traditionally “your testimonies.” The Hebrew noun עֵדוּת (’edut) refers here to the demands of God’s covenant law. See Ps 19:7.
notes.3358: (sn): The rules you set down. God’s covenant contains a clear, reliable witness to his moral character and demands.
notes.3359: (sn): Holiness refers here to God’s royal transcendence (see vv. 1-4), as well as his moral authority and perfection (see v. 5a).
notes.3360: (tn, Heb): “for your house holiness is fitting, O Lord, for length of days.”
notes.3361: (sn): Psalm 94. The psalmist asks God to judge the wicked and affirms his confidence in God’s justice.

rashi.heb:
*עדתיך.* 
שהעידו והבטיחו נביאך לביתך שהוא נאוה קודש:
rashi.eng: *Your testimonies.* which Your prophets prophesied and promised concerning Your house, which is the dwelling of holiness.

rashi.heb:
*נאמנו מאד לביתך.* 
ולאורך ימים הוא מצפה להם ואע"פ שארכו הימים נאמנים הם לה' מאד:
rashi.eng: *are very faithful to Your house.* and to the length of days He looks forward to them, and although it has been a long time, they are very faithful to God.

rashi.heb:
*נאוה.* 
כמו (לעיל טו) נאות אלהים לשון נאוה ותדע שכל נוה שבמקרא אינן מפקין אל"ף לפי שהם לשון נוי וזה מפיק אל"ף:
rashi.eng: *dwelling.* Heb. נאוה, like (83:13): “the dwellings נְאוֹת of God,” an expression of נָוֶה. You should know [that this is so] because no instance of נָאוָה has a pronounced “aleph,” for they are an expression of נוֹי beauty, but this one has an “aleph” which is pronounced.

rashi.heb:
*הופיע.* 
הראה וגלה לנו את נקמתך:
rashi.eng: *show.* Heb. הופיע, show and reveal to us Your vengeance.

notes.3365: (tn): The Hitpael of אָמַר (’amar) occurs only here (and perhaps in Isa 61:6).

rashi.heb:
*יתאמרו.* 
ישתבחו כמו (דברים כו) האמרת והאמירך:
rashi.eng: *boast.* Heb. יתאמרו. They praise themselves, as (Deut. 26:17): “you praised (האמרת),” and “praised you (האמירך).”

notes.3367: (tn): The Hebrew noun יָתוֹם (yatom) refers to one who has lost his father (not necessarily his mother, see Ps 109:9). Because they were so vulnerable and were frequently exploited, fatherless children are often mentioned as epitomizing the oppressed (see Pss 10:14; 68:5; 82:3; 146:9; as well as Job 6:27; 22:9; 24:3, 9; 29:12; 31:17, 21).

notes.3369: (tn, Heb): “understand.” The verb used in v. 7 is repeated here for rhetorical effect. The people referred to here claim God is ignorant of their actions, but the psalmist corrects their faulty viewpoint.

rashi.heb:
*בינו בוערים בעם.* 
קצת שוטים שבעולם:
rashi.eng: *Understand, [you] most boorish of the people.* the most foolish peoples in the world.

notes.3371: (tn, Heb): “The one who plants an ear, does he not hear? The one who forms an eye, does he not see?”

rashi.heb:
*הנוטע אזן.* 
שמא הקב"ה שנטע אוזן לא ישמע צעקת עמו ועניו:
rashi.eng: *Will He Who implants the ear.* Is it possible that the Holy One, blessed be He, Who implanted the ear, should not hear the cry of His people and their affliction?

rashi.heb:
*הלא יוכיח.* 
ייסר אתכם על כך:
rashi.eng: *will He… not reprove.* and chastise you for that?

notes.3372: (tn, Heb): “the Lord knows the thoughts of man, that they are emptiness.” The psalmist thinks specifically of the “thoughts” expressed in v. 7.

rashi.heb:
*ה' יודע.* 
מחשבותיכם שאתם סבורין להתגאות בנזר המלוכה ותדעו כי הבל הם:
rashi.eng: *The Lord knows.* your thoughts, that you are thinking to be haughty with the crown of the kingdom, and you should know that they [your thoughts] are vanity.

notes.3373: (tn, Heb): “[Oh] the happiness [of] the man.” Hebrew wisdom literature often assumes and reflects the male-oriented perspective of ancient Israelite society. The principle of the psalm is certainly applicable to all people, regardless of their gender or age. To facilitate modern application, we translate the gender and age specific “man” with the more neutral “one.” The generic masculine pronoun is used in v. 2.

rashi.heb:
*אשרי הגבר.* 
אשריהם הצדיקי' המעוני' תחת ידיכם ובלבד שיהו עוסקין בתורה ובמצות:
rashi.eng: *Fortunate is the man.* Fortunate are the righteous who are afflicted under Your hands, provided that they engage in Torah and mitzvoth.

notes.3374: (tn, Heb): “to give him rest from the days of trouble.”
notes.3375: (tn, Heb): “until a pit is dug for the wicked.”

rashi.heb:
*להשקיט לו מימי רע.* 
כי היסורין גורמין לו להשקיט להם מימי דין גיהנם:
rashi.eng: *To grant him peace from days of evil.* For the chastisements cause him to have peace from the days of the judgment of Gehinnom.

rashi.heb:
*עד.* 
שיראה שיכרה לרשע שחת:
rashi.eng: *while.* he sees that a pit is dug for the wicked man.

notes.3378: (tn, Heb): “for judgment will return to justice.”
notes.3379: (tn, Heb): “all the pure of heart.” The “heart” is here viewed as the seat of one’s moral character and motives. The “pure of heart” are God’s faithful followers who trust in and love the Lord and, as a result, experience his deliverance (see Pss 7:10; 11:2; 32:11; 36:10; 64:10; 97:11).
notes.3380: (tn, Heb): “and after it [are] the pure of heart.”

rashi.heb:
*כי עד צדק ישוב משפט.* 
היסורין שלהם עד שיצדקו בשבילם ואחר המשפט כל ישרי לב יתקבצו כי יטלו שכרם:
rashi.eng: *For until righteousness will judgment return.* [i. e., the judgment of] their chastisements [will persist] until they become righteous because of them. And after the judgment, all those upright in heart will gather, for they will receive their reward.

notes.3382: (sn): Who will stand up for me…? The questions anticipate the answer, “No one except God” (see v. 17).

rashi.heb:
*מי יקום לי.* 
זכות מי יעמד לנו בין המריעים הללו:
rashi.eng: *Who will rise up for me.* Whose merit will stand up for us among these evildoers?

notes.3383: (tn, Heb): “If the Lord [were] not my help, quickly my life would have lain down in silence.” The psalmist, perhaps speaking as the nation’s representative, recalls God’s past intervention. For other examples of conditional sentences with the term לוּלֵי (luley, “if not”) in the protasis and a perfect verbal form in the apodosis, see Pss 119:92 and 124:2-5.

rashi.heb:
*דומה.* 
דומיה:
rashi.eng: *Silent.* silence.

notes.3384: (tn, Heb): “when my worries are many within me.”
notes.3385: (tn, Heb): “your comforts cause my soul to delight.”

notes.3386: (tn, Heb): “a throne of destruction.” “Throne” stands here by metonymy for rulers who occupy thrones.
notes.3387: (tn, Heb): “Is a throne of destruction united to you, one that forms trouble upon a statute?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “Of course not!” The translation, while not preserving the interrogative form of the statement, reflects its rhetorical force.

rashi.heb:
*היחברך כסא הוות.* 
היוכל להדמות לך האומות היוצרים צלמים ומסכות של עמל:
rashi.eng: *Will the throne of evil join You.* Will it be able to compare to You?

rashi.heb:
*עלי חק.* 
בשביל חק להיותו חק להם עבודתם:
rashi.eng: *for a statute.* for the sake of a statue, to be for them as the statute of their worship.

notes.3390: (tn, Heb): “and the blood of the innocent they declare guilty.”

rashi.heb:
*יגודו.* 
יאספו גדודים על נפש צדיק להרוג:
rashi.eng: *They gather.* Troops gather upon a Jewish soul to kill [him].

rashi.heb:
*ירשיעו.* 
יחייבו בדין להורגו:
rashi.eng: *and condemn.* Heb. ירשיעו. They condemn in judgment to kill him.

notes.3391: (tn, Heb): “and the Lord has become my elevated place.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive is used in a rhetorical sense, describing an anticipated development as if it were already reality.
notes.3392: (tn, Heb): “and my God [has become] a rocky summit of my safety.”

notes.3393: (tn): The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive is used in a rhetorical sense, describing an anticipated development as if it were already reality.
notes.3395: (sn): Psalm 95. The psalmist summons Israel to praise God as the creator of the world and the nation’s protector, but he also reminds the people not to rebel against God.

rashi.heb:
*אונם.* 
אונסם כמו (איוב כ״א:י״ט) יצפון לבניו אונו:
rashi.eng: *their violence.* Heb. אונם, their violence, as (Job 21:19): “Should God lay away his violence (אונו) for his sons?”

notes.3396: (tn, Heb): “to the rocky summit of our deliverance.”

notes.3400: (tn): The phrase “in his hand” means within the sphere of his authority.

rashi.heb:
*ותועפות.* 
לשון גובה כעוף המעופף:
rashi.eng: *and the heights.* An expression of height, like a bird that flies [up high].

rashi.heb:
*נברכה.* 
לשון ויברך את הגמלים (בראשית כד):
rashi.eng: *let us kneel.* Heb. נברכה, an expression of (Gen. 24:11): “He made the camels kneel (ויברך).”

notes.3403: (tn, Heb): “if only you would listen to his voice.” The Hebrew particle אִם (’im, “if”) and following prefixed verbal form here express a wish (cf. Ps 81:8). Note that the apodosis (the “then” clause of the conditional sentence) is suppressed.

rashi.heb:
*היום.* 
בעולם הזה אם בקולו תשמעו:
rashi.eng: *today.* In this world.

notes.3404: (tn): The words “he says” are supplied in the translation to clarify that the following words are spoken by the Lord (see vv. 9-11).
notes.3405: (sn): The name Meribah means “strife.” Two separate but similar incidents at Meribah are recorded in the Pentateuch (Exod 17:1-7; Num 20:1-13, see also Pss 81:7; 106:32). In both cases the Israelites complained about lack of water and the Lord miraculously provided for them.
notes.3406: (sn): The name Massah means “testing.” This was another name (along with Meribah) given to the place where Israel complained following the Red Sea Crossing (see Exod 17:1-7, as well as Deut 6:16; 9:22; 33:8).
notes.3407: (tn, Heb): “do not harden your heart[s] as [at] Meribah, as [in] the day of Massah in the wilderness.”

rashi.heb:
*בחנוני.* 
חנם:
rashi.eng: *tested Me.* for nothing.

rashi.heb:
*גם ראו פעלי.* 
במצרים:
rashi.eng: *even though they had seen My work.* in Egypt.

notes.3409: (tn): The prefixed verbal form is either a preterite or an imperfect. If the latter, it emphasizes the ongoing nature of the condition in the past. The translation reflects this interpretation of the verbal form.
notes.3410: (tn, Heb): “a people, wanderers of heart [are] they.”
notes.3411: (tn, Heb): “and they do not know my ways.” In this context the Lord’s “ways” are his commands, viewed as a pathway from which his people, likened to wayward sheep (see v. 7), wander.

rashi.heb:
*ארבעים שנה.* 
קטתי בהם, רבתי עמהם לשון נקטה נפשי בחיי (איוב י׳:א׳) נלחמתי בם ארבעים שנה להמיתם במדבר כי אמרתי תועי לבב הם:
rashi.eng: *Forty years.* I quarreled with them and contended with them. [אקוט is] an expression of (Job 10:1): “My soul quarrels (נקטה) with my life.” I strove with them for forty years to kill them in the desert, because I said, “They are of erring heart.”

notes.3412: (tn, Heb): “my resting place.” The promised land of Canaan is here viewed metaphorically as a place of rest for God’s people, who are compared to sheep (see v. 7).
notes.3413: (sn): Psalm 96. The psalmist summons everyone to praise the Lord, the sovereign creator of the world who preserves and promotes justice in the earth.

rashi.heb:
*אל מנוחתי.* 
לארץ ישראל ולירושלים אשר קראתים מנוחה שנאמר (לקמן קלב) זאת מנוחתי עדי עד:
rashi.eng: *My resting place.* [In] to the land of Israel and Jerusalem, which I called “resting place,” as it says (below 132:14): “This is my resting place forever.”

notes.3414: (sn): A new song is appropriate because the Lord is constantly intervening in the world as its just king. See also Pss 33:3; 40:3; 98:1.

rashi.heb:
*שיר חדש.* 
מזמור זה על העתיד וסופו מוכיח כי בא לשפוט את הארץ, בכל מקום שיר חדש על העתיד:
rashi.eng: *a new song.* This song deals with the future, as is proven by the final verse, “for He has come to judge the earth.” Any reference to a “new song” deals with the future.

notes.3415: (tn, Heb): “announce from day to day his deliverance.”

notes.3416: (tn): The verb “tell” is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).

notes.3417: (tn): Or perhaps “and feared by all gods.” See Ps 89:7.

notes.3418: (tn): The Hebrew term אֱלִילִים (’elilim, “worthless”) sounds like אֱלֹהִים (’elohim, “gods”). The sound play draws attention to the statement.

notes.3420: (tn, Heb): “strength and beauty [are] in his sanctuary.”

rashi.heb:
*הבו לה' משפחות עמים.* 
ומה תתנו לו הבו לה' כבוד ועוז:
rashi.eng: *Ascribe to the Lord, families of peoples.* And what shall you ascribe to Him? Ascribe to the Lord glory and might.

rashi.heb:
*ה' מלך.* 
לעתיד לבא יהא שיר זה:
rashi.eng: *“The Lord has reigned”.* This song will be [sung] in the future.

rashi.heb:
*ידין עמים במישרים.* 
אותם שיהפוך להם שפה ברורה:
rashi.eng: *He will judge peoples with equity.* Those whom he will turn into a clear tongue (Zeph. 3:9).

rashi.heb:
*במישרים.* 
זכיות:
rashi.eng: *with equity.* with merits.

rashi.heb:
*ירעם הים.* 
להרים קול בתהלה:
rashi.eng: *the sea… will roar.* to raise its voice in praise.

rashi.heb:
*כל עצי יער.* 
כל שלטוני האומות:
rashi.eng: *all the forest trees.* All the rulers of the nations.

notes.3423: (tn): The verbal forms in v. 13 probably describe God’s typical, characteristic behavior, though they may depict in dramatic fashion the outworking of divine judgment or anticipate a future judgment of worldwide proportions, in which case they could be translated “will judge the world.”
notes.3424: (tn, Heb): “and the nations with his integrity.”
notes.3425: (sn): Psalm 97. The psalmist depicts the Lord as the sovereign, just king of the world who comes in power to vindicate his people.

rashi.heb:
*ה' מלך.* 
בנטלו המלוכה מעמלק ומזרעו:
rashi.eng: *The Lord has reigned.* when He takes the kingdom from Amalek and from his descendants.

rashi.heb:
*תגל הארץ.* 
זהו שאמר (יחזקאל ל״ה:י״ד) כשמוח כל הארץ שממה אעשה לך, על עמלק נתנבא כן:
rashi.eng: *the earth will exult.* This is what Ezekiel said (35:14): “When the whole earth rejoices, I shall make you desolate.” He prophesied this concerning Amalek.

notes.3426: (sn): The Lord’s throne symbolizes his kingship.

rashi.heb:
*אש לפניו תלך.* 
במלחמת גוג ומגוג דכתיב במלחמתו (שם לח) ונשפטתי אתו בדבר ובדם וגשם שוטף ואבני אלגביש אש וגפרית:
rashi.eng: *Fire will go before Him.* in the war of Gog and Magog, for it is written concerning his war (Ezek. 38:22): “And I shall plead against him with pestilence and with blood, and rain bringing floods and great hailstones, fire and brimstone.”

rashi.heb:
*ברקיו.* 
זהרוריו, לשון למען היה לה ברק מורטה (יחזקאל כ״א:ט״ו):
rashi.eng: *His lightnings.* His brilliant lights, an expression of (Ezek. 21:15): “It is polished that it may glitter (ברק).”

rashi.heb:
*ותחל.* 
ביום ההוא יהיה רעש גדול על אדמת ישראל ורעשו מפניו דגי הים ותחל לשון חיל כיולדה (מיכה ד):
rashi.eng: *and quaked.* “Surely there will be a great earthquake on that day in the land of Israel. And at My presence, the fishes of the sea… will quake.” [The word] וַתָּחֵל is an expression of (above 48:7): “pangs (חיל) like [those of] a woman in confinement.”

rashi.heb:
*כדונג נמסו.* 
דכתיב ונהרסו ההרים ונפלו המדרגות:
rashi.eng: *melted like wax.* Heb. כדונג, as it is written (Ezek. 38:20): “and the mountains will be thrown down, and the cliffs will fall.”

rashi.heb:
*כדונג.* 
כשעוה:
rashi.eng: *wax.* Like wax.

notes.3428: (tn): The translation assumes that the prefixed verbal form in the first line is an imperfect (“are ashamed”) and that the ambiguous form in the third line is a perfect (“bow down”) because the psalmist appears to be describing the effect of the Lord’s mighty theophany on those who witness it (see vv. 5, 8). Another option is to take the prefixed form in the first line as a jussive (“let all who worship idols be ashamed”) and the ambiguous form in the third line as an imperative (“All you gods, bow down before him!”; cf. NIV).

rashi.heb:
*יבשו כל עובדי פסל.* 
דכתיב (ישעיהו ב׳:י״ח) והאלילים כליל יחלוף:
rashi.eng: *All worshippers of graven images will be ashamed.* as it is written (Isa. 2:18): “And the idols will completely pass away.”

rashi.heb:
*המתהללים.* 
המתפארים לע"ג:
rashi.eng: *who boast.* Who praise themselves with their worship.

notes.3429: (tn, Heb): “daughters.” The term “daughters” refers to the cities of Judah surrounding Zion (see Ps 48:11 and H. Haag, TDOT 2:336).

rashi.heb:
*משפטיך.* 
נקמתך:
rashi.eng: *Your judgments.* Your vengeance.

notes.3431: (tn): The participle may be verbal, though it might also be understood as substantival and appositional to “the Lord.” In this case one could translate, “Hate evil, you who love the Lord, the one who protects the lives…and delivers them.”

notes.3433: (tn, Heb): “Light is planted for the godly, and for the upright of heart joy.” The translation assumes an emendation of זָרַע (zara’, “planted”) to זָרַח (zara’, “shines”) which collocates more naturally with “light.” “Light” here symbolizes the joy (note the following line) that accompanies deliverance and the outpouring of divine favor.

rashi.heb:
*אור זרוע לצדיק.* 
זריעה ממש מוכנת לצמוח להם:
rashi.eng: *A light is sown for the righteous.* A real sowing is prepared to grow for them.

notes.3434: (tn, Heb): “to his holy remembrance.” The Hebrew noun זָכַר (zakhar, “remembrance”) here refers to the name of the Lord as invoked in liturgy and praise. Cf. Pss 6:5; 30:4. The Lord’s “name” is “holy” in the sense that it is a reminder of his uniqueness and greatness.
notes.3435: (sn): Psalm 98. The psalmist summons the whole earth to praise God because he reveals his justice and delivers Israel.

notes.3436: (sn): A new song is appropriate because the Lord is constantly intervening in the world as its just king. See Ps 96:1.
notes.3437: (tn): The perfect verbal forms in vv. 1-3 are understood here as describing characteristic divine activities. Another option is to translate them as present perfects, “has performed…has accomplished deliverance, etc.” referring to completed actions that have continuing results.
notes.3438: (tn, Heb): “his right hand delivers for him and his holy arm.” The right hand and arm symbolize his power as a warrior-king (see Isa 52:10). His arm is “holy” in the sense that it is in a category of its own; God’s power is incomparable.

rashi.heb:
*שירו לה'.* 
כל אלה לעתיד:
rashi.eng: *Sing to the Lord.* All these are for the future.

notes.3440: (tn, Heb): “he remembers his loyal love and his faithfulness to the house of Israel.”
notes.3441: (tn, Heb): “the deliverance of our God,” with “God” being a subjective genitive (= God delivers).

rashi.heb:
*נהרות ימחאו כף.* 
הנביאים דברו בלשון שהאוזן שומעת לא שיהא לנהרות כף אלא לשון שמחה וחדוה:
rashi.eng: *Rivers will clap hands.* The prophets spoke in a language that the ear can hear; not that the rivers have a hand, but it is an expression of joy and gladness.

notes.3442: (tn): The verbal forms in v. 9 probably describe God’s typical, characteristic behavior, though they may depict in dramatic fashion the outworking of divine judgment or anticipate a future judgment of worldwide proportions (“will judge…”).
notes.3443: (sn): Psalm 99. The psalmist celebrates the Lord’s just rule and recalls how he revealed himself to Israel’s leaders.

notes.3444: (tn): The prefixed verbal forms in v. 1 are understood here as indicating the nations’ characteristic response to the reality of the Lord’s kingship. Another option is to take them as jussives: “let the nations tremble…let the earth shake!”
notes.3445: (sn, Heb): Winged angels ( “cherubs”). Cherubs, as depicted in the OT, possess both human and animal (lion, ox, and eagle) characteristics (see Ezek 1:10; 10:14, 21; 41:18). They are pictured as winged creatures (Exod 25:20; 37:9; 1 Kgs 6:24-27; Ezek 10:8, 19) and serve as the very throne of God when the ark of the covenant is in view (Ps 99:1; see Num 7:89; 1 Sam 4:4; 2 Sam 6:2; 2 Kgs 19:15). The picture of the Lord seated on the cherubs suggests they might be used by him as a vehicle, a function they carry out in Ezek 1:22-28 (the “living creatures” mentioned here are identified as cherubs in Ezek 10:20). In Ps 18:10 the image of a cherub serves to personify the wind.
notes.3446: (tn): The Hebrew verb נוּט (nut) occurs only here in the OT, but the meaning can be determined on the basis of the parallelism with רָגַז (ragaz, “tremble”) and evidence from the cognate languages (see H. R. Cohen, Biblical Hapax Legomena [SBLDS], 121).

rashi.heb:
*ירגזו עמים.* 
מדבר במלחמת גוג ומגוג, ואז ירגזו עמים כענין שנאמר (זכריה י״ד:י״ב) וזאת תהיה המגפה וגו':
rashi.eng: *nations will quake.* [This] deals with the war of Gog and Magog. Then the nations will quake, as the matter that is said (Zech. 14:12): “And this shall be the plague, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*תנוט.* 
לשון נטיו רגלי:
rashi.eng: *will falter.* Heb. תנוט, an expression of (73:2): “my feet faltered (נטוי).”

notes.3448: (tn): The pronoun refers to the Lord himself (see vv. 5, 9).

rashi.heb:
*יודו שמך.* 
יודו את עז מלך האוהב משפט:
rashi.eng: *They will acknowledge Your name.* They will acknowledge the might of the King Who loves judgment.

notes.3449: (tn, Heb): “and strength, a king, justice he loves.” The syntax of the Hebrew text is difficult here. The translation assumes that two affirmations are made about the king, the Lord (see v. 1, and Ps 98:6). The noun עֹז (’oz, “strength”) should probably be revocalized as the adjective עַז (’az, “strong”).

rashi.heb:
*ועז מלך.* 
מוסב על מקרא העליון:
rashi.eng: *and the might of the King Who loves judgment.* This refers back to the preceding verse.

rashi.heb:
*אתה כוננת מישרים.* 
פשרה ושימת שלום בין אנשים כוננת באמרך (שמות כ״ג:ד׳) כי תראה חמור שונאך רובץ וגו', כי תפגע שור אויבך ומי הוא שיראה את שונאו גומל לו חסד שלא ידבנו לבו לחבקו ולנשקו, תנחומא:
rashi.eng: *You founded equity.* You founded compromise and peacemaking between persons, by Your statement (Exod. 23:5): “Should you see your enemy’s donkey lying etc.;” (ibid. verse 4), “Should you come upon Your enemy’s ox, etc.” Now who is it who sees his enemy being kind to him, whose heart will not be inspired to embrace him and kiss him? (Tanchuma).

notes.3453: (tn, Heb): “among those who called on his name.”
notes.3454: (tn, Heb): “those who.” The participle is in apposition to the phrase “those who called on his name” in the preceding line.

notes.3455: (sn): A pillar of cloud. The psalmist refers to the reality described in Exod 33:9-10; Num 12:5; and Deut 31:15.

rashi.heb:
*בעמוד ענן ידבר אליהם.* 
אף עם שמואל וזה הוא שנאמר (שמואל א ט׳:י״א-י״ב) היש בזה הרואה ותעננה אותם ותאמרנה יש, ראו הענן קשור על פתחו, כד"א ויש אשר יהיה הענן (במדבר י׳:י״א):
rashi.eng: *In a pillar of cloud He would speak to them.* Even with Samuel. This is what is stated (I Sam. 9:11f.): “and they said to them, Is the seer here? And they answered them and said, He is (יֵש).” You will see a cloud attached to his doorway, as Scripture says (Num. 9:20): “And sometimes the cloud would be…”

rashi.heb:
*שמרו עדתיו וחק נתן למו.* 
וחוק אשר נתן למו:
rashi.eng: *they kept His testimonies and the statute He gave them.* The statute that He gave them.

notes.3456: (tn, Heb): “a God of lifting up [i.e., forgiveness] you were to them, and an avenger concerning their deeds.” The present translation reflects the traditional interpretation, which understands the last line as qualifying the preceding one. God forgave Moses and Aaron, but he also disciplined them when they sinned (cf. NIV, NRSV). Another option is to take “their deeds” as referring to harmful deeds directed against Moses and Aaron. In this case the verse may be translated, “and one who avenged attacks against them.” Still another option is to emend the participial form נֹקֵם (noqem, “an avenger”) to נֹקָם (noqam), a rare Qal participial form of נָקַה (naqah, “purify”) with a suffixed pronoun. In this case one could translate, “and one who purified them from their [sinful] deeds” (cf. NEB “and held them innocent”).

rashi.heb:
*אל נושא.* 
עון ישראל:
rashi.eng: *a forgiving God.* [Forgiving] the iniquity of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*היית להם.* 
בשבילם:
rashi.eng: *for them.* Heb. להם, for their sake.

rashi.heb:
*ונוקם.* 
היית על עלילותם, משה ואהרן (שם כ) שמעו נא המורים, שמואל על שלא הדריך בניו בדרך טובה מת בחור:
rashi.eng: *but vengeful.* You were vengeful for their misdeeds: Moses and Aaron for “Hear now, you rebels!” As for Samuel, because he did not direct his sons in the good way, he died young.

notes.3458: (sn): Psalm 100. The psalmist celebrates the fact that Israel has a special relationship to God and summons worshipers to praise the Lord for his faithfulness.

rashi.heb:
*כי קדוש ה' אלהינו.* 
על אשר הוא מדקדק עם הצדיקים הוא מקודש בעולם, וכן הוא אומר (שמות כ״ט:מ״ג) ונקדש בכבודי, במכובדי:
rashi.eng: *for the Lord our God is holy.* because He is strict with the righteous, He is sanctified in the world, and so He says (Exod. 29:43): “and it will be sanctified with My glory,” meaning “with those glorified by Me.”

rashi.heb:
*מזמור לתודה.* 
להודיה לאומרו על זבחי תודה:
rashi.eng: *A song for a thanksgiving offering.* For thanksgiving, to recite it over thanksgiving offerings.

rashi.heb:
*עבדו את ה' בשמחה.* 
וכל כך למה דעו כי ה' הוא האלהים כשמשלם שכר פעולתכם אבל עובדי ע"ג אין להם לעבוד בשמחה שאין משלמין שכר:
rashi.eng: *Serve the Lord with joy.* Now why so much? You should know the Lord is God, Who recompenses you with reward for your work, but the heathens need not worship with joy because their deities do not give them any reward.

notes.3460: (tn): The present translation (like most modern translations) follows the Qere (marginal reading), which reads literally, “and to him [are] we.” The Kethib (consonantal text) has “and not we.” The suffixed preposition לו (“to him”) was confused aurally with the negative particle לא because the two sound identical.

rashi.heb:
*הוא עשנו ולא.* 
כשלא היינו בעולם:
rashi.eng: *He made us and we are His.* When we were not in the world.

rashi.heb:
*בתודה.* 
בהודייה:

notes.3462: (tn, Heb): “and to a generation and a generation [is] his faithfulness.”
notes.3463: (sn): Psalm 101. The psalmist, who appears to be a king, promises to promote justice in his land and vows to rid his royal court of evildoers.

rashi.heb:
*ועד דר ודר.* 
קיימת אמונתו כל לשון אמת ואמונה אמונת הבטחה שמאמין ומבטיח הבטחתו:
rashi.eng: *and until generation after generation.* His faith will endure. Every expression of truth (אמת) and faith (אמונה) means the realization of a promise, that He makes true and assures His promise.

rashi.heb:
*חסד ומשפט אשירה.* 
כשאתה עושה עמי חסד אקלסך ברוך הטוב והמטיב וכשאתה עושה בי משפט אני אשיר ברוך דיין האמת בין כך ובין כך לך ה' אזמרה:
rashi.eng: *I shall sing of kindness and judgment.* when You bestow kindness upon me, I will praise you [with the blessing:] “Blessed be He Who is good and does good,” and when You perform judgment upon me, I will sing, “Blessed be the true Judge.” In either case, to You, O Lord, I shall sing.

notes.3465: (tn, Heb): “I will walk about in the integrity of my heart in the midst of my house.”

rashi.heb:
*אשכילה.* 
אתן לב על דרך התמים:
rashi.eng: *I shall concern myself.* I shall direct my thoughts to the way of integrity.

rashi.heb:
*מתי תבא אלי.* 
הדרך הישרה להתהלך בה ואתהלך בתם לבבי אף בקרב ביתי בהצנע כמו בפרהסיא:
rashi.eng: *When will it come to me.* The straight path, to walk upon it, and I shall walk with the integrity of my heart even within my house, in private as well as in public.

notes.3466: (tn, Heb): “I will not set before my eyes a thing of worthlessness.”
notes.3467: (tn, Heb): “the doing of swerving [deeds] I hate.” The Hebrew term סֵטִים (setim) is probably an alternate spelling of שֵׂטִים (setim), which appears in many medieval Hebrew mss. The form appears to be derived from a verbal root שׂוּט (sut, “to fall away; to swerve”; see Ps 40:4).
notes.3468: (tn, Heb): “it [i.e., the doing of evil deeds] does not cling to me.”

rashi.heb:
*סטים.* 
לשון כי תשטה אשתו (במדבר ה׳:י״ב) לסור מן הדרך דישטול"מנט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *wayward.* Heb. סטים, an expression of (Num. 5:12): “whose wife strays (תשטה) from the right path,” to turn away from the road, destolemant in Old French, to swerve.

notes.3469: (tn, Heb): “a perverse heart will turn aside from me.” The adjective עִקֵּשׁ (’iqqesh) has the basic nuance “twisted; crooked” and by extension refers to someone or something that is morally perverse (see Ps 18:26). It appears frequently in the Book of Proverbs, where it is used of evil people (22:5), speech (8:8; 19:1), thoughts (11:20; 17:20), and life styles (2:15; 28:6).
notes.3470: (tn, Heb): “know.” The king will not willingly allow perverse individuals to remain in his royal court.

rashi.heb:
*רע לא אדע.* 
לא אהב לא אכיר בדבר רע:
rashi.eng: *I know no evil.* I love no [evil] (Another explanation: [Shem Ephraim]) I recognize no evil thing.

notes.3471: (tn, Heb): “[one who has] pride of eyes and wideness [i.e., arrogance] of heart, him I will not endure.”

rashi.heb:
*אותו לא אוכל.* 
שיהא חבירי שלא אלמד ממעשיו:
rashi.eng: *I cannot tolerate him.* that he should be my friend, lest I learn from his deeds.

notes.3472: (tn, Heb): “my eyes [are] on the faithful of the land.”
notes.3473: (tn): The Hebrew text simply reads, “in order to live with me.”
notes.3474: (tn, Heb): “one who walks in the way of integrity, he will minister to me.”

notes.3475: (tn, Heb): “he will not live in the midst of my house, one who does deceit.”
notes.3476: (tn, Heb): “one who speaks lies will not be established before my eyes.”

notes.3477: (sn): Psalm 102. The psalmist laments his oppressed state, but longs for a day when the Lord will restore Jerusalem and vindicate his suffering people.

rashi.heb:
*לבקרים אצמית.* 
מדי יום יום אכרית מעט מעט רשעי ישראל המחויבין מיתה:
rashi.eng: *Betimes I cut down.* Every day, I cut down the wicked of Israel little by little, those who are condemned to death.

notes.3478: (tn, Heb): “and may my cry for help come to you.”

rashi.heb:
*תפלה לעני.* 
ישראל שהם עם עני:
rashi.eng: *A prayer for a poor man.* Israel, who is a poor people.

rashi.heb:
*כי יעטף.* 
בהתעטף נפשם בצרה:
rashi.eng: *when he enwraps himself.* when their soul is enwrapped in distress.

notes.3479: (tn, Heb): “do not hide your face from me in the day of my trouble.” The idiom “to hide the face” can mean “to ignore” (see Pss 10:11; 13:1; 51:9) or carry the stronger idea of “to reject” (see Pss 29:7; 30:7; 88:14).

notes.3481: (tn, Heb): “for my days come to an end in smoke.”
notes.3482: (tn): The Hebrew noun מוֹ־קֵד (mo-qed, “fireplace”) occurs only here, in Isa 33:14 (where it refers to the fire itself), and perhaps in Lev 6:2.

notes.3485: (sn): I am unable to eat food. During his time of mourning, the psalmist refrained from eating. In the following verse he describes metaphorically the physical effects of fasting.

rashi.heb:
*נחרו.* 
הנו"ן משמשת כמו נעשו נקנו והוא לשון יובש כמו (איוב ל׳:ל׳) ועצמי חרה מני חורב, נחר מפוח (ירמיה ו):
rashi.eng: *are dried up.* Heb. נחרו. The “nun” serves as a prefix, as: נַעֲשׂוּ, they were made, נִקְנוּ, they were acquired; and it is an expression of dryness, as (Job 30:30): “and my bones dried out (חרה) from the heat” ; (Jer. 6:29), “the bellows is heated (נחר).”

notes.3486: (tn, Heb): “from the sound of my groaning my bone[s] stick to my flesh.” The preposition at the beginning of the verse is causal; the phrase “sound of my groaning” is metonymic for the anxiety that causes the groaning. The point seems to be this: Anxiety (which causes the psalmist to groan) keeps him from eating (v. 4). This physical deprivation in turn makes him emaciated – he is turned to “skin and bones,” so to speak.

notes.3487: (tn): The Hebrew term קָאַת (qa’at) refers to some type of bird (see Lev 11:18; Deut 14:17) that was typically found near ruins (see Zeph 2:14). Modern translations have frequently rendered this as some type of owl (NIV, REB “desert owl”; NRSV “owl”).
notes.3488: (tn): The Hebrew term כוֹס (khos) refers to a bird (see Lev 11:17; Deut 14:16), probably a type of owl (cf. NIV, REB “owl”; NRSV “little owl”).
notes.3489: (sn): By comparing himself to a screech owl among the ruins, the psalmist may be highlighting his loneliness (see v. 7), though he may also be comparing his cries for help to the owl’s screech.

notes.3490: (tn): This probably refers to the psalmist’s inability to sleep. Another option is to translate, “I keep watch,” in which case it might refer to watching for a response from the Lord (see vv. 1-2).

rashi.heb:
*דמיתי לקאת מדבר.* 
לקאת שם עוף הוא:
rashi.eng: *Like a bird of.* Heb. לקאת. It is the name of a bird.

rashi.heb:
*ככוס חרבות.* 
שם עוף כמו (ויקרא י״א:י״ז) את הכוס ואת השלך ואת הינשוף:
rashi.eng: *Like an owl of the wasteland.* Heb. ככוס, the name of a bird, as (Lev. 11:17): “The owl (הכוס), the cormorant, and the night owl.”

rashi.heb:
*חרבות.* 
מדברות דמיתי לקאת מדבר כך אנו נדודים ממקומנו ללכת בגולה:
rashi.eng: *wasteland.* deserts. I was like a bird of the desert. So do we wander from our place to go into exile.

notes.3491: (tn, Heb): “by me they swear.” When the psalmist’s enemies call judgment down on others, they hold the psalmist up as a prime example of what they desire their enemies to become.

rashi.heb:
*שקדתי.* 
התבוננתי בעצמי והנני כצפור הבודד על גג יושב לבדו באין זוג:
rashi.eng: *I pondered.* I pondered about myself, and behold I am like a lonely bird on a roof, sitting alone without a mate.

rashi.heb:
*בודד.* 
יושב בדד:
rashi.eng: *lonely.* Heb. בודד, sitting alone.

notes.3492: (sn): Mourners would sometimes put ashes on their head or roll in ashes as a sign of mourning (see 2 Sam 13:19; Job 2:8; Isa 58:5).

rashi.heb:
*מהוללי.* 
המתלוצצים בי ל' הוללות:
rashi.eng: *those who scorn me.* Heb. מהוללי, those who scorn me, an expression of mockery.

rashi.heb:
*בי נשבעו.* 
ראו ברעתי ונשבעים בי ואומרים אם לא יארע בי כמו שאירע לישראל כה יעשה לי כמו לישראל:
rashi.eng: *swear by me.* They saw my misfortune and they swear by me and say, “If it is not so, what happened to Israel should happen to me.” “So may the Lord do to me as to Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*בבכי מסכתי.* 
בדמעה מזגתי:
rashi.eng: *I mixed with weeping..* I mixed with tears.

notes.3495: (tn, Heb): “my days [are] like an extended [or “lengthening”] shadow,” that is, like a late afternoon shadow made by the descending sun that will soon be swallowed up by complete darkness.

rashi.heb:
*כי נשאתני.* 
תחילה והגבהתני ועתה השלכתני משמים ארץ ואם לא נשאתני תחילה לא היתה חרפתי רבה כל כך:
rashi.eng: *for You picked me up.* First You picked me up and now You cast me down from heaven to the Earth, and if You had not picked me up first, my disgrace would not be so great.

notes.3496: (tn, Heb): “sit” (i.e., sit enthroned, see Ps 9:7). The imperfect verbal form highlights the generalization.
notes.3497: (tn, Heb): “and your remembrance [is] for a generation and a generation.”

rashi.heb:
*כצל נטוי.* 
לעת ערב כשהצללי' נוטים וכשחשיכה אין נכרים אלא כלים והולכים:
rashi.eng: *Like a lengthening shadow.* At eventide, when the shadows lengthen, and when it becomes dark, they are not recognizable, but progressively disappear.

notes.3498: (tn): The imperfect verbal forms are understood as expressing the psalmist’s confidence in God’s intervention. Another option is to take them as expressing the psalmist’s request or wish, “You, rise up and have compassion!”

rashi.heb:
*ואתה.* 
אשר לעולם תשב ונשבעת לנו בך כשם שאתה קיים יש עליך לקיימנו, לפיכך:
rashi.eng: *But You.* Who will be enthroned forever, and Who swore to us by Yourself, just as You exist, it is incumbent upon You to fulfill it. Therefore…

notes.3500: (tn): The Poel of חָנַן (khanan) occurs only here and in Prov 14:21, where it refers to having compassion on the poor.
notes.3501: (tn, Heb): “her dust,” probably referring to the dust of the city’s rubble.

rashi.heb:
*אתה תקום תרחם ציון כי עת לחננה.* 
כי בך הבטחת (דברים ל״ב:ל״ו) כי יראה כי אזלת יד והרי אזלת יד:
rashi.eng: *You will rise, You will have mercy on Zion for it is time to favor it.* For so You promised (Deut. 32:36): “When He sees that their power is gone,” and it is indeed gone.

notes.3502: (tn, Heb): “will fear the name of the Lord.” To “fear” God’s name means to have a healthy respect for his revealed reputation which in turn motivates one to obey God’s commands (see Ps 86:11).
notes.3503: (tn): The verb “will fear” is understood by ellipsis in the second line (see the preceding line).

rashi.heb:
*כי רצו.* 
אהבו אף את אבניה ואת עפרה ומדרש אגדה כשיצא יכניהו וגלותו נשאו עמהם מאבני ירושלים ועפרה לבנות להם בבבל בית הכנסת:
rashi.eng: *For Your servants desired.* They loved even its stones and its earth. [According to] Midrash Aggadah, when Jeconiah and his exile left, they carried with them some of the stones and the earth of Jerusalem to build a synagogue for themselves there in Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*וייראו גוים.* 
את שמך כשתושיע את עמך:
rashi.eng: *And the nations will fear.* Your name when You save Your people.

notes.3504: (tn): The Hebrew adjective עַרְעָר (’arar, “destitute”) occurs only here in the OT. It is derived from the verbal root ערר (“to strip oneself”).
notes.3506: (tn): The perfect verbal forms in vv. 16-17 are functioning as future perfects, indicating future actions that will precede the future developments described in v. 15.

notes.3507: (tn): The Hebrew text has simply “this,” referring to the anticipated divine intervention on behalf of Zion (vv. 13, 16-17). The referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*הערער.* 
הצועק כמו (ישעיהו ט״ו:ה׳) זעקת שבר יעטרו, ד"א ערער הרוס ונשחת כמו, (לקמן קלז) ערו ערו:
rashi.eng: *He has turned to the prayer of those who cried out.* Heb. הערער, who cries out, as (Isa. 15:5): “a cry of destruction they will raise (יעוערו).” Another explanation: ערער means devastated and destroyed, as (below 137:7) “who say, ‘Raze it, raze it.’ ”

notes.3508: (tn, Heb): “from the height of his sanctuary.”
notes.3509: (tn): The perfect verbal forms in v. 19 are functioning as future perfects, indicating future actions that will precede the future developments described in v. 18.

rashi.heb:
*תכתב זאת.* 
כך יאמרו רואי הישועה תכתב הישועה הזאת לספר אותה לדור אחרון:
rashi.eng: *Let this be inscribed.* So will those who see the salvation say, “let this salvation be inscribed for the latest generation.”

rashi.heb:
*ועם נברא.* 
שנעשה בריה חדשה לצאת מעבדות לחרות מאופל לאור גדול:
rashi.eng: *and a created people.* that became a new creature to emerge from slavery to freedom and from darkness to a great light.

notes.3510: (tn, Heb): “the sons of death.” The phrase “sons of death” (see also Ps 79:11) is idiomatic for those condemned to die.

rashi.heb:
*אל ארץ הביט.* 
לראות בעני עמו:
rashi.eng: *looked… to Earth.* to see the affliction of His people.

notes.3512: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*תמותה.* 
חולה למות אנמוריני"דא בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the dying.* Heb. תמותה, mortally ill, enmorindes in Old French (as above 79:11).

notes.3513: (tn): “and the kingdoms to serve the Lord.”

notes.3514: (tn, Heb): “he has afflicted my strength in the way.” The term “way” refers here to the course of the psalmist’s life, which appears to be ending prematurely (vv. 23b-24).

notes.3515: (tn, Heb): “do not lift me up in the middle of my days.”
notes.3516: (tn, Heb): “in a generation of generations [are] your years.”

rashi.heb:
*ענה בדרך כחי.* 
חוזר לקבלו הראשון כי נשאתני ותשליכני ימי כצל נטוי ענה בדרך אויבי כחי:
rashi.eng: *He has afflicted my strength on the way.* He returns to his original complaint, “for You picked me up and cast me down. My days are like a lengthening shadow.” My enemy afflicted my strength on the way.

rashi.heb:
*אומר.* 
לה' אלי. אתה:
rashi.eng: *I say.* to the Lord, “You are my God.”

rashi.heb:
*אל תעלני בחצי ימי.* 
אל תסלק אותנו להשמידנו מן האדמה ביד אויבינו בחצי ימינו ומה הם ימינו כל ימות דור דורים שנותיך, הבטחת לקיימנו לפניך כמו שאמר בסוף המזמור ושנותיך לא יתמו וזרע עבדיך לפניך יכון:
rashi.eng: *do not take me away in the middle of my days.* Do not take us away to destroy us from the earth in the hands of our enemies in the middle of our days. And what are our days? All the days of all generations, of Your years, You promised to keep us alive before You, as he says at the end of the psalm, “and Your years do not end… and their seed will be established before You.”

notes.3518: (tn): The Hebrew verb חָלַף (khalaf) occurs twice in this line, once in the Hiphil (“you will remove them”) and once in the Qal (“they will disappear”). The repetition draws attention to the statement.

rashi.heb:
*לפנים.* 
מתחלה:
rashi.eng: *In the beginning.* Heb. לפנים, from the beginning.

notes.3519: (tn, Heb): “you [are] he,” or “you [are] the one.” The statement may echo the Lord’s affirmation “I am he” in Isa 41:4; 43:10, 13; 46:10; 48:12. In each of these passages the affirmation emphasizes the fact that the Lord transcends time limitations, the very point being made in Ps 102:27.

rashi.heb:
*כלבוש תחליפם.* 
כאדם ההופך לבושו לפושטו:
rashi.eng: *like raiment You will turn them over.* like a person who turns his garment inside out to take it off.

notes.3522: (sn): Psalm 103. The psalmist praises God for his mercy and willingness to forgive his people.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה הוא.* 
העומד וקיים:
rashi.eng: *But You are He.* Who stands and exists.

notes.3523: (tn): The verb “praise” is understood by ellipsis in the second line (see the preceding line).

rashi.heb:
*ברכי נפשי.* 
חמשה ברכי נפשי יש כאן כנגד חמשה עולמו' שאדם דר בהם כמו שאמרו רבותינו במסכ' ברכות דר במעי אמו ינק משדי אמו וכן כלם:
rashi.eng: *My soul, bless.* There are five mentions of “My soul, bless” here, corresponding to the five worlds in which man lives, as our Sages said in Tractate Berachoth (10a): “He lived in his mother’s womb, he sucked his mother’s breasts, and so all of them.”

notes.3524: (tn): Or “his benefits” (see 2 Chr 32:25, where the noun is also used of kind deeds performed by the Lord).

notes.3525: (tn): This relatively rare noun refers to deadly diseases (see Deut 29:22; Jer 14:18; 16:4; 2 Chr 21:19).

notes.3527: (tn): The Hebrew term שַׁחַת (shakhat, “pit”) is often used as a title for Sheol (see Pss 16:10; 30:9; 49:9; 55:24.

notes.3528: (tc, Heb): “who satisfies with the good of your ornaments.” The text as it stands makes little, if any, sense. The translation assumes an emendation of עֶדְיֵךְ (’ed’ekh, “your ornaments”) to עֹדֵכִי (’odekhiy, “your duration; your continuance”) that is, “your life” (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 18).
notes.3529: (sn): The expression your youth is renewed like an eagle’s may allude to the phenomenon of molting, whereby the eagle grows new feathers.

rashi.heb:
*תתחדש כנשר נעוריכי.* 
כנשר הזה שמחדש כנפיו ונוצה משנה לשנה, ויש מדרש אגדה על מין נשר שכשמזקין חוזר לנערותו:
rashi.eng: *that your youth renews itself like the eagle.* Like this eagle, which renews its wings and feathers from year to year. There is a Midrash Aggadah about a kind of eagle that returns to its youth when it becomes old.

notes.3530: (tn, Heb): “the Lord does fairness, and [acts of] justice for all the oppressed.”

notes.3531: (tn, Heb): “made known his ways.” God’s “ways” in this context are his protective and salvific acts in fulfillment of his promise (see also Deut 32:4; Pss 18:30; 67:2; 77:13 [note vv. 11-12, 14]; 138:5; 145:17).

rashi.heb:
*יודיע דרכיו.* 
מודיע דרכיו למשה:
rashi.eng: *He makes His ways known.* He makes His ways known to Moses.

notes.3533: (tn, Heb): “and great of loyal love” (see Ps 86:15).

notes.3534: (tn): The Hebrew verb נָטַר (natar) is usually taken to mean “to keep; to guard,” with “anger” being understood by ellipsis. The idiom “to guard anger” is then understood to mean “to remain angry” (see Lev 19:18; Jer 3:5, 12; Nah 1:2). However, it is possible that this is a homonymic root meaning “to be angry” (see HALOT 695 s.v. נטר).

notes.3535: (tn, Heb): “not according to our sins does he do to us.”
notes.3536: (tn, Heb): “and not according to our misdeeds does he repay us.”

notes.3537: (tn): For this sense of the verb גָבַר (gavar), see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 17, 19.

notes.3541: (tn): The Hebrew term פֶּשַׁע (pesha’, rebellious act”) is here used metonymically for the guilt such actions produce.

notes.3542: (tn): Or “sons,” but the Hebrew term sometimes refers to children in general.

rashi.heb:
*זכור כי עפר אנחנו.* 
זכור הוא ולא שכח שאנחנו עפר ויודע שאנוש כחצר ימיו וגו':
rashi.eng: *He remembers that we are dust.* He remembers and has not forgotten that we are dust and He knows that: “As for man, his days, etc.”

notes.3547: (tn, Heb): “[as for] mankind, like grass [are] his days.” The Hebrew noun אֱנוֹשׁ (’enosh) is used here generically of human beings. What is said is true of all mankind.

notes.3548: (tn, Heb): “[the] wind.” The word “hot” is supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*רוח עברה בו.* 
אם עברה חולי של מיתה:
rashi.eng: *For a wind passes over him.* If mortal illness passes over him.

notes.3549: (tn, Heb): “but the loyal love of the Lord [is] from everlasting to everlasting over those who fear him.”
notes.3550: (tn, Heb): “and his righteousness to sons of sons.”

notes.3551: (tn, Heb): “to those who remember his precepts to do them.”

rashi.heb:
*משלה.* 
מושלת:

notes.3553: (tn, Heb): “[you] mighty ones of strength, doers of his word, by listening to the voice of his word.”

notes.3555: (tn, Heb): “his attendants, doers of his desire.”

notes.3556: (tn, Heb): “all his works,” which includes mankind.
notes.3558: (sn): Psalm 104. The psalmist praises God as the ruler of the world who sustains all life.

rashi.heb:
*ברכו ה' כל מעשיו.* 
אשר הם בכל מקומות שממשלתו שם:
rashi.eng: *Bless the Lord, all His works.* who are in all the places of His dominion.

rashi.heb:
*עוטה אור.* 
ברקיע כשלמה:
rashi.eng: *[You] enwrap Yourself with light.* in the sky like a garment.

notes.3560: (tn, Heb): “one who lays the beams on water [in] his upper rooms.” The “water” mentioned here corresponds to the “waters above” mentioned in Gen 1:7. For a discussion of the picture envisioned by the psalmist, see L. I. J. Stadelmann, The Hebrew Conception of the World, 44-45.
notes.3561: (sn): Verse 3 may depict the Lord riding a cherub, which is in turn propelled by the wind current. Another option is that the wind is personified as a cherub. See Ps 18:10 and the discussion of ancient Near Eastern parallels to the imagery in M. Weinfeld, “‘Rider of the Clouds’ and ‘Gatherer of the Clouds’,” JANESCU 5 (1973): 422-24.

notes.3562: (tc, Heb): “and his attendants a flaming fire.” The lack of agreement between the singular “fire” and plural “attendants” has prompted various emendations. Some read “fire and flame.” The present translation assumes an emendation to “his attendant” (יו in the Hebrew text being virtually dittographic). In Ugaritic mythology Yam’s messengers appear as flaming fire before the assembly of the gods. See G. R. Driver, Canaanite Myths and Legends, 42.

rashi.heb:
*עושה מלאכיו רוחות.* 
עושה את הרוחות שלוחיו:
rashi.eng: *He makes winds His messengers.* lit. He makes His messengers winds. He makes the wind His messengers.

notes.3563: (tc, Heb): “you covered it.” The masculine suffix is problematic if the grammatically feminine noun “earth” is the antecedent. For this reason some emend the form to a feminine verb with feminine suffix, כִּסַּתָּה (kisattah, “[the watery deep] covered it [i.e., the earth]”), a reading assumed by the present translation.
notes.3565: (sn): Verse 6 refers to the condition described in Gen 1:2 (note the use of the Hebrew term תְּהוֹם [t�hom, “watery deep”] in both texts).

rashi.heb:
*תהום כלבוש כסיתו.* 
זה דוגמת האמור במקום אחר (איוב ל״ח:ט׳) בשומי ענן לבושו וגו':
rashi.eng: *You covered the deep as [with] a garment.* This is similar to what is said elsewhere (Job 38:9): “When I made the cloud its raiment, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*תהום.* 
הוא הים:
rashi.eng: *the deep.* That is the sea.

rashi.heb:
*על הרים יעמדו.* 
מי אוקיינוס גבוה מכל העולם עומד על ההרים, וכן הוא אומר (עמוס ה ט) הקורא למי הים וישפכם על פני הארץ אין שפיכה אלא מלמעלה למטה:
rashi.eng: *the waters stand on the mountains.* The waters of the ocean are higher than the whole world. They stand on the mountains, and so Scripture states (Amos 5:8, 9:6): “He who calls the water of the sea and pours it upon the face of the earth.” Pouring denotes only [pouring] from above downward.

rashi.heb:
*מן גערתך ינוסון.* 
כשאמרת (בראשית א׳:ט׳) יקוו המים ומאותו הקול יחפזון ונקוו אל מקום אשר יסדת להם:
rashi.eng: *From Your rebuke they fled.* When You said (Gen. 1:9): “Let the waters gather.” And from that voice they hastened away and gathered in the place that You founded for them.

notes.3566: (tn, Heb): “from your shout they fled, from the sound of your thunder they hurried off.” Verses 7-8 poetically depict Gen 1:9-10.

notes.3567: (tn, Heb): “a boundary you set up, they will not cross, they will not return to cover the earth.”

rashi.heb:
*גבול שמת.* 
להם החול אשר סביב שפתו:
rashi.eng: *You set a boundary.* for them, viz. the sand that is around its shore.

notes.3568: (tn, Heb): “[the] one who sends springs into streams.” Another option is to translate, “he sends streams [i.e., streams that originate from springs] into the valleys” (cf. NIV).

notes.3569: (tn, Heb): “among the thick foliage they give a sound.”

rashi.heb:
*עליהם עוף השמים ישכון.* 
על המעינות:
rashi.eng: *Beside them the fowl of the heavens dwell.* Beside the springs.

rashi.heb:
*מבין עפאים.* 
ענפי אילנות וכן (דניאל ד) עפיה שפיר:
rashi.eng: *from between the branches.* Heb. עפאים, the branches of the trees, and so (Dan. 4:11): “its branches were (עפיה) beautiful.”

notes.3571: (tn, Heb): “from the fruit of your works the earth is full.” The translation assumes that “fruit” is literal here. If “fruit” is understood more abstractly as “product; result,” then one could translate, “the earth flourishes as a result of your deeds” (cf. NIV, NRSV, REB).

notes.3572: (tn, Heb): “causes the grass to sprout up.”
notes.3573: (tn, Heb): “for the service of man” (see Gen 2:5).
notes.3574: (tn, Heb): “to cause food to come out from the earth.”

notes.3575: (tn, Heb): “and wine [that] makes the heart of man happy.”
notes.3576: (tn, Heb): “to make [the] face shine from oil.” The Hebrew verb צָהַל (tsahal, “to shine”) occurs only here in the OT. It appears to be an alternate form of צָהַר (tsahar), a derivative from צָהָרִים (tsaharim, “noon”).
notes.3577: (tn, Heb): “and food [that] sustains the heart of man.”

rashi.heb:
*מצמיח חציר וגו' ויין אשר ישמח לבב.* 
אנוש גם אותו יוציא מן הארץ ושמן. להצהיל בו פנים:
