לקרבני אליך:
rashi.eng: *to attach me.* Heb. לרעי, to attach me to You.

notes.4490: (tn, Heb): “my traveling and my lying down you measure.” The verb זָרָה (zarah, “to measure”) is probably here a denominative from זָרָת (zarat, “a span; a measure”), though some derive it from זָרָה (zarat, “to winnow; to sift”; see BDB 279-80 s.v. זָרָה).

rashi.heb:
*ארחי ורבעי זרית.* 
דרכי ורבצי ושכני סבבת מחיצה שאין לי לעשות דבר בלא ידיעתך:
rashi.eng: *My going about and my lying down You encompassed.* My way, my lying down, and my dwelling You have encompassed with a wall, for I can do nothing without Your knowledge.

rashi.heb:
*זרית.* 
לשון זר זהב סביב (שמות כה) וכן חברו מנחם, ורבותינו דרשו על טיפת תשמיש שהולד נוצר מן הברור שבה ופירושו זרית לשון זורה התבואה לברור את הפסולת שבה:
rashi.eng: *You encompassed.* heb. זרית, an expression of (Exod. 25:24): “a gold crown (זר).” Menachem associated it in this manner (p. 82). Our Sages, however, interpreted it (Nid. 31a, Mid. Ps. 139:3) as referring to the droplet of [semen, transmitted in] sexual intercourse, from whose choicest part the fetus is formed, and the meaning of זֵרִיתָ (זורה) is an expression of winnowing the grain to purify it of the refuse it contains.

rashi.heb:
*הסכנתה.* 
למדת:
rashi.eng: *You are accustomed.* Heb. הִסכנתה, you are accustomed.

notes.4493: (tn, Heb): “look, O Lord, you know all of it.”

rashi.heb:
*אחור וקדם צרתני.* 
פני ואחורי:
rashi.eng: *From the rear and the front.* My face and my back.

rashi.heb:
*כפכה.* 
אכפך ורדוייך דישטרוי"ט בלעז:
rashi.eng: *Your pressure.* your coercion and your ruling, destroit in Old French.

notes.4494: (tn, Heb): “too amazing [is this] knowledge for me, it is elevated, I cannot attain to it.”

rashi.heb:
*פליאה דעת וגו'.* 
מכוסה ונעלם ממני מקום לברוח מפניך (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *Knowledge is hidden from me, etc..* A place to escape from You is covered up and hidden from me. (I found this.)

notes.4495: (tn, Heb): “Where can I go from your spirit, and where from your face can I flee?” God’s “spirit” may refer here (1) to his presence (note the parallel term, “your face,” and see Ps 104:29-30, where God’s “face” is his presence and his “spirit” is the life-giving breath he imparts) or (2) to his personal Spirit (see Ps 51:10).

notes.4496: (tn): The Hebrew verb סָלַק (salaq, “to ascend”) occurs only here in the OT, but the word is well-attested in Aramaic literature from different time periods and displays a wide semantic range (see DNWSI 2:788-90).

rashi.heb:
*ואציעה.* 
מצע ומשכב:
rashi.eng: *and if I make my bed.* Heb. ואציעה, an expression of a spread (מצע) and a bed.

notes.4499: (sn): On the wings of the dawn. This personification of the “dawn” may find its roots in mythological traditions about the god Shachar, whose birth is described in an Ugaritic myth (see G. R. Driver, Canaanite Myths and Legends, 126) and who is mentioned in Isa 14:12 as the father of Helel.

rashi.heb:
*אשא כנפי שחר.* 
אם אשא לי כנפים כשחר הזה המבהיק לפי שעה מסוף העולם לסופו כן אמהר לעוף עד אשר אשכון באחרית ים:
rashi.eng: *[If] I take up the wings of dawn.* If I take up for myself the wings of dawn, which shine at once from one end of the world to the other, so will I fly swiftly until I dwell at the end of the sea.

notes.4501: (tn): The Hebrew verb שׁוּף (shuf), which means “to crush; to wound,” in Gen 3:15 and Job 9:17, is problematic here. For a discussion of attempts to relate the verb to Arabic roots, see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 251. Many emend the form to יְשׂוּכֵּנִי (yesukkeniy), from the root שׂכך (“to cover,” an alternate form of סכך), a reading assumed in the present translation.

rashi.heb:
*ואמר אך חשך ישופני.* 
אם אמרתי אהיה נסתר במחשך והחשך יחשיך עלי ולא תראני, ישופני לשון נשף:
rashi.eng: *I said, “Darkness will darken me”.* If I said, “I will be hidden in the darkness, and the darkness will envelop me so that You will not see me.” יְשׁוּפֵנִי is an expression of נֶשֶׁף, evening.

rashi.heb:
*ולילה אור בעדני.* 
והלילה יהי מאפיל לנגדי, אור זה לשון אופל הוא כמו (איוב לז, יא) יפיץ ענן אורו וכן כל ככבי אור (לקמן קמ"ח) וכן ויאר את הלילה (שמות י"ד):
rashi.eng: *“and the night will be dark about me”.* Heb. אור, lit. light. And the night will darken before me. This אוֹר is an expression of darkness, like (Job 37: 11): “he spreads his clouds of darkness (אור);” similarly (below 148:3), “all stars of the night (אור);” similarly (Exod. 14:20), “and it darkened (ויאר) the night.”

notes.4503: (tn): The words “to see” are supplied in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*כחשיכה כאורה.* 
שניהם שוין לך:
rashi.eng: *Even.* there I have no asylum, for no darkness will obscure [anything] from You.

rashi.heb:
*גם.* 
שם אין לי מנוס כי כל חשך לא יחשיך ממך:
rashi.eng: *as darkness, so is the light.* Both are the same to You.

notes.4507: (tn, Heb): “my kidneys.” The kidneys were sometimes viewed as the seat of one’s emotions and moral character (cf. Pss 7:9; 26:2). A number of translations, recognizing that “kidneys” does not communicate this idea to the modern reader, have generalized the concept: “inmost being” (NAB, NIV); “inward parts” (NASB, NRSV); “the delicate, inner parts of my body” (NLT). In the last instance, the focus is almost entirely on the physical body rather than the emotions or moral character. The present translation, by using a hendiadys (one concept expressed through two terms), links the concepts of emotion (heart) and moral character (mind).
notes.4508: (tn): The Hebrew verb סָכַךְ (sakhakh, “to weave together”) is an alternate form of שָׂכַךְ (sakhakh, “to weave”) used in Job 10:11.

rashi.heb:
*כליותי.* 
החושבים כל מחשבותי:
rashi.eng: *For You created my reins.* which think all my thoughts.

rashi.heb:
*תסוכני.* 
תסוככני:
rashi.eng: *You covered me.* Heb. תסכני, [equivalent to] תסוֹככני.

notes.4509: (tc, Heb): “because awesome things, I am distinct, amazing [are] your works.” The text as it stands is syntactically problematic and makes little, if any, sense. The Niphal of פָּלָה (pala’) occurs elsewhere only in Exod 33:16. Many take the form from פָלָא (pala’; see GKC 216 �75.qq), which in the Niphal perfect means “to be amazing” (see 2 Sam 1:26; Ps 118:23; Prov 30:18). Some, following the LXX and some other ancient witnesses, also prefer to emend the verb from first to second person, “you are amazing” (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 249, 251). The present translation assumes the text conflates two variants: נפלאים, the otherwise unattested masculine plural participle of פָלָא, and נִפְלָאוֹת (nifla’ot), the usual (feminine) plural form of the Niphal participle. The latter has been changed to a verb by later scribes in an attempt to accommodate it syntactically. The original text likely read, נוראות נפלאותים מעשׂיך (“your works [are] awesome [and] amazing”).
notes.4510: (tc, Heb): “and my being knows very much.” Better parallelism is achieved (see v. 15a) if one emends יֹדַעַת (yoda’at), a Qal active participle, feminine singular form, to יָדַעְתָּ (yada’ta), a Qal perfect second masculine singular perfect. See L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 252.

notes.4511: (tc): The Hebrew term אֲשֶׁר (’asher, “which”) should probably be emended to כֲּאַשֶׁר (ka’asher, “when”). The kaf (כ) may have been lost by haplography (note the kaf at the end of the preceding form).
notes.4512: (sn): The phrase depths of the earth may be metaphorical (euphemistic) or it may reflect a prescientific belief about the origins of the embryo deep beneath the earth’s surface (see H. W. Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament, 96-97). Job 1:21 also closely associates the mother’s womb with the earth.

rashi.heb:
*עשיתי בסתר.* 
בתשמיש:
rashi.eng: *I was made in secret.* In sexual intercourse.

rashi.heb:
*בתחתיות ארץ.* 
במדור התחתון שבמעי אמי:
rashi.eng: *in the lowest parts of the earth.* In the lowest compartment in my mother’s womb.

notes.4513: (tn, Heb): “Your eyes saw my shapeless form.” The Hebrew noun גֹּלֶם (golem) occurs only here in the OT. In later Hebrew the word refers to “a lump, a shapeless or lifeless substance,” and to “unfinished matter, a vessel wanting finishing” (Jastrow 222 s.v. גּוֹלֶם). The translation employs the dynamic rendering “when I was inside the womb” to clarify that the speaker was still in his mother’s womb at the time he was “seen” by God.
notes.4514: (tn, Heb): “and on your scroll all of them were written, [the] days [which] were formed, and [there was] not one among them.” This “scroll” may be the “scroll of life” mentioned in Ps 69:28 (see the note on the word “living” there).

rashi.heb:
*גלמי ראו עיניך.* 
מאז בראת את העולם ראו עיניך את כל גולמי הדורות הבאים:
rashi.eng: *Your eyes saw my unformed body.* From the time that You created the world, Your eyes saw all the forms of the coming generations.

rashi.heb:
*גולמי.* 
זהרתי ותבנית צורתי בטרם הולדי ובטרם בואי לעולם ראו עיניך:
rashi.eng: *My unformed body.* Heb. גלמי. My splendor and the pattern of my form, before I was born and before I came into the world, Your eyes saw.

rashi.heb:
*ועל ספרך כולם יכתבו.* 
וכל יצורי עולם כמוני כמוהם גם כלם בטרם הבראם יחדיו גלוים לפניך:
rashi.eng: *and on Your book they were all written.* And all the creatures of the world, like me, like them, even all of them, before they were created, were together revealed before You.

rashi.heb:
*ימים יצרו ולא אחד בהם.* 
כל מעשה האדם ותכליתיהם גלוים לפניך כאילו יוצרו כבר אע"פ שלא היה אחד מכולם ולא היה עדיין כאחד בעולם ואלו הם פלאי מפעלות אלהים ומשפט גבורתו שעתידות גלוים לפניו טרם תבאנה וכן הוא אומר בטרם אצרך בבטן וגו' (ירמיהו א׳:ה׳):
rashi.eng: *days have been formed and one of them.* All man’s deeds and the end of the days are revealed before You as if they were already formed, although not one of them was in existence, and not one was yet in the world. These are the wonders of God’s works and the way of His might, that future events are revealed to Him before they come. And so, Scripture says (Jer. 1:5): “When I had not yet formed you in the womb, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*ועל ספרך כלם יכתבו.* 
ספר תולדות אדם שהראית לאדם הראשון:
rashi.eng: *and on Your book, they were all written.* The book of the generations of man, which You showed to Adam.

rashi.heb:
*כלם יכתבו.* 
כמו נכתבו:
rashi.eng: *written.* lit. all of them will be written, like נכתבוּ.

rashi.heb:
*ימים יוצרו ולא אחד בהם.* 
לסוף ימים רבים היו עתידין להבראות ולא היה עדיין אחד מהם נברא בהן לפי המסורת שכתוב ולא זהו פירושו, ולפי המקרא שהוא נקרא ולו כך פירושו ימים יוצרו הראהו ימים העתידים להבראות ולחלקו בירר אחד את יום השבת ד"א זה יום הכפורים לסליחה:
rashi.eng: *days were formed without one of them.* Ultimately, many days were destined to be created, but not one of them was yet created. According to the masoretic text, in which לא is written, this is its explanation. And according to the reading, for it is read לו this is its explanation: days have been formed, He showed the days that were destined to be created, and for His share, He chose one of them, viz. the Sabbath day. Another explanation: This is the Day of Atonement, for forgiveness.

notes.4515: (tn, Heb): “and to me how precious are your thoughts, O God.” The Hebrew verb יָקַר (yaqar) probably has the sense of “difficult [to comprehend]” here (see HALOT 432 s.v. יקר qal.1 and note the use of Aramaic יַקִּר in Dan 2:11). Elsewhere in the immediate context the psalmist expresses his amazement at the extent of God’s knowledge about him (see vv. 1-6, 17b-18).
notes.4516: (tn, Heb): “how vast are their heads.” Here the Hebrew word “head” is used of the “sum total” of God’s knowledge of the psalmist.

rashi.heb:
*ולי מה יקרו רעיך.* 
כנסת ישראל אומרת מה נכבדו בעיני הצדיקים שבכל דור ודור:
rashi.eng: *And to me, how dear are Your friends.* The congregation of Israel says, “How esteemed in my eyes are the righteous in every generation!”

rashi.heb:
*מה עצמו ראשיהם.* 
חשבון ספירותיה' לשון כי תשא את ראש בני ישראל (שמות ל׳:י״ב):
rashi.eng: *How great is their sum!.* The calculation of their counting, an expression of (Exod. 30:12): “When you take the sum (ראש) of the children of Israel.”

notes.4517: (tc, Heb): “I awake and I [am] still with you.” A reference to the psalmist awaking from sleep makes little, if any, sense contextually. For this reason some propose an emendation to הֲקִצּוֹתִי (haqitsoti), a Hiphil perfect form from an otherwise unattested verb קָצַץ (qatsats) understood as a denominative of קֵץ (qets, “end”). See L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 252-53.

rashi.heb:
*אספרם מחול.* 
אם באתי לספור את טוב מעשיהם מחול ירבון:
rashi.eng: *I shall count them… than sand.* If I came to count the good of their deeds, they would be more numerous than sand.

rashi.heb:
*הקיצותי ועודי עמך.* 
הנני באתי עתה לקץ הדורות אשר קצבת מאז עד היום ועוד דור זה עמך וביראתך ולא נטיתי מאחריך:
rashi.eng: *I have come to the end, and I am still with You.* Behold I have now come to the end of the generations that You allotted from then until today, and this generation is still with You and in fear of You, and I have not turned away from following You.

notes.4518: (tn): The Hebrew particle אִם (’im, “if”) and following prefixed verbal form here express a wish (see Pss 81:8; 95:7, as well as GKC 321 �109.b).

rashi.heb:
*אם תקטל וגו'.* 
הלואי ותקטול את עמלק הרשע:
rashi.eng: *If only You would slay the wicked.* If only You would slay the wicked.

notes.4521: (tc, Heb): “they speak [of] you.” The suffixed form of the verb אָמַר (’amar, “to speak”) is peculiar. The translation assumes an emendation to יַמְרֻךָ (yamrukha), a Hiphil form from מָרָה (marah, “to rebel”; see Ps 78:40).
notes.4523: (tc, Heb): “lifted up for emptiness, your cities.” The Hebrew text as it stands makes no sense. The form נָשֻׂא (nasu’; a Qal passive participle) should be emended to נָשְׂאוּ (nos�u; a Qal perfect, third common plural, “[they] lift up”). Many emend עָרֶיךָ (’arekha, “your cities”) to עָלֶיךָ (’alekha, “against you”), but it is preferable to understand the noun as an Aramaism and translate “your enemies” (see Dan 4:16 and L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 253).

rashi.heb:
*ימרוך למזמה.* 
מזכירים שמך על כל מחשבות רעתם ומכנים אלהותך לע"ג:
rashi.eng: *Who mention You with wicked thought.* They mention Your name regarding all the thoughts of their evil and call their deities with Your name.

rashi.heb:
*נשוא לשוא.* 
כמו נשאו לשוא:
rashi.eng: *took it up.* Heb. נשוא, like נשאו, they took up.

rashi.heb:
*עריך.* 
אויביך, נשאו לשוא אויביך את שמך:
rashi.eng: *Your enemies… in vain.* Your enemies took up Your name in vain.

notes.4524: (tc, Heb): “who raise themselves up against you.” The form וּבִתְקוֹמְמֶיךָ (uvitqom�mekha) should be emended to וּבְמִתְקוֹמְמֶיךָ (uv�mitqom�mekha), a Hitpolel participle (the prefixed mem [מ] of the participle is accidentally omitted in the MT, though a few medieval Hebrew mss have it).

notes.4525: (tn, Heb): “[with] completeness of hatred I hate them.”

notes.4527: (tn): The Hebrew noun שַׂרְעַפַּי (sar’apay, “concerns”) is used of “worries” in Ps 94:19.

notes.4528: (tn): Many understand the Hebrew term עֹצֶב (’otsev) as a noun meaning “pain,” and translate the phrase דֶּרֶךְ עֹצֶב (derekh ’otsev) as “of pain,” but this makes little sense here. (Some interpret it to refer to actions which bring pain to others.) It is preferable to take עֹצֶב as “idol” (see HALOT 865 s.v. I עֹצֶב) and understand “way of an idol” to refer to idolatrous actions or tendency. See L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 253.
notes.4529: (tn, Heb): “in the path of antiquity.” This probably refers to the moral path prescribed by the Lord at the beginning of Israel’s history. See Jer 6:16; 18:15, as well as L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 253.
notes.4530: (sn): Psalm 140. The psalmist asks God to deliver him from his deadly enemies, calls judgment down upon them, and affirms his confidence in God’s justice.

rashi.heb:
*אם דרך עוצב וגו'.* 
אם דרך מעצבה וקלקול בי:
rashi.eng: *whether there is any vexatious way about me.* Whether there is a way of vexation and deterioration in me.

notes.4531: (tn, Heb): “from a wicked man.” The Hebrew uses the singular in a representative or collective sense (note the plural verbs in v. 2).
notes.4532: (tn, Heb): “a man of violent acts.” The Hebrew uses the singular in a representative or collective sense (note the plural verbs in v. 2).

notes.4534: (tc, Heb): “they attack [for] war.” Some revocalize the verb (which is a Qal imperfect from גּוּר, gur, “to attack”) as יְגָרוּ (y�garu), a Piel imperfect from גָרָה (garah, “stir up strife”). This is followed in the present translation.

notes.4535: (tn, Heb): “they sharpen their tongue like a serpent.” Ps 64:3 reads, “they sharpen their tongues like sword.” Perhaps Ps 140:3 uses a mixed metaphor, the point being that “they sharpen their tongues [like a sword],” as it were, so that when they speak, their words wound like a serpent’s bite. Another option is that the language refers to the pointed or forked nature of a serpent’s tongue, which is viewed metaphorically as “sharpened.”
notes.4536: (tn): The Hebrew term is used only here in the OT.

rashi.heb:
*יגורו מלחמות.* 
יהיו מלחמות במגוריהם ובמושבותם:
rashi.eng: *every day they gather to wage war.* There will be wars in their dwellings and in their settlements.

rashi.heb:
*חמת עכשוב.* 
חמת לשון ארס כמו (דברים ל״ב:ל״ג) חמת תנינים יינם שאם תפרשהו לשון אף וכי לשון אף נופל אצל יין אלא לשון ארס ויצו"ש בלע"ז וכן נופל כאן לשון ארס תחת השפה:
rashi.eng: *the venom of a spider.* Heb. חמתעכשוב. חמת is an expression of venom, as (Deut. 32:33): “the venom of (חמת) dragons is their wine,” for if you interpret it as an expression of wrath, does an expression of wrath fit with wine? Rather, it is an expression of venom, venimos in Old French. Similarly, here the term venom relates to “under the lips.”

rashi.heb:
*עכשוב.* 
עכביש איריינ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *a spider.* Heb. עכשוב, a spider, araignee in French.

notes.4540: (tn, Heb): “and ropes,” but many prefer to revocalize the noun as a participle (חֹבְלִים, khov�lim) from the verb חָבַל (khaval, “act corruptly”).

rashi.heb:
*וחבלים פרשו רשת.* 
דרך הרשת לקשור חבל ארוך בראשה והציד כשרואה את העופות שוכנים תחת הרשת מושך החבל והרשת נופל על העופות:
rashi.eng: *and [with] ropes they spread a net.* It is customary to tie a long rope to the end of a net, and when the hunter sees the birds resting under the net, he draws the rope, and the net falls on the birds.

rashi.heb:
*ליד מעגל.* 
אצל נתיבתי ופעמי:
rashi.eng: *beside [my] path.* Beside my paths and my steps.

rashi.heb:
*ליד.* 
אצל כמו (שמואל ב י״ד:ל׳) ראו חלקת יואב על ידי:
rashi.eng: *beside.* Heb. ליד, like (II Sam. 14:30): “See, Joab’s field is near mine (ידי).”

notes.4543: (tn, Heb): “do not grant the desires of the wicked.”
notes.4544: (tn, Heb): “his.” The singular is used in a representative sense (see v. 1).
notes.4545: (tn, Heb): “his plot do not promote, they rise up.” The translation understands the final verb as being an unmarked temporal clause. Another option is to revocalize the verb as a Hiphil and take the verb with the next verse, “those who surround me lift up [their] head,” which could refer to their proud attitude as they anticipate victory (see Ps 27:6).

notes.4546: (tn, Heb): “harm of their lips.” The genitive here indicates the source or agent of the harm.

rashi.heb:
*מאוי רשע.* 
עמלק הרשע:
rashi.eng: *the desires of the wicked.* The wicked Esau.

rashi.heb:
*זממו אל תפק.* 
מחשבתו אל תצליח:
rashi.eng: *for they are constantly haughty.* Heb. ירומו סלה, because they are arrogant always. Our Rabbis, however (Gen. Rabbah 75:9) explained זממוֹ as an expression of a bit that muzzles the camel, and it is a Mishnaic expression.

rashi.heb:
*ירומו סלה.* 
כי יתגאו סלה, ורבותינו פירשו זממו לשון רסן הזומם את פי הגמל ולשון משנה הוא אל תפק. אל תוציא מלחייו:
rashi.eng: *do not take out.* Heb. תפק אל, Do not take it out of his jaws.

notes.4547: (tn): The verb form in the Kethib (consonantal Hebrew text) appears to be a Hiphil imperfect from the root מוּט (mut, “to sway”), but the Hiphil occurs only here and in Ps 55:3, where it is preferable to read יַמְטִירוּ (yamtiru, “they rain down”). In Ps 140:10 the form יַמְטֵר (yamter, “let him rain down”) should probably be read.
notes.4548: (tn, Heb): “into bottomless pits, they will not arise.” The translation assumes that the preposition -בְּ (bet) has the nuance “from” here. Another option is to connect the line with what precedes, take the final clause as an asyndetic relative clause, and translate, “into bottomless pits [from which] they cannot arise.” The Hebrew noun מַהֲמֹרָה (mahamorah, “bottomless pit”) occurs only here in the OT.

rashi.heb:
*ראש מסבי.* 
חבורת חשבון גדודי עשו האומרים להסב אותי מעליך עמל שפתיהם יכסם (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *The numbers of those who surround me.* Armies of the number of the troops of Esau who plan to surround me, may the lies of their lips cover them. (I found.)

notes.4551: (tn, Heb): “for blows.” The Hebrew noun מַדְחֵפֹה (madkhefoh, “blow”) occurs only here in the OT.

rashi.heb:
*ימוטו.* 
יהיו מוטים הגחלים עליהם ישכבו בהם עד שיתמוטטו ויכבו מאליהם נמצא הגוף כלה ואבד:
rashi.eng: *descend.* May the coals descend on them. Let them lie upon them until they sink and become extinguished by themselves. The body will thus disintegrate and disappear.

rashi.heb:
*באש יפילם.* 
המפיל ונוקם גחלים של גיהנם:
rashi.eng: *He will cast them into fire.* He Who casts and avenges [will cast them] into the fire of Gehinnom.

rashi.heb:
*במהמורות.* 
יפילם לבל יקומו עוד:
rashi.eng: *in wars.* He will cast them so that they will no longer rise.

rashi.heb:
*במהמורות.* 
במלחמות ותגר ל' ממרים הייתם (דברים ט):
rashi.eng: *in wars.* Heb. במהמרות, in wars and strife, an expression of (Deut. 9:4): “You have been rebellious (ממרים).”

notes.4552: (tc): The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading a first person verb form here. The Kethib reads the second person.
notes.4553: (tn, Heb): “and the just cause of the poor.”

rashi.heb:
*איש לשון.* 
עשו כי ציד בפיו צד את אביו בפיו:
rashi.eng: *A slanderer.* Esau, who would trap with his mouth.

rashi.heb:
*יצודנו.* 
הרע שהוא עושה הוא יצודנו:
rashi.eng: *will trap him.* The evil that he does will trap him.

notes.4554: (sn): Psalm 141. The psalmist asks God to protect him from sin and from sinful men.

rashi.heb:
*ידעתי.* 
כי סוף הדברים יעשה ה' דין עני וינקום נקמת עבדיו:
rashi.eng: *I know.* that ultimately the Lord will perform the judgment of a poor man, and He will avenge the vengeance of His servants.

rashi.heb:
*אך.* 
ימהר ויעשה כדי שיודו צדיקים לשמו:
rashi.eng: *But.* May he hasten and do it so that the righteous will thank His name.

notes.4555: (tn, Heb): “may my prayer be established [like] incense before you, the uplifting of my hands [like] an evening offering.”

rashi.heb:
*משאת כפי.* 
מה שאני נושא כפי אליך:
rashi.eng: *the lifting of my hands.* What I lift up my hands to You.

notes.4556: (tn, Heb): “door.” The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.
notes.4557: (sn): My mouth…my lips. The psalmist asks God to protect him from speaking inappropriately or sinfully.

rashi.heb:
*שיתה ה' שמרה לפי.* 
בהתפללי לפניך להיותי מדבר צחות שיהיו לרצון:
rashi.eng: *O Lord, place a guard for my mouth.* when I pray before You, that I should speak poetically, that it should be acceptable.

rashi.heb:
*דל שפתי.* 
היא שפה העליונה (כמו דלתות שפתי):
rashi.eng: *the portal of my lips.* That is the upper lip (like portals of my lips).

notes.4558: (tn, Heb): “do not turn my heart toward an evil thing.”
notes.4559: (tn, Heb): “to act sinfully in practices in wickedness with men, doers of evil.”
notes.4560: (sn): Their delicacies. This probably refers to the enjoyment that a sinful lifestyle appears to offer.

rashi.heb:
*אל תט לבי.* 
אל יהיה נוטה לרע:
rashi.eng: *Do not incline my heart.* May my heart not be inclined toward evil.

rashi.heb:
*את אישים.* 
עם אנשים (מצאתי):

*ובל אלחם במנעמיהם.* 
ולא אהיה מיסב בסעודתם:
rashi.eng: *and may I not partake of their feasts.* And I shall not sit at their feasts.

notes.4561: (tn): The form יָנִי (yaniy) appears to be derived from the verbal root נוּא (nu’). Another option is to emend the form to יְנָא (y�na’), a Piel from נָאָה (na’ah), and translate “may choice oil not adorn my head” (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 271). In this case, choice oil, like delicacies in v. 4, symbolize the pleasures of sin.
notes.4562: (sn): May my head not refuse choice oil. The psalmist compares the constructive criticism of the godly (see the previous line) to having refreshing olive oil poured over one’s head.
notes.4563: (tc, Heb): “for still, and my prayer [is] against their evil deeds.” The syntax of the Hebrew text is difficult; the sequence -כִּי־עוֹד וּ (kiy-’od u-, “for still and”) occurs only here. The translation assumes an emendation to כִּי עֵד תְפלָּתִי (“indeed a witness [is] my prayer”). The psalmist’s lament about the evil actions of sinful men (see v. 4) testifies against the wicked in the divine court.

rashi.heb:
*יהלמני צדיק חסד ויוכיחני.* 
טוב לי שיוכיחני וייסרני נביא אמת וצדק שכל מהלומיו ותוכחתו חסד:
rashi.eng: *May a righteous man strike me with kindness and reprove me.* It is better that a true and righteous prophet reprove me and chastise me, for all his blows and his reproof are kindness.

rashi.heb:
*שמן ראש אל יני ראשי.* 
שמן מלכות שהוצק על ראשי כמו שנאמר (לעיל כ"ג) דשנת בשמן ראשי אל יסיר את ראשי מתוכחת הצדיק ללכת וללחום את פועלי און:
rashi.eng: *may the oil of the anointment of my head not turn my head away.* The royal oil that was poured onto my head, as it is said (above 23:5): “You anointed my head with oil,” should not turn my head away from the reproof of the righteous man, to go and eat bread with the workers of iniquity.

rashi.heb:
*כי עוד.* 
כי כל עוד ותפלתי בפי הרי היא בשביל רעותיהם של פועלי און שלא אכשל בהם:
rashi.eng: *for as long as.* For as long as my prayer is in my mouth, it is about the evils of the workers of iniquity, that I should not stumble on them.

notes.4564: (tn, Heb): “they are thrown down by the hands of a cliff, their judges.” The syntax of the Hebrew text is difficult and the meaning uncertain. The perfect verbal form is understood as rhetorical; the psalmist describes the anticipated downfall of the wicked as if it had already occurred. “Their judges” could be taken as the subject of the verb, but this makes little, if any, sense. The translation assumes the judges are the agents and that the wicked, mentioned earlier in the psalm, are the subjects of the verb.
notes.4565: (tn): It is unclear how this statement relates to the preceding sentence. Perhaps the judges are the referent of the pronominal subject (“they”) of the verb “will listen,” and “my words” are the referent of the pronominal subject (“they”) of the phrase “are pleasant.” The psalmist may be affirming here his confidence that he will be vindicated when he presents his case before the judges, while the wicked will be punished.

rashi.heb:
*נשמטו בידי סלע שופטיהם.* 
כי דייניהם ומנהיגיהם של אלו נשמטו מדרך הטוב ביד יצר הרע ולב האבן וקשה כסלע:
rashi.eng: *Their judges were led astray by [their hearts of] stone.* For the judges and leaders of these [people] have been led astray from the good way by the evil inclination and the heart of stone, and it is as hard as a rock.

rashi.heb:
*ושמעו אמרי.* 
הנעימים שאני מדבר במצותיו של הקב"ה ואינם שבים מדרכם הרעה ורבותינו בבריית' דסיפרא דרשוהו במשה ואהרן שמתו על ידי הסלע אבל איני יכול ליישב המקרא סופו לראשו, ויש ליישבו ולומר דומין אלו לעקשות לאותן שמתו משה ואהרן ע"י הסלע על ידיהם כי אף אלו שמעו אמרי' נעימים ואינם שבים:
rashi.eng: *although they heard my words.* [my] pleasant [words], which I speak of the commandments, and they do not repent of their evil way. Our Rabbis in the Baraitha of Sifrei (Deut. 3:23) interpreted it concerning Moses and Aaron, but I cannot reconcile the end of the verse with its beginning. I can perhaps reconcile it and say that in stubbornness, these people equal the stubbornness of those through whom Moses and Aaron died through the rock, for these too heard the pleasant words but do not repent.

notes.4566: (tn, Heb): “like splitting and breaking open in the earth.” The meaning of the statement and the point of the comparison are not entirely clear. Perhaps the psalmist is suggesting that he and other godly individuals are as good as dead; their bones are scattered about like dirt that is dug up and tossed aside.

rashi.heb:
*כמו פולח.* 
עצים:
rashi.eng: *As one who chops.* wood.

rashi.heb:
*פולח.* 
לשון בקוע כמו יפלח כליותי (איוב ט"ו):
rashi.eng: *and splits on the ground.* So were our bones scattered to reach the entrance of death because of the evils of the transgressors.

rashi.heb:
*ובוקע בארץ.* 
כן נפזרו עצמינו להגיע לפתח המות בשביל רעותיהם של עוברי עבירה:
rashi.eng: *Chops.* Heb. פלח, an expression of splitting, as (Job 16:13): “He splits my kidneys.”

notes.4568: (tn, Heb): “do not lay bare my life.” Only here is the Piel form of the verb collocated with the term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “life”). In Isa 53:12 the Lord’s servant “lays bare (the Hiphil form of the verb is used) his life to death.”

rashi.heb:
*כי אליך ה' אדני עיני.* 
מוסב למקראות של מעלה שיתה שמרה לפי ואל תט כי עליך עיני וגו':
rashi.eng: *For to You, etc., are my eyes.* This goes back to the above verses (3f.): Place a guard for my mouth… Do not incline… for to You… are my eyes, etc.

rashi.heb:
*אל תער נפשי.* 
אל תשלח נפשי מלפניך כמו ותער כדה אל השקת (בראשית כ״ד:כ׳):
rashi.eng: *do not cast out my soul.* Heb. אל תער. Do not cast me from before You, like (Gen. 24:20): “and emptied (ותער) her pitcher into the watering trough.”

notes.4569: (tn, Heb): “and the traps of the doers of evil.”

notes.4570: (tn): The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive of prayer. Another option is to translate, “the wicked will fall.”
notes.4572: (tn, Heb): “at the same [that] I, until I pass by.” Another option is to take יַחַד (yakhad) with the preceding line, “let the wicked fall together into their own nets.”
notes.4573: (sn): Psalm 142. The psalmist laments his persecuted state and asks the Lord to deliver him from his enemies.
notes.4574: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. The word is derived from a verb meaning “to be prudent; to be wise.” Various options are: “a contemplative song,” “a song imparting moral wisdom,” or “a skillful [i.e., well-written] song.” The term occurs in the superscriptions of Pss 32, 42, 44, 45, 52-55, 74, 78, 88, 89, and 142, as well as in Ps 47:7.
notes.4575: (sn): According to the superscription, David wrote this psalm while in “the cave.” This probably refers to either the incident recorded in 1 Sam 22:1 or to the one recorded in 1 Sam 24:3. See the superscription of Ps 57.

rashi.heb:
*יפלו במכמוריו רשעים.* 
יפול הרשע עצמו במכמוריו שהוא פורש לרגלי:
rashi.eng: *May the wicked fall… into his nets.* May the wicked man himself fall into his nets that he spreads at my feet.

notes.4576: (tn, Heb): “[with] my voice to the Lord I cry out.”
notes.4577: (tn, Heb): “[with] my voice to the Lord I plead for mercy.”

rashi.heb:
*במערה.* 
שכרת בה כנף המעיל אשר לשאול:
rashi.eng: *in the cave.* where he severed the skirt of Saul’s robe.

notes.4578: (tn, Heb): “my trouble before him I declare.”

notes.4581: (tn, Heb): “there is no one who recognizes me.”
notes.4582: (tn, Heb): “ a place of refuge perishes from me.”
notes.4583: (tn, Heb): “there is no one who seeks for the sake of my life.”

rashi.heb:
*ואתה ידעת נתיבתי.* 
כמה מוקשים יש בה:
rashi.eng: *and You know my path.* how many snares are in it.

notes.4584: (tn, Heb): “my portion.” The psalmist compares the Lord to landed property, which was foundational to economic stability in ancient Israel.

rashi.heb:
*ואין לי מכיר.* 
אין בכל משרתי שאול שימחה בידו:
rashi.eng: *no one recognizes me.* Among all of Saul’s servants, there is no one who protests against him.

notes.4588: (tn): The Hebrew idiom גָּמַל עַל (gamal ’al) means “to repay,” here in a positive sense.
notes.4589: (sn): Psalm 143. As in the previous psalm, the psalmist laments his persecuted state and asks the Lord to deliver him from his enemies.

rashi.heb:
*בי יכתירו צדיקים.* 
בשבילי יכתירוך צדיקים ויודו לשמך שאתה סומך את יראיך:
rashi.eng: *because of me the righteous will crown You.* Because of me, the righteous will crown You and give thanks to Your name, for You support those who fear You.

rashi.heb:
*באמונתך.* 
להאמין הבטחה שהבטחתני:
rashi.eng: *with Your faith.* to realize the promise that You promised me.

notes.4590: (tn, Heb): “do not enter into judgment with.”
notes.4591: (tn, Heb): “for no one living is innocent before you.”

notes.4593: (tn, Heb): “an enemy.” The singular is used in a representative sense to describe a typical member of the larger group of enemies (note the plural “enemies” in vv. 9, 12).
notes.4594: (tn, Heb): “he crushes on the ground my life.”
notes.4596: (sn): Dark regions refers to Sheol, which the psalmist views as a dark place located deep in the ground (see Ps 88:6).

rashi.heb:
*כי רדף אויב נפשי.* 
כלומר אם חטאתי לך הרי לקיתי וכנגד כל ישראל נאמר מזמור זה:
rashi.eng: *For an enemy pursued my soul.* That is to say: If I have sinned before You, behold, I have suffered. This psalm was recited as referring to all of Israel in Babylon.

notes.4598: (tn, Heb): “in my midst my heart is shocked.” For a similar use of the Hitpolel of שָׁמֵם (shamem), see Isa 59:16; 63:5.

rashi.heb:
*ישתומם.* 
לשון אוטם ותמהון כמו ואשב שם שבעת ימים משמים בתוכם (יחזקאל ג׳:ט״ו) ותשב תמר ושוממה (שמואל ב י״ג:כ׳):
rashi.eng: *is appalled.* Heb. ישתומם, an expression of daze and astonishment, like (Ezek. 3:15): “and I remained there overwhelmed (משמים) among them seven days.” Also (II Sam. 13:20): “and Tamar sat, overwhelmed (ושוממה).”

rashi.heb:
*זכרתי ימים מקדם.* 
שהפלית לנו נסים רבי':
rashi.eng: *I remember the days of yore.* when You performed for us many wondrous miracles.

notes.4601: (tn): The words “in prayer” are supplied in the translation to clarify that the psalmist is referring to a posture of prayer.
notes.4603: (tc, Heb): “my soul like a faint land for you.” A verb (perhaps “thirsts”) is implied (see Ps 63:1). The translation assumes an emendation of the preposition -כְּ (k�, “like”) to -בְּ (b�, “in,” see Ps 63:1; cf. NEB “athirst for thee in a thirsty land”). If the MT is retained, one might translate, “my soul thirsts for you, as a parched land does for water/rain” (cf. NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*כארץ עיפה.* 
בגולה:
rashi.eng: *like a weary land.* in exile.

notes.4605: (tn, Heb): “do not hide your face from me.” The idiom “hide the face” (1) can mean “ignore” (see Pss 10:11; 13:1; 51:9) or (2) can carry the stronger idea of “reject” (see Pss 30:7; 88:14).
notes.4607: (tn, Heb): “the pit.” The Hebrew noun בּוֹר (bor, “pit; cistern”) is sometimes used of the grave and/or the realm of the dead. See Ps 28:1.

rashi.heb:
*כלתה רוחי.* 
המתאוה ואינו משיג קרוי כליון עינים וכליון רוח:
rashi.eng: *my spirit pines.* If one longs and does not attain, it is called the pining of the eyes and the pining of the spirit.

notes.4608: (tn, Heb): “cause me to hear in the morning your loyal love.” Here “loyal love” probably stands metonymically for an oracle of assurance promising God’s intervention as an expression of his loyal love. The morning is sometimes viewed as the time of divine intervention (see Pss 30:5; 59:16; 90:14).
notes.4609: (sn): The way probably refers here to God’s moral and ethical standards and requirements (see v. 10).
notes.4610: (tn, Heb): “for to you I lift up my life.” The Hebrew expression נָאָשׂ נֶפֶשׁ (na’as nefesh, “to lift up [one’s] life”) means “to desire; to long for” (see Deut 24:15; Prov 19:18; Jer 22:27; 44:14; Hos 4:8, as well as H. W. Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament, 16).

rashi.heb:
*בבקר.* 
בצמוח הגאולה (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *in the morning.* When the redemption sprouts. (I found.)

rashi.heb:
*הודיעני דרך זו.* 
נשאתי נפשי אליך שתקבל שאלתי (סא"א):
rashi.eng: *let me know the way in which I am to go; I lift up my soul.* that You accept my request.

notes.4611: (tn, Heb): “to you I cover,” which makes no sense. The translation assumes an emendation to נַסְתִּי (nastiy, “I flee,” a Qal perfect, first singular form from נוּס, nos). Confusion of kaf (כ) and nun (נ) is attested elsewhere (see P. K. McCarter, Textual Criticism [GBS], 48). The collocation of נוּס (“flee”) with אֶל (’el, “to”) is well-attested.

rashi.heb:
*אליך כסיתי.* 
תלאותי אני מכסה מכל אדם להגידם אליך:
rashi.eng: *to You I have hidden.* My tribulations I conceal from all men to tell them to You.

notes.4613: (tn, Heb): “your good spirit.” God’s “spirit” may refer here to his presence (see the note on the word “presence” in Ps 139:7) or to his personal Spirit (see Ps 51:10).
notes.4614: (tn): The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive. Taking the statement as a prayer fits well with the petitionary tone of vv. 7-10a.
notes.4615: (sn): A level land (where one can walk free of obstacles) here symbolizes divine blessing and protection. See Pss 26:12 and 27:11 for similar imagery.

notes.4616: (tn, Heb): “name,” which here stands metonymically for God’s reputation.
notes.4617: (tn): The imperfect verbal forms in vv. 11-12a are understood as expressing the psalmist’s desire. Note the petitionary tone of vv. 7-10a.
notes.4618: (tn, Heb): “by your justice bring out my life from trouble.”

notes.4620: (tn): The perfect with vav (ו) consecutive carries on the mood of the preceding imperfect.
notes.4621: (tn, Heb): “all the enemies of my life.”
notes.4622: (sn): Psalm 144. The psalmist expresses his confidence in God, asks for a mighty display of divine intervention in an upcoming battle, and anticipates God’s rich blessings on the nation in the aftermath of military victory.

notes.4623: (tn, Heb): “my rocky summit.” The Lord is compared to a rocky summit where one can find protection from enemies. See Ps 18:2.
notes.4624: (tn, Heb): “blessed [be] the Lord, my rocky summit.”
notes.4625: (sn): The one who trains my hands for battle. The psalmist attributes his skill with weapons to divine enablement (see Ps 18:34). Egyptian reliefs picture gods teaching the king how to shoot a bow. See O. Keel, The Symbolism of the Biblical World, 265.

notes.4626: (tn, Heb): “my loyal love,” which is probably an abbreviated form of “the God of my loyal love” (see Ps 59:10, 17).
notes.4628: (tn, Heb): “the one who subdues nations beneath me.”

rashi.heb:
*הרודד עמי תחתי.* 
הרוקע ושוטח את עמי לרבוץ במקומו כמו (איוב י"ב) שוטח לגוים מגדיל אותם, רודד תרגום של רוקע כדמתרגם וירקעו ורדידו, ויש פותרים הרודד עמים תחתי המחליש עמים תחתי אך בספר מדויק מוגה עמי ומסורה עליו ג' סבירין עמים וקורין עמי ועל תחתי יש מסורה עליו תחתיו קרי:
rashi.eng: *Who flattens peoples beneath me.* Who flattens and spreads out my people to rest in its place, as (Job 12:23): He spreads out (שוטח) the nations." He makes them great. רוֹדֵד is the Aramaic translation of רוֹקַע, as the Targum renders (Exod. 39:3): וַיְרַקְעוּ, and they spread out; וְרַדִּידוּ. Others interpret הרודד, Who weakens peoples under me. But in an accurate revised version, [the reading is]: עמי, upon which the Masorah states: In three cases, the meaning is עמים, peoples, but the reading is עמי, and on תחתי, it says: the reading is תחתיו, under Him.

notes.4629: (tn, Heb): “What is mankind?” The singular noun אֱנוֹשׁ (’enosh) is used here in a collective sense and refers to the human race. See Ps 8:5.
notes.4630: (tn, Heb): “and the son of man.” The phrase “son of man” is used here in a collective sense and refers to human beings. For other uses of the phrase in a collective or representative manner, see Num 23:19; Ps 146:3; Isa 51:12.
notes.4631: (tn, Heb): “take account of him.” The two imperfect verbal forms in v. 4 describe God’s characteristic activity.

rashi.heb:
*מה אדם.* 
מה פרס וישמעאל לפניך כי ידעתם להרבות להם גדולה:
rashi.eng: *what is man.* What are Persia [Esau, acc. to mss.] and Ishmael before You that You know them to lavish greatness upon them?

notes.4633: (tn, Heb): “his days [are] like a shadow that passes away,” that is, like a late afternoon shadow made by the descending sun that will soon be swallowed up by complete darkness. See Ps 102:11.

rashi.heb:
*ימיו כצל עובר.* 
שלמה אמר ויעשם כצל (קהלת ו׳ י״ב) ולא פירש אם צל דקל או צל כותל שהם קבועים כבר פי' אביו כצל עובר צלו של עוף הפורח:
rashi.eng: *his days are as a fleeting shadow.* Solomon said (Ecc. 6:12): “that he do them like a shadow,” but he did not explain whether [this refers to] the shadow of a palm or the shadow of a wall, which are permanent. His father already explained, “as a fleeting shadow,” the shadow of a flying bird.

notes.4634: (tn): The Hebrew verb נָטָה (natah) can carry the sense “to [cause to] bend; to [cause to] bow down.” For example, Gen 49:15 pictures Issachar as a donkey that “bends” its shoulder or back under a burden. Here the Lord causes the sky, pictured as a dome or vault, to sink down as he descends in the storm. See Ps 18:9.
notes.4635: (tn, Heb): “so you might come down.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose after the preceding imperative. The same type of construction is utilized in v. 6.
notes.4636: (tn, Heb): “so they might smolder.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose after the preceding imperative.

notes.4637: (sn): Arrows and lightning bolts are associated in other texts (see Pss 18:14; 77:17-18; Zech 9:14), as well as in ancient Near Eastern art (see R. B. Chisholm, “An Exegetical and Theological study of Psalm 18/2 Samuel 22” [Th.D. diss., Dallas Theological Seminary, 1983], 187).

notes.4639: (tn, Heb): “mighty waters.” The waters of the sea symbolize the psalmist’s powerful foreign enemies, as well as the realm of death they represent (see the next line and Ps 18:16-17).
notes.4640: (tn, Heb): “from the hand of the sons of foreignness.”

rashi.heb:
*פצני.* 
הוציאני ולשון הצלה הוא וכן הפוצה את דוד עבדו (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *deliver me.* פצני, take me out. That is an expression of saving, and so is (verse 10): “Who delivers (הפוצה) David His servant.” (I found.)

notes.4641: (tn, Heb): “who [with] their mouth speak falsehood, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.” The reference to the “right hand” is probably a metonymy for an oath. When making an oath, one would raise the hand as a solemn gesture. See Exod 6:8; Num 14:30; Deut 32:40. The figure thus represents the making of false oaths (false promises).

rashi.heb:
*פיהם דבר שוא וגו'.* 
תלה הכתוב שוא בפה ושקר בימין, באו לספר בפה בודים גוזמא על שוא אף לשנות את הידוע, באו לפשוט ימינם לשבועה חדלו משוא שנתפס עליו כגנב אבל בשקר נשבעין שכך גורלם:
rashi.eng: *Whose mouth speaks vanity, etc..* Scripture connects vanity with the mouth and falsehood with the right hand. When they come to tell with their mouth, they invent exaggerations of vanity, even to misrepresent what is known. If they come to stretch forth their right hand to swear, they refrain from vanity, lest they be caught as thieves, but they do swear falsely, for so is their lot.

rashi.heb:
*הנותן תשועה למלכים.* 
מדבר על סלע המחלקות שהיה דוד קרוב ליתפש ביד שאול ובא מלאך אל שאול מהרה ולכה וגו' (שמואל א כ״ג:כ״ז) הציל את שאול מהיות שופך דם נקי ואת דוד מהיות נהרג:
rashi.eng: *Who gives salvation to kings.* This speaks about the Rock of the Divisions, when David was close to being seized by Saul (I Sam. 23:27): “A messenger came to Saul, saying, ‘Make haste and go, etc.’” He saved Saul from shedding innocent blood, and David from being killed.

notes.4644: (tn, Heb): “from the hand of the sons of foreignness.”
notes.4645: (tn, Heb): “who [with] their mouth speak falsehood, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.” See v. 8 where the same expression occurs.

rashi.heb:
*פצני והצילני.* 
כאשר פצית אז כן פצני עתה:
rashi.eng: *Deliver me and rescue me.* As You delivered me then, so shall You deliver me now.

notes.4646: (tn): Some consider אֲשֶׁר (’asher) problematic, but here it probably indicates the anticipated consequence of the preceding request. (For other examples of אֲשֶׁר indicating purpose/result, see BDB 83 s.v. and HALOT 99 s.v.) If the psalmist – who appears to be a Davidic king preparing to fight a battle (see vv. 10-11) – is victorious, the whole nation will be spared invasion and defeat (see v. 14) and can flourish. Some prefer to emend the form to אַשְׁרֵי (“how blessed [are our sons]”). A suffixed noun sometimes follows אַשְׁרֵי (’ashrey; see 1 Kgs 10:8; Prov 20:7), but the presence of a comparative element (see “like plants”) after the suffixed noun makes the proposed reading too awkward syntactically.
notes.4647: (tn, Heb): “grown up in their youth.” The translation assumes that “grown up” modifies “plants” (just as “carved” modifies “corner pillars” in the second half of the verse). Another option is to take “grown up” as a predicate in relation to “our sons,” in which case one might translate, “they will be strapping youths.”
notes.4648: (tn): The Hebrew noun occurs only here and in Zech 9:15, where it refers to the corners of an altar.
notes.4649: (tn, Heb): “carved [in] the pattern of a palace.”

rashi.heb:
*אשר בנינו וגו'.* 
כלומר גם עתה דור זה כשר הוא:
rashi.eng: *For our sons are, etc..* That is to say that now too this generation is righteous.

rashi.heb:
*בנינו כנטיעים.* 
שאין בהם מום כל כך הם מנוקים מעבירה (מצאתי):
rashi.eng: *our sons are like saplings.* which have no blemish, so pure are they from sin. (I found.)

rashi.heb:
*מגדלים בנעוריהם.* 
בשם טוב זה שהם כנטיעים בנערותם גדלים כל ימיהם ואי אפשר לקיים כל שבח זה אלא בדורו של חזקיהו:
rashi.eng: *grown up in their youth.* with this good name, that they are like saplings in their youth, growing all their lives; and this praise cannot be substantiated except in the generation of Hezekiah.

rashi.heb:
*בנותינו.* 
גבוהות קומה נאה כזויות של בית אבנים שזויות אבן מכוונות כנגד חברתה ועולה למעלה עד שהזויות מיושרות:
rashi.eng: *our daughters.* are of tall, beautiful stature like the cornerstones of a stone house, in which the cornerstones are placed exactly one opposite the other, and it ascends upward until the corners are even.

rashi.heb:
*מחטבות תבנית היכל.* 
מהוללות בפי רואיהן ומדמין אותם לתבנית קומת ההיכל, ורבותינו פירשו בנותינו כזויות מתמלאות תאוה כזויות מזבח המלאות דם ואינן נבעלות אלא לבעליהן:
rashi.eng: *praised as the form of the Temple.* Praised by those who see them and compare them to the form of the height of the Temple. Our Rabbis, however, explained: Our daughters are like corners full of desire as the corners of the altar are full of blood, but they are intimate only with their husbands:

notes.4650: (tn): The Hebrew noun occurs only here.
notes.4651: (tn, Heb): “from kind to kind.” Some prefer to emend the text to מָזוֹן עַל מָזוֹן (mazon ’al mazon, “food upon food”).
notes.4653: (tn, Heb): “in outside places.” Here the term refers to pastures and fields (see Job 5:10; Prov 8:26).

rashi.heb:
*מזוינו מלאים.* 
זויות אוצרותינו מלאים טוב:
rashi.eng: *Our corners are full.* The corners of our storehouses are full of goodness.

rashi.heb:
*מפיקים מזן אל זן.* 
מספיקים מזון משנה לשנה:
rashi.eng: *supplying from harvest to harvest.* Supplying food from year to year.

rashi.heb:
*מזן אל זן.* 
משעת אסיף מזון לשנה זו עד זמן אסיף לשנה אחרת, זן גובירניי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *from harvest to harvest.* Heb. מזן אל זן, from the time of the ingathering of this year’s food until the time of the ingathering of next year’s food. זַן is gouvernayl in Old French, food, provisions.

rashi.heb:
*מאליפות מרובבות.* 
לאלפים ולרבבו' עושו' פרי:
rashi.eng: *produce thousands, yea, ten thousands.* They produce offspring of thousands and ten thousands.

notes.4654: (tn, Heb): “weighted down.” This probably refers (1) to the cattle having the produce from the harvest placed on their backs to be transported to the storehouses (see BDB 687 s.v. סָבַל). Other options are (2) to take this as reference to the cattle being pregnant (see HALOT 741 s.v. סבל pu) or (3) to their being well-fed or fattened (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 288).
notes.4655: (tn, Heb): “there [will be] no breach, and there [will be] no going out, and there [will be] no crying out in our broad places.”

rashi.heb:
*אלופינו מסבלים.* 
אלופים גדולים שבנו נסבלים על קטניהם שהקטנים נשמעים לגדולים ומתוך כך אין פרץ בנו:
rashi.eng: *Our princes are borne.* The great princes among us are borne by those smaller than they, for the small ones obey the greater ones, the result being that there is no breach among us.

rashi.heb:
*ואין יוצאת.* 
אין שמועה רעה יוצאת למרחוק:
rashi.eng: *nor rumor going out.* No bad news goes far away.

rashi.heb:
*ואין צוחה.* 
ואין קול מהומות מלחמה:
rashi.eng: *nor is there a cry.* There is no sound of the confusion of war.

notes.4656: (tn, Heb): “[O] the happiness of the people who [it is] such to them.”
notes.4657: (sn): Psalm 145. The psalmist praises God because he is a just and merciful king who cares for his people.

rashi.heb:
*שככה לו.* 
שכל טובה הזאת שלו:
rashi.eng: *Praiseworthy is the people that has this.* That has all this good.

notes.4660: (tn, Heb): “and concerning his greatness there is no searching.”

notes.4661: (tn): The prefixed verbal forms in v. 4 are understood as imperfects, indicating how the psalmist expects his audience to respond to his praise. Another option is to take the forms as jussives, indicating the psalmist’s wish, “may one generation praise…and tell about.”

rashi.heb:
*דור לדור ישבח מעשיך.* 
וגם אני הדר כבוד הודך אשיחה:
rashi.eng: *Generation to generation will praise Your works.* And I, too, shall speak of the majesty of the glory of Your splendor.

notes.4662: (tn, Heb): “the splendor of the glory of your majesty, and the matters of your amazing deeds I will ponder.”

notes.4663: (tn): The prefixed verbal form is understood as an imperfect, indicating how the psalmist expects his audience to respond to his praise. Another option is to take the forms as a jussive, indicating the psalmist’s wish, “may they proclaim.”

rashi.heb:
*ועזוז נוראותיך יאמרו.* 
וגם אני גדולתך אספרנה:
rashi.eng: *And the strength of Your awesome deeds they will tell.* And I, too, shall recite Your greatness.

notes.4664: (tn, Heb): “the fame of the greatness of your goodness.”
notes.4665: (tn): The prefixed verbal forms in v. 7 are understood as imperfects, indicating how the psalmist expects his audience to respond to his praise. Another option is to take the forms as jussives, indicating the psalmist’s wish, “may they talk…and sing.”

rashi.heb:
*זכר רב טובך יביעו.* 
דור לדור:
rashi.eng: *Of the remembrance of Your abundant goodness they will speak.* i.e., one generation to another generation.

notes.4667: (tn, Heb): “and great of loyal love” (see Pss 86:15; 103:8).

notes.4668: (tn, Heb): “and his compassion is over all his works.”

rashi.heb:
*גבורתך ידברו.* 
זה לזה לאמר טוב לנו להודיע לבני האדם גבורותיו וכבוד הדר מלכותו של הקב"ה (מצאתי) נו"ן חסרה מאלפ"א בית"א לפי שראה דוד בה מפלה קשה נפלה ולא תוסיף קום בתולת ישראל (עמוס ו') וחזר וסמכה ברוח הקודש סומך ה' לכל הנופלים:
rashi.eng: *and they will speak of Your might.* to each other, saying, “It is good for us to make known to the children of men His mighty deeds and the glory of the majesty of the kingdom of the Holy One, blessed be He.” (I found.)(The “nun” is missing from the “aleph-beth” because David saw in it a serious downfall [Amos 5:2]: “The virgin of Israel has fallen and shall not continue to rise.” And he returned and supported her with the holy spirit: The Lord supports all those who fall.)

notes.4671: (tc): Psalm 145 is an acrostic psalm, with each successive verse beginning with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet. However, in the traditional Hebrew (Masoretic) text of Psalm 145 there is no verse beginning with the letter nun. One would expect such a verse to appear as the fourteenth verse, between the mem (מ) and samek (ס) verses. Several ancient witnesses, including one medieval Hebrew manuscript, the Qumran scroll from cave 11, the LXX, and the Syriac, supply the missing nun (נ) verse, which reads as follows: “The Lord is reliable in all his words, and faithful in all his deeds.” One might paraphrase this as follows: “The Lord’s words are always reliable; his actions are always faithful.” Scholars are divided as to the originality of this verse. L. C. Allen argues for its inclusion on the basis of structural considerations (Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 294-95), but there is no apparent explanation for why, if original, it would have been accidentally omitted. The psalm may be a partial acrostic, as in Pss 25 and 34 (see M. Dahood, Psalms [AB], 3:335). The glaring omission of the nun line would have invited a later redactor to add such a line.

notes.4673: (tn, Heb): “the eyes of all wait for you.”
notes.4674: (tn, Heb): “and you give to them their food in its season” (see Ps 104:27).

rashi.heb:
*ומשביע לכל חי רצון.* 
כדי פרנסתו הוא משביע את טובו ואת רצונו ואת ברכתו רצון. אפיימנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and satisfy every living thing [with] its desire.* With a sufficiency to sustain him, He satisfies his goodness, his will, and his blessing.

rashi.heb:
*רצון.* 
אפיימנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *desire.* Heb. רצון, apayement in Old French, propitiation.

notes.4677: (tn, Heb): “and [is] loving in all his deeds.”

notes.4679: (tn): In this context “desire” refers to the followers’ desire to be delivered from wicked enemies.
notes.4680: (tn, Heb): “the desire of those who fear him, he does.”

notes.4681: (tn, Heb): “the praise of the Lord my mouth will speak.”
notes.4683: (sn): Psalm 146. The psalmist urges his audience not to trust in men, but in the Lord, the just king of the world who cares for the needy.

rashi.heb:
*תהלת ה' ידבר פי.* 
וגם כל בשר יברך את שם קדשו לעולם ועד:
rashi.eng: *My mouth will speak the praise of the Lord.* and also all flesh will bless His holy name forever and ever.

rashi.heb:
*אזמרה לאלהי בעודי.* 
בעוד אני חי:
rashi.eng: *as long as I exist.* Heb. בעודי.

notes.4684: (tn, Heb): “in a son of man, to whom there is no deliverance.”

notes.4685: (tn, Heb): “his spirit goes out, it returns to his ground; in that day his plans die.” The singular refers to the representative man mentioned in v. 3b.

rashi.heb:
*עשתונותיו.* 
מחשבותיו:
rashi.eng: *his thoughts.* Heb. עשתונותיו his thoughts.

rashi.heb:
*אשרי.* 
מי שאל יעקב בעזרו, שהבטיחו הקדוש ברוך הוא הנה אנכי עמך ושמרתיך והשיבותיך (בראשית כ״ח:ט״ו) ולמה אשריו לפי שהוא עושה שמים וארץ ואת הים וכיון שהכל שלו יש בידו לשמרו בים וביבשה אבל מלך עו"ג אם שומרו ביבשה אינו יכול לשומרו בים:
rashi.eng: *Praiseworthy.* is he in whose help is the God of Jacob, for the Holy One, blessed be He, promised him (Gen. 28:15): “Behold I am with you, and I shall guard You, etc., and I shall return you.” Now why is He praiseworthy? Because He made heaven and Earth and the sea, and since all is His, He has the power to guard him on the sea and on dry land; but a mortal king, although he watches him on dry land, cannot watch him on the sea.

notes.4686: (tn, Heb): “the one who guards faithfulness forever.”

rashi.heb:
*השומר אמת לעולם.* 
לסוף דורות רבים הוא מקיים ושומר אמיתת הבטחתו:
rashi.eng: *Who keeps truth forever.* To the end of many generations, He fulfills and keeps the truth of His promise.

notes.4689: (sn): God is depicted here as a just ruler. In the ancient Near Eastern world a king was responsible for promoting justice, including caring for the weak and vulnerable, epitomized by resident aliens, the fatherless, and widows.
notes.4690: (tn, Heb): “he makes the way of the wicked twisted.” The “way of the wicked” probably refers to their course of life (see Prov 4:19; Jer 12:1). God makes their path tortuous in the sense that he makes them pay the harmful consequences of their actions.

rashi.heb:
*יעודד.* 
לשון כח:
rashi.eng: *strengthens.* Heb. יעודד, an expression of strength.

notes.4691: (tn, Heb): “for a generation and a generation.”
notes.4692: (sn): Psalm 147. The psalmist praises the Lord for he is the sovereign ruler of the world who cares for the needs of his covenant people.

rashi.heb:
*ימלך ה' לעולם.* 
יקיים את מלכותו בשמירת בניו:
rashi.eng: *The Lord will reign forever.* He will perpetuate His kingdom with the redemption of His children.

rashi.heb:
*כי טוב זמרה.* 
כי טוב לזמר לו:
rashi.eng: *For it is good to sing.* For it is good to sing to Him.

notes.4694: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.4697: (tn, Heb): “to his wisdom there is no counting.”

notes.4699: (tn, Heb): “sing to the Lord with thanksgiving.”

rashi.heb:
*לחמה.* 
מאכלה:
rashi.eng: *its food.* Heb. לחמה, lit. its bread.

rashi.heb:
*לבני עורב.* 
פירשו רבותינו שהוא אכזרי על בניו והקב"ה מרחם עליהם ומזמין להם יתושין מתוך צואתם ונכנסין לתוך פיהם:
rashi.eng: *to the young ravens.* Our Sages explained that he [the raven] is cruel to his offspring, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has pity on them and prepares for them gnats from their excrement, which enter their mouths.

notes.4703: (tn, Heb): “he does not desire the strength of the horse, he does not take delight in the legs of the man.” Here “the horse” refers to the war horse used by ancient Near Eastern chariot forces, and “the man” refers to the warrior whose muscular legs epitomize his strength.

rashi.heb:
*לא בגבורת הסוס יחפץ.* 
הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *He does not desire the might of the horse.* [i.e.,] the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*לא בשוקי האיש ירצה.* 
ולא בקלות מרוצת שוקי האיש ירצה:
rashi.eng: *nor does He take pleasure in the legs of man.* nor does He want the swiftness of the running of the legs of man.

rashi.heb:
*חלב חטים.* 
טוב חטים שמנים:
rashi.eng: *the best of the wheat.* Heb. חלב, lit. fat. The best, fat wheat kernels.

notes.4710: (tn, Heb): “the one who sends his word, the earth.” The Hebrew term אֶרֶץ (’erets, “earth”) is an adverbial accusative; one must supply a preposition before it (such as “through” or “to”) in the English translation.

notes.4712: (tn, Heb): “the one who gives snow like wool, frost like ashes he scatters.”

rashi.heb:
*כפור.* 
גליז"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *hoarfrost.* Heb. כפור, jelede in Old French.

notes.4714: (tn, Heb): “Before his cold, who can stand?”

rashi.heb:
*משליך קרחו כפתים.* 
המים מגלידים ונעשין פתיתין פתיתין, ומדרש אגדה כפתים הכל לפי משא הבריות העני לפי חוסר מלבושיו מיקל עליו:
rashi.eng: *He hurls His ice like crumbs.* The water congeals and becomes crumbs. [According to] Midrash Aggadah like crumbs Everything [is] according to the burden of the people: the poor man, according to his lack of clothing, He is lenient with him:

rashi.heb:
*מי יעמוד.* 
שלא יהא צונן בקרתו:
rashi.eng: *who can stand.* that he should not become chilled from His cold?

notes.4715: (tn, Heb): “he sends his word and melts them.”

rashi.heb:
*ישלח דברו וימסם.* 
לאותם פתים:
rashi.eng: *He sends His word and melts them.* those crumbs.

rashi.heb:
*ישב רוחו.* 
רוח מערבי להשבית הקרח ויזלו מים:
rashi.eng: *He blows His wind.* The west wind, to get rid of the ice, and water runs.

notes.4717: (sn): Psalm 148. The psalmist calls upon all creation to praise the Lord, for he is the creator and sovereign king of the world.

rashi.heb:
*כוכבי אור.* 
כוכבי לילה:
rashi.eng: *stars of the night.* Heb. כוכבי אור, stars of the night.

notes.4721: (sn): The “water” mentioned here corresponds to the “waters above” mentioned in Gen 1:7. See also Ps 104:3. For a discussion of the picture envisioned by the psalmist, see L. I. J. Stadelmann, The Hebrew Conception of the World, 47.

notes.4723: (tn, Heb): “and it will not pass away.”

rashi.heb:
*חק נתן.* 
בהם, זה ישמש ביום וזה ישמש בלילה:
rashi.eng: *He issued a decree.* to them, that this one should serve by day and that one should serve by night.

rashi.heb:
*ולא יעבור.* 
אותו חק:
rashi.eng: *which will not change.* That decree.

rashi.heb:
*תנינים.* 
דגים גדולים:
rashi.eng: *sea monsters.* Heb. תנינים, huge fish.

notes.4724: (tn): In Ps 119:83 the noun refers to “smoke,” but here, where the elements of nature are addressed, the clouds, which resemble smoke, are probably in view.

rashi.heb:
*וברד.* 
גלצ"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and hail.* Heb. וברד, gresle or grezle in Old French, hail.

rashi.heb:
*שלג.* 
נייף בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *snow.* Heb. שלג, neyf or nayf in old French, snow.

rashi.heb:
*וקיטור.* 
ענין שואה שקורין ברואינ"ה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and vapor.* וקיטור, an expression of a mist called bruine or broine in Old French, mist, fog.

rashi.heb:
*רוח סערה.* 
העושה את דברו ושליחותו, ואמרו רבותינו שהדברים הללו היו תחלתם גנוזים בשמים ובא דוד והורידן לארץ לפי שהם מיני פורעניות ואין נאה להם להיות גנוזין במגוריו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *a storm wind.* which performs His word and His mission. Our Sages said (Chag. 12b): These things were originally hidden in Heaven, and David came and brought them down to Earth because they are kinds of punishment, and it is not fitting for them to be hidden in the dwellings of the Holy One, blessed be He.

notes.4727: (tn, Heb): “and he lifted up a horn for his people.” The horn of an ox underlies the metaphor (see Deut 33:17; 1 Kgs 22:11; Ps 92:10). The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “exalt/lift up the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 75:10; 89:17, 24; 92:10; Lam 2:17). Another option is to take the “horn” as a symbol for the Davidic king, through whom the Lord gives his people military victory.
notes.4728: (tn): “[there is] praise for all his loyal followers, to the sons of Israel, the people near him.” Here “praise” stands by metonymy for the victory that prompts it.
notes.4729: (sn): Psalm 149. The psalmist calls upon God’s people to praise him because he is just and avenges them.

notes.4730: (tn, Heb): “his praise in the assembly of the godly ones.”

notes.4732: (sn): The Lord is the king here, as the parallelism in the previous line (“their creator”) indicates.

notes.4734: (tn, Heb): “in glory.” Here “glory” probably refers to the “honor” that belongs to the Lord’s people as a result of their deliverance (see v. 4).
notes.4735: (tn): The significance of the reference to “beds” is unclear. Perhaps the point is that they should rejoice at all times, even when falling asleep or awaking.

notes.4736: (tn, Heb): “[May] praises of God [be] in their throat, and a two-edged sword in their hand.”

rashi.heb:
*רוממות אל בגרונם.* 
והם לחרב פיפיות בידם:
rashi.eng: *Lofty praises of God in their throats.* and they will be for them a double-edged sword.

rashi.heb:
*בזקים.* 
שרשראות:
rashi.eng: *with chains.* Heb. בזקים, chains.

notes.4739: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (the enemies of the people of God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.4740: (tn, Heb): “to do against them judgment [that] is written.”
notes.4741: (tn, Heb): “it is honor for all his godly ones.” The judgment of the oppressive kings will bring vindication and honor to God’s people (see vv. 4-5).
notes.4742: (sn): Psalm 150. The Psalter concludes with a resounding call for praise from everything that has breath.

rashi.heb:
*משפט כתוב.* 
ונתתי את נקמתי באדום וגומר (יחזקאל כ״ה:י״ד), ואם תאמר עדיין לא נולד יחזקאל כשאמר דוד זאת נתנבא דוד על קץ הגאולה וכשיבא הקץ כבר כתוב הוא המשפט זה ימים רבים:
rashi.eng: *a written judgment.* (Ezek. 25:14) “And I shall lay My vengeance, etc.” If you ask [challenge] that Ezekiel was not yet born when David said this, [I will answer that] David prophesied about the end of the redemption, and when the end comes, the judgment will have been written for a long time.

rashi.heb:
*במנים ועוגב.* 
מיני כלי שיר הם:
rashi.eng: *with stringed instrument and flute.* Heb. במנים ועגב. They are kinds of musical instruments.

rashi.heb:
*בצלצלי שמע.* 
מצלתים המשמיעים קול שמע 
שם דבר הוא כמו שמע בסגול ומפני האתנחתא הוא נקוד קמץ גדול ולכך טעמו למעלה תחת השי"ן: סליק ספר תהלים:
rashi.eng: *with resounding cymbals.* Heb. בצלצלי שמע, cymbals that let a sound be heard. שָׁמַע is a noun, like שֶׁמַע, with a “segol,” but because of the “ethnactha” [which denotes a pause], it is vowelized with a long “kamatz,” and therefore, its accent is above, under the “shin.”
